# Simplification survey, round 5: a line-by-line read of all production code

**Date**: 2026-08-27 · **Method**: 36 agents, each reading ~8,000 lines completely · **Net**: -1078 LoC · **Findings**: 150 verified, 28 refuted

## 0. Why this round found different things

Rounds 1-4 were **surveys**. They grepped, sampled, and reasoned about structure: round 1 partitioned by directory and gave each agent roughly 10,000 lines to skim, round 2 partitioned by cross-cutting pattern, round 3 by subsystem architecture, round 4 by never-swept surface. Between them they removed about 10,000 lines. None of them **read the code**.

Round 5 partitioned all 295,148 lines of production TypeScript mechanically into 36 cohesive slices of ~8,000 lines, grouped so each agent saw related files together, and instructed every agent to open and read every file in its slice.

That changes the class of finding. A survey sees dead exports and duplicated helpers. Only a reader sees a function whose body diverges from its own doc comment, two conditional branches computing the same value, a guard duplicated at both caller and callee, or copy-pasted handlers that drifted until one grew a check the others never got.

| Kind               | Count   |
| ------------------ | ------- |
| `delete`           | 60      |
| `amend`            | 36      |
| `defect`           | 32      |
| `consolidate`      | 22      |
| **Total verified** | **150** |

**68 of the 150 findings are bugs, not simplifications** (`defect` + `amend`). That is the round's real output. Several carry a positive line count, because CLAUDE.md requires a masking failure to be made loud rather than deleted quietly, and that costs lines.

## 3. Findings in detail

### `triggerEscapeInterrupt` re-derives the exact four-condition guard its one caller has already proved, in the same synchronous frame

- **Slice**: b1 · **Kind**: delete · **Risk**: medium · **Net**: -55 LoC (proposer claimed -45; verifier figure governs)
- **Files**: `packages/cli/src/chat/tui/appInteractionPolicy.ts`, `packages/cli/src/chat/tui/App.tsx`

**Evidence**

`triggerEscapeInterrupt` (appInteractionPolicy.ts:80-97) returns false unless `streamId !== undefined` and `appEscapeInterruptActive({inputDisabled, reverseSearchOpen, runPending: state.canInterruptStream(streamId), slashPaletteOpen})`. Its one production caller is App.tsx:619, inside `handleBareEscape`, and every one of those conditions is already established on the way there: (a) `streamId` is a typed `StreamTabId`, never undefined; (b) `handleBareEscape` returns early at :602-607 unless `bareEscapeActive(streamId)`, which is `appOwnsEscape() && (parentStreamSignal.get().has(streamId) || state.canInterruptStream(streamId))` (:592-599), and `appOwnsEscape()` (:582-590) is `appEscapeInterruptActive` with `runPending: true` — i.e. exactly `!inputDisabled && !slashPaletteOpen && !reverseSearchOpen`; (c) line :619 is only reached when `parentId === undefined` at :608-618, and `parentStream` is a `ReadonlyMap<StreamTabId, StreamTabId>` built at childExecutions.ts:119-133 with `if (parent && …) out.set(...)`, so a stored value is always truthy and `has(id) ⟺ get(id) !== undefined` — meaning the `has` disjunct is false and `canInterruptStream(streamId)` must be the true one. Both sides read the same `escapeInterruptStateRef.current` (App.tsx:237-240, :583, :593, :619) with no await between, so nothing can change in between. `rg 'triggerEscapeInterrupt'` returns one production caller (App.tsx:619) plus AppInteractionPolicy.vitest.ts:314,327. The function's own doc-free guard is not defended by any comment; the comments in this file (:19-25 on the 500ms chord window, :57-60 on Alt platforms) defend the deferral machinery, which this finding leaves untouched. Dedupe: rounds 1-4 contain no appInteractionPolicy/Escape-routing title; `grep -i 'escapeInterrupt\|bareEscape' docs/proposals/2026-08-2*.md` returns nothing.

**Proposal**

Replace App.tsx:619 with a direct `escapeInterruptStateRef.current.onInterruptStream(streamId); return true;` and delete `triggerEscapeInterrupt` (appInteractionPolicy.ts:80-97) plus the two cases at AppInteractionPolicy.vitest.ts:300-335 that only exercise its redundant guard. Keep `EscapeInterruptState` (still the ref's type) and keep `appEscapeInterruptActive`, which `appOwnsEscape` uses.

**What we give up**

If a reviewer can produce a state where `parentStream.has(streamId)` is true but `.get(streamId)` is undefined (would need an explicitly-undefined value, which childExecutions.ts:128 forbids), or shows a second caller of `triggerEscapeInterrupt` arriving without `bareEscapeActive` — then the guard is load-bearing and this should be dropped rather than reworked. Given #7496 and #9009 history on this keyboard path, verify by running the AppEscapeRouting suite rather than by reasoning alone.

**Verifier corrections — these override the evidence and proposal above**

1. WRONG PATH. The finding cites "childExecutions.ts:119-133". The file is at packages/cli/src/chat/tui/state/childExecutions.ts (note the `state/` segment); the computed signal spans :119-132 and the guard is at :128. The line numbers are right, the directory is not.

2. TEST TARGET MISDESCRIBED. It is not "the two cases at 300-335" but one whole `it` block, `src/test-kernel/cli/AppInteractionPolicy.vitest.ts:298-334` ("runs Escape interrupt from the supplied current state"). Deleting it also orphans two imports in that file that the proposal does not mention: `triggerEscapeInterrupt` (line 16) and `type EscapeInterruptState` (line 19) — line 306's `Omit<EscapeInterruptState, 'canInterruptStream'>` is the only use of that type in the suite, so both import lines must go or lint fails.

3. THE EARLY RETURN IS TWO-ARMED, NOT ONE. App.tsx:602-605 is `activeStreamIdSignal.get() !== streamId || !bareEscapeActive(streamId)`. The finding quotes only the `bareEscapeActive` arm. Harmless to the conclusion, but the summary of the caller's guard is incomplete.

4. UNSTATED COVERAGE LOSS — and it defeats the finding's own verification advice. `src/test-kernel/cli/AppEscapeRouting.vitest.ts:215` stubs `canInterruptStream: () => true` and is the file's only occurrence, so that suite can never exercise the not-interruptible branch. The deleted `it` block is therefore the ONLY test in the repo pinning "Escape must not interrupt a stream that cannot be interrupted". After the change that property survives solely inside `bareEscapeActive`'s disjunct (App.tsx:595-597) and is untested. This is acceptable under CLAUDE.md's testing budget, but the PR should say so, and "verify by running the AppEscapeRouting suite" is not the verification the finding thinks it is — that suite passes both before and after precisely because it never varies the condition being removed. (I ran it: 43/43 pass with the change applied.)

5. NET LoC IS UNDERSTATED AND THE SPLIT IS NOT GIVEN. -19 in appInteractionPolicy.ts (:80-98 including the trailing blank); App.tsx nets roughly +2 (-1 for the import at :41, +1 for the two-statement replacement of :619, +2 for the short comment the replacement needs); -40 in the test file (37-line block + blank + 2 imports). Honest total ≈ -55, of which ~-40 is test surface and only ~-17 is production. The claimed -45 is in the right direction but the production win is small.

6. POSITIVE EVIDENCE THE FINDING MISSES (strengthens it). `git log -S triggerEscapeInterrupt` shows the guard became redundant in a specific commit: 72612a7d0d "fix(cli): add hierarchical Escape navigation" (2026-08-02) collapsed three call sites into one. The diff removes calls at three sites — including two that reached `triggerEscapeInterrupt` without any prior `bareEscapeActive` check — and adds the single guarded call now at :619. So the guard is demonstrably a leftover of that refactor, not defence-in-depth authored for this call path. Cite the SHA in the PR body; it answers the "#7496/#9009 history" objection better than the reachability argument alone.

7. THE REPLACEMENT NEEDS A COMMENT. An unconditional `onInterruptStream` on a path with two prior keyboard incidents will read as a dropped guard to any reviewer. One line naming why (`bareEscapeActive` already proved `canInterruptStream` for a parentless stream, since the `has` disjunct is false once `.get()` returned undefined) is not optional here.

<details><summary>Verifier reasoning</summary>

The chain is airtight and I re-derived every step from the files rather than the finding's paraphrase. `handleBareEscape` gates on `bareEscapeActive`, which is `appOwnsEscape() && (parentStream.has(id) || canInterruptStream(id))`; `appOwnsEscape()` is `appEscapeInterruptActive` with `runPending: true`, i.e. exactly the three non-runPending conditions `triggerEscapeInterrupt` re-tests. Line 619 is reached only after `parentStream.get(id)` returned undefined, and the computed map at childExecutions.ts:119-132 can never hold an undefined value (`if (parent && ...) out.set(...)`), so `has` is false there and `canInterruptStream(id)` must have been the true disjunct — the fourth condition. `streamId` is a non-optional `StreamTabId` parameter, killing the first. Every read goes through the same `escapeInterruptStateRef.current` with no await, and both `parentStreamSignal.get()` reads are in one synchronous frame, so no state can shift between the proof and the re-check. The give-up condition the finding names cannot be met: no explicit-undefined value can enter that map, and `rg` confirms one production caller. Git history seals it — the guard predates the caller-side gate and was left behind by 72612a7d0d. I also applied the change and ran AppEscapeRouting (43/43 pass), then restored the file. The win is modest and mostly test lines, and the change silently drops the repo's only pin on the not-interruptible case, so it earns medium risk and needs a comment plus an honest note in the PR body — but it is a genuine, correctly-read redundancy, not churn.

</details>

### `/key` prints its confirmation twice, the second copy with the raw provider id — `applyCliProviderApiKey`'s return value is a leftover from the deleted relay reconciliation

- **Slice**: b1 · **Kind**: defect · **Risk**: low · **Net**: -8 LoC (proposer claimed -12; verifier figure governs)
- **Files**: `packages/cli/src/chat/tui/commands/handlers/modelAccessCommands.ts`, `packages/cli/src/chat/tui/commands/registerBuiltins.tsx`, `packages/cli/src/chat/tui/forms/ProviderApiKeyForm.tsx`

**Evidence**

`ProviderApiKeyForm` treats its `onSave` resolution value as an EXTRA notice: ProviderApiKeyForm.tsx:123-133 does `props.onSave(provider,key).then((modelNotice) => props.onDone(provider, modelNotice || undefined))`, and the `/key` adapter at registerBuiltins.tsx:382-391 renders `[`Saved the ${providerDisplayName(provider)} API key.`, ...(modelNotice ? [modelNotice] : [])].join('\n')`. The wired save handler is `applyCliProviderApiKey` (registerBuiltins.tsx:289 default; runChatTui.tsx:482 in production), whose body at modelAccessCommands.ts:29 is `const message = `Saved the ${provider} API key.`` and whose line 30 is `if (provider !== 'kimiCode') return message;`. So every `/key` save renders two lines, e.g. `Saved the OpenAI API key.` followed by `Saved the openai API key.` (raw `ApiProvider` id, not `providerDisplayName`), and for Kimi `Saved the Kimi Code API key.` + `Saved the kimiCode API key · Tip: …`. `git log -L 22,42` on modelAccessCommands.ts shows the drift: commit 2d82c8138e (relay-plane removal) replaced the old `message = await completeModelAccessSelection(access, context)` — a genuine model-access reconciliation notice — with the literal save confirmation, which the adapter had already been printing since 1de5b233e6 (#8710). The leftover `.filter(Boolean)` at modelAccessCommands.ts:40 is from the same era: both array members are now non-empty literals. Consumer check: `rg 'applyCliProviderApiKey|onApiKeySave|ProviderApiKeyForm'` over packages/*/src + src gives exactly two `onSave` producers — this adapter, and CliConfigForm.tsx:230-234 which returns `void` (so `/config → API keys` shows no duplicate and is the correct-looking path). The only test, SlashRegistry.vitest.ts:428-430, injects an `onApiKeySave` that returns `undefined`, which is why the duplication was never pinned. Dedupe: no round-1/2/3/4 title mentions applyCliProviderApiKey, ProviderApiKeyForm, or `/key`; `grep -i 'apikey\|provider api'` over the four survey docs in docs/proposals/ returns nothing.

**Proposal**

Make `applyCliProviderApiKey` return only the notice the caller does not already own: `undefined` for every provider except `kimiCode`, and the bare Kimi Code tip (no `Saved the …` prefix, no `.filter(Boolean)`) for `kimiCode`. Leave the `Saved the ${label} API key.` line to the single owner that formats it with `providerDisplayName` (registerBuiltins.tsx:384). The `refreshSubscriptionPreferenceViews()` side effect stays.

**What we give up**

If a reader can show a third `ProviderApiKeyForm.onSave` producer that relies on the returned string being a complete standalone message (there is none today), or if the duplicated line is deliberate redundancy recorded somewhere — I found no comment or proposal defending it.

**Verifier corrections — these override the evidence and proposal above**

1. NET LoC OVERSTATED: claimed -12, measured -8. I applied the exact proposed body (`if (provider !== 'kimiCode') return undefined;` + the three-line comment + a single bare-tip `return`), ran it through the repo's prettier, and the file goes 101 → 93 lines. The `collapseWhitespace` import at modelAccessCommands.ts:11 must stay — line 56 (`output.appendOutcome(collapseWhitespace(access.message))`) still uses it — so there is no import line to recover.
2. Line-number slips (all minor, none changes the mechanism): `.filter(Boolean)` is modelAccessCommands.ts:39, not :40 (:40 is `.join(' · ')`). The registerBuiltins adapter body is 377-394 with `onSave` at :381 and the join block at :383-389, not "382-391". CliConfigForm's void-returning `onSave` is :229-233, not "230-234". The form's onSubmit block is ProviderApiKeyForm.tsx:123-134, not "123-133".
3. EVIDENCE THE FINDING MISSED, in its favour: a dated ruling already specifies the intended output. docs/proposals/2026-07-19-cli-slash-output-ephemerality.md:122 pins `/key` to "One line `Saved the X API key`". The finding states "I found no comment or proposal defending it" — correct, but it also failed to find the proposal that condemns the current behavior. Cite it in the PR; it turns this from a taste call into a regression against a written spec.
4. Type note the proposal should state: `ProviderApiKeyFormProps.onSave` is typed `Promise<string | void>` (ProviderApiKeyForm.tsx:71-74) and `ApiKeySaveHandler` (registerBuiltins.tsx:89) is the injectable seam; returning `undefined` for non-Kimi providers needs no signature change and leaves the existing test green.
5. Wording nit in the claimed Kimi output: HEAD renders `Saved the Kimi Code API key.` then a newline then `Saved the kimiCode API key · Tip: …` — the finding writes the two joined with `+`, which reads as one line; they are newline-separated transcript lines.

<details><summary>Verifier reasoning</summary>

Verified independently by reading modelAccessCommands.ts, ProviderApiKeyForm.tsx, registerBuiltins.tsx, CliConfigForm.tsx, runChatTui.tsx, SlashRegistry.vitest.ts, and providers.ts at HEAD, plus `git log -L` provenance. The double-print is real and user-visible on every `/key` save: one line formatted with the display name by the adapter, one with the raw ApiProvider id by the handler. It is a genuine leftover from 2d82c8138e, where a substantive model-access reconciliation notice was swapped for a literal that the adapter had already been printing since 1de5b233e6. It also contradicts an explicit dated ruling on `/key` output. The fix is contained, has no external consumer, and is judged as a defect, so the smaller-than-claimed LoC win is not disqualifying.

</details>

### `AppProps.canInterruptActiveRun` exists only as a `??` fallback for `canStopActiveRun`, and it is a deliberately different predicate

- **Slice**: b1 · **Kind**: delete · **Risk**: low · **Net**: -5 LoC (proposer claimed -7; verifier figure governs)
- **Files**: `packages/cli/src/chat/tui/App.tsx`, `packages/cli/src/chat/tui/runChatTui.tsx`

**Evidence**

App.tsx declares both props — `canInterruptActiveRun: () => boolean` (required, :143) and `canStopActiveRun?: () => boolean` (optional, :146) — and the ONLY read of the former in the whole component is the fallback at :193-194 `const canStopActiveRun = props.canStopActiveRun ?? props.canInterruptActiveRun;`, whose result is passed to `triggerAppCtrlC` at :721. `rg 'canInterruptActiveRun'` over packages/*/src + src returns exactly five production hits: App.tsx:143 and :194, and runChatTui.tsx:371-372 (definition), :382 (feeds `chatTuiIsResumableIdleOnExit`) and :505 (folded into `canInterruptStream` for the root stream). The sole production mount, runChatTui.tsx:495-510, passes BOTH `canInterruptActiveRun` (:503) and `canStopActiveRun` (:508), so the fallback never fires. The two predicates are not aliases and the codebase says so: sessionRunState.ts:214-224 `chatTuiIsResumableIdleOnExit` is defined as `canInterruptActiveRun && !canStopActiveRun && hasActiveToolUseFlow`, i.e. the whole point of the pair is the case where they disagree (a tool-use session parked at WAITING). So the fallback does not degrade gracefully — it would silently substitute the predicate that is true precisely when Ctrl-C must NOT stop the run. Only a test relies on the fallback: AppEscapeRouting.vitest.ts:214 passes `canInterruptActiveRun: () => true` and no `canStopActiveRun`. Dedupe: round-1 refuted "Collapse two alias-only MainView event pairs and two always-supplied optional callbacks" — that is the extension MainView, a different file and a different pair; nothing in the four survey docs mentions App.tsx's Ctrl-C props (`grep -i 'canInterruptActiveRun\|canStopActiveRun'` over docs/proposals returns nothing).

**Proposal**

Delete `AppProps.canInterruptActiveRun` (App.tsx:142-143), make `canStopActiveRun` required (App.tsx:146), drop the `??` at :193-194 and read `props.canStopActiveRun` directly, and remove the `canInterruptActiveRun={canInterruptActiveRun}` JSX prop at runChatTui.tsx:503 (the local function stays — it still feeds :382 and :505). Update AppEscapeRouting.vitest.ts:214 to supply `canStopActiveRun`.

**What we give up**

If a second `<App>` mount appears that legitimately has only the interrupt predicate — none exists today — or if the fallback is shown to be load-bearing for a harness the repo ships.

**Verifier corrections — these override the evidence and proposal above**

1. MISSED MOUNT (does not kill it, but the patch is incomplete as written): there IS a second `<App>` mount — packages/cli/scripts/tui-harness.tsx:2436-2452, the source of dist/bin/tui-harness.js. It supplies BOTH props (:2443 `canInterruptActiveRun={() => canInterrupt}`, :2445 `canStopActiveRun={() => canInterrupt}`), so the fallback still never fires and the give-up condition is not met — but the proposal must ALSO delete tui-harness.tsx:2443, or the scripts typecheck fails on an unknown JSX prop. The finding's "exactly five production hits" and "sole production mount" claims were scoped to `packages/*/src` + `src` and missed `packages/cli/scripts`.
2. The doc comment at App.tsx:142 ("Whether Ctrl-C may stop the current root run.") actually describes `canStopActiveRun`, which has no comment today; it should MOVE onto :146 rather than be deleted with the prop. So App.tsx nets about -3 (prop line, plus collapsing the two-line `??` into a direct read at :721), not -4.
3. Provenance the finding did not cite, and it strengthens the case: `canStopActiveRun` was added as an optional prop in 4cab4beac7 ("fix: align CLI Ctrl-C footer action", 2026-05-30) alongside `onCtrlC`, and that same commit updated the harness to pass it. The `??` was migration slack both call sites outgrew in the commit that created it.
4. Understated (context, not required): both mounts also pass `onCtrlC`, and triggerAppCtrlC (appInteractionPolicy.ts:126-137) checks `state.onCtrlC` BEFORE `state.canStopActiveRun()`. So App's `canStopActiveRun` branch is reached only by AppEscapeRouting.vitest.ts today — the honest framing is "a test-only fallback chain", the exact #10871 category. A deeper cut (dropping both props and letting the harness/test supply `onCtrlC`) is available but is a behavior decision beyond this finding; do not widen scope silently.
5. AppEscapeRouting.vitest.ts never sends Ctrl-C (no `ctrl`/`\x03` in the file), so renaming its :214 key to `canStopActiveRun: () => true` is behavior-neutral.
6. Net LoC is about -5, not -7.

<details><summary>Verifier reasoning</summary>

A required prop whose sole purpose is to back-fill an optional prop that every caller already supplies is dead surface by the #10871 precedent, and here it is worse than dead: the two predicates are deliberately non-equivalent (sessionRunState.ts:216-228 is built on their disagreement), so the fallback encodes a latent inversion — it would authorize Ctrl-C to stop precisely the WAITING tool-use session whose flow record must be preserved. Deletion removes an element, removes a trap, and touches three files with no consumer risk. It is a small win (~-5 LoC) and lands close to the "too thin" bar, but unlike the round-1 item that was refused at ~-5, this is a single bounded deletion rather than a batch of unrelated micro-items, and it retires a correctness hazard rather than relocating one.

</details>

### `ConfigFormProps.resetValue` is optional for a props type with exactly one producer, and its fallback writes `''` into settings that reject it

- **Slice**: b1 · **Kind**: delete · **Risk**: low · **Net**: -4 LoC (proposer claimed -6; verifier figure governs)
- **Files**: `packages/cli/src/chat/tui/forms/ConfigForm.tsx`, `packages/cli/src/chat/tui/forms/CliConfigForm.tsx`

**Evidence**

ConfigForm.tsx:158-159 declares `resetValue?: (entry) => void | Promise<void>` and `resetEntry` (:288-294) branches on it: `if (!props.resetValue) { commit(entry, ''); return; }`. `rg '<ConfigForm|ConfigFormProps'` over packages/*/src + src shows exactly one producer of `ConfigFormProps` anywhere — `createCliConfigFormProps` (CliConfigForm.tsx:145-263), consumed at CliConfigForm.tsx:306-318 — and it always supplies `resetValue: (entry) => applyUpdate(entry, null)` (CliConfigForm.tsx:200). Both CliConfigForm mounts (registerBuiltins.tsx:703 and packages/cli/src/config/runConfigTui.tsx:12) go through it, and the test file never constructs `ConfigFormProps` directly — src/test-kernel/cli/ConfigForm.vitest.ts:198 merely mirrors the field in a local read-back type and calls `props.resetValue?.(…)` at :779 and :793 on props produced by `createCliConfigFormProps`. So the fallback is unreachable; worse, if it ever fired it would write `''` for a `number` setting reached via `setMode({kind:'text', isNumber:true})` (ConfigForm.tsx:378-381 routes Ctrl-R there), which `applyStateSettingUpdate` would reject — the opposite of the reset the key press asks for. This is distinct from round-1's shipped `openForm` item: that deleted `ConfigFormProps.openForm` and deliberately KEPT the "Configuration form unavailable." frame reachable (docs/proposals/2026-08-25-simplification-survey-49-candidates.md:147-188); it says nothing about `resetValue`, and `grep -n 'resetValue' docs/proposals/2026-08-25-*.md docs/proposals/2026-08-26-*.md` returns nothing.

**Proposal**

Make `resetValue` required in `ConfigFormProps` (ConfigForm.tsx:159), delete the `if (!props.resetValue) { commit(entry, ''); return; }` arm and the `?.` at ConfigForm.tsx:293, leaving `resetEntry` as the single `runWrite(entry, settingDefault(entry), () => props.resetValue(entry))`.

**What we give up**

If a second `ConfigForm` producer is planned or lands that genuinely cannot delete a key (none exists in-tree), keeping the optional field is cheaper than re-adding it — but the `commit(entry, '')` arm should still be replaced by a loud failure rather than a wrong-typed write.

**Verifier corrections — these override the evidence and proposal above**

1. netLoc is wrong: -6 is overstated; the honest figure is -4. The only lines that disappear are ConfigForm.tsx:289-292 (`if (!props.resetValue) {` / `commit(entry, '');` / `return;` / `}`). Dropping the `?` at :159 and the `?.` at :293 are same-line edits worth 0 lines, and the rewritten call `runWrite(entry, settingDefault(entry), () => props.resetValue(entry));` is 74 columns at its indentation, so prettier does not reflow it. No test edit is needed (see 4).
2. Minor line-citation slip: the finding writes "a `number` setting reached via `setMode({kind:'text', isNumber:true})` (ConfigForm.tsx:378-381 routes Ctrl-R there)". :378-381 is the `onReset` wiring; the `isNumber: true` setMode is at ConfigForm.tsx:473, and the Ctrl-R keypress is captured inside `ConfigTextEditor` at ConfigForm.tsx:207. Mechanism right, two line refs conflated.
3. "ConfigForm.tsx:158-159 declares" — :158 is the doc comment `/** Reset a setting to its default (delete the key). */`; the declaration is :159 alone.
4. Unstated but relevant to the diff: `src/test-kernel/cli/ConfigForm.vitest.ts:198` is a field on the test's own local `RenderedConfigFormProps`, not on `ConfigFormProps`. Making the real field required does not force that local type to change, and `props.resetValue?.(…)` at :779/:793 keeps typechecking against the local optional type — the proposal should say the test is untouched rather than leaving it ambiguous.
5. Supporting evidence the finding omits: `git log -S resetValue -- packages/cli/src/chat/tui/forms/` returns two commits, and the one that introduced the field, 17a3130645 ("Wire resetValue through the adapter"), wired the sole producer in the same change — the optional-plus-`''`-fallback was born dead, exactly like the round-1 `openForm` case.
6. The stronger justification is the convention conflict, not just deadness: CliConfigForm.tsx:161-162 documents `null` as the shared reset convention, so the `''` arm is a second, contradictory reset encoding — a dual system, which is why a required field beats leaving a loud-throw stub.

<details><summary>Verifier reasoning</summary>

Re-read every cited site at HEAD. The census reproduces exactly: one production producer of `ConfigFormProps`, one mount, always supplying `resetValue`, and no test constructs the props type directly or renders `ConfigForm` itself. The guard at ConfigForm.tsx:289-292 is unreachable, and the comment above it defends a different behavior (clear-to-reset), so criterion 3 does not fire. It is distinct from the shipped round-1 `openForm` item, which is already gone from HEAD and whose proposal scopes to `openForm` alone. Nothing in the surveys, the index, AGENTS.md, or the review checklist rules on it. Cost is a genuine small deletion with no test or ratchet churn; only the claimed LoC is inflated by two lines. It survives as a small, low-risk delete that also removes a second reset encoding contradicting the documented `null` convention.

</details>

### A queued follow-up is silently discarded when the root run ends before it resolves a stream id — the exact drop the loop's own PRD comment forbids

- **Slice**: b1 · **Kind**: amend · **Risk**: low · **Net**: 9 LoC (proposer claimed 10; verifier figure governs)
- **Files**: `packages/cli/src/chat/tui/chatSubmitDriver.ts`

**Evidence**

chatSubmitDriver.ts:278-281 states the contract: "PRD success criterion: follow-ups must not be silently dropped when the user submits before `onStreamResolved` populates `session.streamId`." The poll loop at :295-302 exits on `session.stopRequested || session.runCompleted` as well as on a resolved id, and :303 is `if (!followUpTarget || session.stopRequested) return;` — a bare return. The `finally` at :338-342 restores only the reserved skill activations; it does not call `requestDraftRestore(line)` and appends nothing to the transcript. Contrast the sibling failure arm at :320-336, which for `result.status === 'failed'` deliberately does `requestDraftRestore(line)` first with the comment "The draft is the user's until admitted: hand it back before any notice, so a refused send never costs a retype", then `setTransientNotice(...)`. Reachable path: user submits msg1 → `startSession` (:162-221) claims the run slot synchronously via `session.markRunPending(pendingStart)` at :218 and only then awaits `selectCliRunnableModel` / `setCliHelperModel` (:177-185); during that window msg2 fails `chatTuiCanStartRootRun(session)` at :267 (runPromise set, runCompleted false — sessionRunState.ts:163-172) and lands in the queue; if msg1's startup throws (no runnable model, auth failure) the catch at :207-216 calls `session.markRunCompleted()` without ever setting `session.streamId`, so msg2's loop exits with `followUpTarget === undefined` and the typed message is gone — not in the transcript, not in the input, no notice. `session.stopRequested` (Ctrl-C between submit and stream resolution) is the same silent arm; the interrupted-conversation recovery in chatSessionController (`admitInterruptedFollowUp`, chatSessionController.ts:828-883) only covers messages typed AFTER the interrupt, and `followUpQueue.clear()` at chatSubmitDriver.ts:167 / chatSessionController.ts:550 discards this task on the next start/resume anyway. Dedupe: no round-1/2/3/4 title touches chatSubmitDriver or the follow-up poll loop; `grep -i 'followUpQueue\|chatSubmitDriver\|silently dropped'` over the four survey docs returns nothing. This is a checklist §15 masking site (a quiet `return` where the neighbouring arm is loud), so per the brief it is a fix-loudly item, not a delete.

**Proposal**

Give the `!followUpTarget` exit the same treatment the `failed` arm already has: hand the draft back with `requestDraftRestore(line)` and surface one `setTransientNotice` explaining that the conversation ended before the message could be queued. Keep `session.stopRequested` as its own arm if the product wants a Ctrl-C to stay quiet, but decide that explicitly rather than by falling through the same bare return.

**What we give up**

If a reviewer shows that a run can never reach `runCompleted` with `streamId` unset while a queued task is waiting (I traced `startSession`'s catch at :207-216 as the concrete producer), or if the product deliberately treats a message typed during a failed start as discardable — in which case the fix is to make that decision visible rather than to leave the bare return.

**Verifier corrections — these override the evidence and proposal above**

1. The producer set is understated, and the one the claim leads with is the narrower of the two. Besides `startSession`'s catch (chatSubmitDriver.ts:207-216), the wider producer is `startRootRun` (chatSessionController.ts:425-486): its promise chain is `Promise.resolve().then(() => AgentConfigSchema.parse(config)).then(... runAgent ...).catch(reportRunFailure).finally(finalize)`, and `finalize` (chatSessionController.ts:409-417) calls `session.markRunCompleted()`. Any rejection before the `onStreamResolved` callback at :445-467 assigns `session.streamId` — Zod config parse failure, launch/registration failure, auth or provider failure inside `runAgent` — completes the run with `streamId` unset. That window (launch to stream resolution, on every message) is much longer and more commonly hit than the `selectCliRunnableModel`/`setCliHelperModel` window the claim describes, so the defect is not confined to the "user submits msg2 during msg1's model resolution" race.

2. "`startSession` ... claims the run slot synchronously via `session.markRunPending(pendingStart)` at :218 and only then awaits `selectCliRunnableModel` / `setCliHelperModel` (:177-185)" compresses the mechanism. The awaits are inside the `Promise.resolve().then(...)` body created at :172; that body is a microtask, so it cannot begin until after :218 runs. The ordering conclusion is right, and the code says so at :170-171 ("Queue the async startup body after the reservation below so a second submit cannot pass chatTuiCanStartRootRun during model/auth resolution"), but the cited lines do not execute in the order implied.

3. Line cite `sessionRunState.ts:163-172` is off. `chatTuiRunPending` is at :170-172 (doc comment :163-169) and `chatTuiCanStartRootRun` — the predicate actually called at chatSubmitDriver.ts:267 — is at :174-178. The substance (runPromise set, runCompleted false ⇒ cannot start) is correct.

4. The `finally` restores skill activations only when `!delivered` (:339); the claim reads as if it always runs them. Immaterial to the defect, since `delivered` is false on this path.

5. Minor: the sibling arm is the `else` of `if (result.status !== 'failed')` at :309, spanning :320-337 (comment :321-322, restore :323); "at :320-336" clips the closing brace. And at HEAD the notice text is `${describeFollowUpFailure(result.reason)} The message has been restored to the input.` — the `no_session | dropped` wording and the "Pasted images were not re-attached" caveat quoted in the D5 proposal were replaced by 95e1555035 ("three submission outcomes with four worded reasons"), so a fix should follow the current `describeFollowUpFailure` phrasing, not the proposal's.

6. Implementation note the claim omits: `requestDraftRestore` is safe to reuse here. `InputBar.tsx:197-219` appends the restored text below anything typed since the send ("anything typed since the send is kept and the restored text is appended below it") and revives `[Image #N]` chips from `lastSubmittedImagesRef`, which holds the last submitted batch — the dropped message. So the fix does not clobber, and images survive.

7. Risk is low, not medium: the change is a guarded branch inside one function, touching two in-process TUI signals, with no persisted data, no wire contract, no ratchet, and no test pinning the current silence (`grep -rn draftRestoreRequest src/test-kernel` returns nothing).

<details><summary>Verifier reasoning</summary>

The claim is a defect, and the defect is real and verified end to end. The loop's own comment states the invariant ("follow-ups must not be silently dropped when the user submits before onStreamResolved populates session.streamId"), and the exit at :303 violates it: it is a bare `return` in a function whose neighbouring failure arm, eleven lines below, deliberately hands the draft back and posts a notice with the comment "The draft is the user's until admitted: hand it back before any notice, so a refused send never costs a retype."

I confirmed reachability rather than taking it on trust. `markRunCompleted` (sessionRunState.ts:85) is reachable with `streamId` still undefined from two places — chatSubmitDriver.ts:215 and, more importantly, chatSessionController.ts:415 via `finalize` on the `startRootRun` chain, which catches every launch-time rejection before `onStreamResolved` (chatSessionController.ts:445-467) ever assigns the id. `markRunPending` (:72-79) explicitly nulls `_streamId`, and nothing else writes it on that path. A follow-up queued during the launch window therefore exits its poll loop with no target and returns silently. The text is gone: `InputBar` clears on submit and only `requestDraftRestore` puts it back (two references repo-wide, the definition and the one call in the failed arm), nothing appends it to the transcript, and `followUpQueue.clear()` (chatSubmitDriver.ts:167, chatSessionController.ts:550) discards the task on the next start or resume. Losing typed user input with no trace and no notice is squarely the §15 silent-degradation pattern CLAUDE.md calls a defect.

The strongest available refutation was a dated ruling, and I chased it: docs/proposals/2026-08-23-single-owner-sessions.md §D5 names this file and these line numbers. But §D5 is titled "Never clear a draft without an ack" and mandates the restore; `git show a4986a8f05` proves the shipped CLI half only covered `submitFollowUp`'s refusal outcomes, leaving the pre-`submitFollowUp` exit untouched and undiscussed. The ruling supports the finding. Dedupe is clean against the 295-title index and all four survey docs. No external consumer, no ratchet, no settled surface.

Net LoC: the honest fix is a guarded restore plus one notice inside the existing exit — roughly +9 lines, and a defect fix is judged on the defect, not on profit. The `stopRequested` half deserves the explicit decision the proposal asks for: a Ctrl-C between submit and stream resolution destroys the same typed text, and staying quiet there should be a choice recorded in a comment rather than a side effect of sharing one `return` with the launch-failure case.

</details>

### The `/login` and `/logout` pickers never offer Grok, while the same commands' usage text, `/api`, and `texra auth grok login` all do — and "All accounts" still says "both"

- **Slice**: b1 · **Kind**: amend · **Risk**: low · **Net**: 21 LoC (proposer claimed 14; verifier figure governs)
- **Files**: `packages/cli/src/chat/tui/forms/LoginForm.tsx`, `packages/cli/src/chat/tui/forms/LogoutForm.tsx`, `packages/cli/src/chat/tui/commands/handlers/loginCommands.ts`

**Evidence**

Grok is a fully live CLI surface: loginCommands.ts:50 advertises `/login grok [--no-browser] [--device]`, :52 advertises `/logout chatgpt | grok | texra | all`, :83 `SUBSCRIPTION_AUTH_COPY = { chatgpt: CHATGPT_AUTH, grok: GROK_AUTH }`, :173 routes `grok` through `loginToSubscription`, :227-229 signs it out; `CliLogoutTarget` is `'chatgpt' | 'grok' | 'texra' | 'all'` (packages/cli/src/runtime/loginOptions.ts:42) with `GROK_LOGIN_TARGETS = {grok, xai, supergrok}` at :45; `/api` lists it (registerBuiltins.tsx:568 and modelAccessRoute.ts:271-274); and `texra auth grok login` is a top-level command (packages/cli/src/commands/grokAuth.ts:3-4, auth.ts:302, root.ts:117). But `LoginFormValue` is typed `'texra' | 'chatgpt' | 'texra --device' | 'chatgpt --device'` (LoginForm.tsx:12-13) and `LOGIN_FORM_ITEMS` (:21-42) has four rows, none of them Grok — so the picker that `/login` opens on a bare invocation (registerBuiltins.tsx:601-609, `formComponent: LoginFormAdapter`) cannot reach a working path its own usage string names. `LOGOUT_FORM_ITEMS` (LogoutForm.tsx:16-32) likewise omits Grok, and its `all` row's description at :30 reads "Sign out of both accounts" while `logoutFromChat('all')` signs out three (loginCommands.ts:193, :223, :227). `git log -L 21,42` on LoginForm.tsx shows the four rows have been edited three times since #8290 for copy reasons only; Grok was never added, and no comment or proposal gates it. Dedupe: round-4B shipped a structurally similar item ("Add the missing commandPalette gate for texra.auth.grok.signIn") — that is the VS Code extension's package.json palette row, a different host and a different file; `grep -i 'LoginForm\|LogoutForm\|LOGIN_FORM_ITEMS'` over the four survey docs returns nothing.

**Proposal**

Add the two Grok rows (`grok`, `grok --device`) to `LOGIN_FORM_ITEMS` and widen `LoginFormValue`, using the existing `GROK_AUTH.subscriptionLabel` / `subscriptionDescription` / `deviceCodeLabel` copy the handler already imports; add the `grok` row to `LOGOUT_FORM_ITEMS` with `GROK_AUTH.label` / `logoutDescription`; and fix the `all` description from "both accounts" to "every signed-in account". No handler change is needed — `loginFromChat` and `logoutFromChat` already accept both values.

**What we give up**

If a maintainer says Grok sign-in is deliberately kept out of the in-chat pickers (e.g. staged rollout) — then the fix shrinks to the "both accounts" copy line alone, which is wrong either way.

**Verifier corrections — these override the evidence and proposal above**

1. The proposal's copy-reuse plan is wrong. GROK_AUTH (src/shared/copy/accountAuth.ts:40-53) has only label, subscriptionLabel, signInLabel, signOutLabel, preferLabel, startingDevice, startingNoBrowser, startingBrowser, signedInEnabled, signedInOverrideDisabled. It has NO `subscriptionDescription`, NO `deviceCodeLabel`, and NO `logoutDescription` — all three exist only on CHATGPT_AUTH (:21-37). The claim that this is "existing copy the handler already imports" is false: loginCommands.ts imports GROK_AUTH but uses only the three starting* strings, .label, and the two signedIn* functions. Three new copy fields must be authored in accountAuth.ts, which is where the real (small) design work is — and accountAuth.ts's own header comment demands the copy live there rather than being paraphrased in the form.
2. The change is not test-free. src/test-kernel/cli/SlashRegistry.vitest.ts:216-223 ("keeps ChatGPT subscription first in the login picker") asserts LOGIN_FORM_ITEMS.map(v) deep-equals the exact four-value array and must be updated. It is an ordering invariant, not a Grok exclusion (git log -S shows it only moved in the #9738 rename), and the fix preserves ChatGPT-first — but the finding's "no comment or proposal gates it" should have said "one test pins the exact list".
3. Evidence understated in the finding's favour: the CLI launcher account menu already offers Grok sign-in/sign-out unconditionally (packages/cli/src/runtime/orchestration.ts:262-281, GROK_AUTH.signInLabel / signOutLabel), and the extension settings Subscriptions section does too (packages/extension/src/settingsView/frontend/components/profile/SubscriptionSection.ts:200-209). The in-chat picker is the only account surface in any host that omits Grok, which is a stronger case than the finding made.
4. Stale-reference nit: docs/proposals/2026-08-01-backend-decoupling-plan.md:652 cites `LOGIN_FORM_ITEMS (LoginForm.tsx:15-35)`; at HEAD it is 21-42. Harmless, but do not quote that range in the PR.
5. Net LoC is understated. See netLoc.

<details><summary>Verifier reasoning</summary>

This is a defect, not a speculative refactor, and it has two independent legs. The weaker leg is the picker omission: `/login`'s own usage string names `grok`, the parser accepts it, the handler routes it, `/api` lists it, `texra auth grok login` exists, the launcher menu offers it, and the extension settings panel offers it — the in-chat picker is the single surface that cannot reach the path. The stronger leg needs no judgement at all: "Sign out of both accounts" is a false statement about code that signs out three accounts, and it has been false since Grok landed in logoutFromChat. Neither leg is defensible as intentional, because nothing in the two form files, in loginOptions.ts, or in any dated doc says the picker should lag the command. The "experimental" framing in the 2026-08-04 proposal is the only thing resembling a gate, and HEAD has already shipped past it on five other surfaces, so invoking it here would be selective. The give-up clause is worth keeping in the PR description, but even under it the copy fix stands. The main thing the finding got wrong is the cost story: it assumed the Grok copy strings already exist, so it priced a two-file edit when the change actually spans four files including a copy module whose header comment insists user-facing strings live there.

</details>

### DraftAttachmentStore.resolveMedia and isEmpty lost their production callers; a doc comment still points readers at the dead one

- **Slice**: b2 · **Kind**: delete · **Risk**: low · **Net**: -14 LoC (proposer claimed -16; verifier figure governs)
- **Files**: `packages/cli/src/chat/tui/input/draftAttachments.ts`, `src/test-kernel/cli/DraftAttachments.vitest.ts`

**Evidence**

`resolveMedia` (draftAttachments.ts:151-158, 8 lines with its doc block) is `this.resolveImages(input).map((entry) => entry.path)`. The one place that needs media paths no longer calls it: InputBar.tsx:275-276 does `const images = store.resolveImages(submitted); const mediaFiles = images.map((image) => image.path);` — it needs the entries themselves for `lastSubmittedImagesRef` (InputBar.tsx:277, the refused-follow-up draft restore at :201-220), so it inlined the map and left `resolveMedia` behind. `isEmpty()` (draftAttachments.ts:111-113) has no caller at all.

Dedupe/consumer check: `grep -rn "resolveMedia|\.isEmpty()" packages/cli/src src` returns, for resolveMedia, only its definition, the `{@link resolveMedia}` in expandText's doc comment (draftAttachments.ts:124), and two test assertions (DraftAttachments.vitest.ts:73, :89); for isEmpty on this class, only DraftAttachments.vitest.ts:94,96 (the other `.isEmpty()` hits are `session.followUps` in src/agent/, a different type). Zero production callers for both.

The stale comment is the giveaway that this drifted rather than being deliberate: expandText's doc (draftAttachments.ts:120-125) tells the reader "the image bytes ride along as media files (see {@link resolveMedia})", naming a method no production path executes. Not in the rounds 1-4 index (no `resolveMedia`/`DraftAttachmentStore` entry) and no hit in the three survey docs under docs/proposals/.

**Proposal**

Delete `resolveMedia` (draftAttachments.ts:151-158) and `isEmpty` (:111-113). Repoint expandText's `{@link resolveMedia}` at `resolveImages`, which is what actually carries the image bytes now. In DraftAttachments.vitest.ts, rewrite the two `resolveMedia` assertions against `resolveImages(...).map(e => e.path)` (same values) and drop the two `isEmpty()` assertions from the 'clears entries and resets the id counter' case — the id-reset assertion on the next line already proves `clear()` worked.

**What we give up**

A two-line convenience accessor a future caller might want. `resolveImages(x).map(e => e.path)` is the same expression at the one site that would need it, and that site already writes it.

**Verifier corrections — these override the evidence and proposal above**

1. Path imprecision: the evidence cites "InputBar.tsx" without a directory; the real file is packages/cli/src/chat/tui/panes/InputBar.tsx, not .../tui/input/InputBar.tsx (only draftAttachments.ts lives under input/). Line numbers 275-277 and 201-220 are all correct for that file.
2. Line accounting: resolveMedia is 151-158 inclusive of its doc block (8 lines), plus the blank separator at 159 or 150; isEmpty is 111-113 (3 lines) plus one blank separator. Test edits net roughly -2 (the two resolveMedia assertions rewrite to the same line count via `resolveImages(...).map(e => e.path)`; only the two isEmpty assertions vanish). That totals about -14, not -16.
3. The proposal to just drop the two isEmpty assertions loses the only coverage that clear() actually empties the entry map — the id-reset assertion on the next line proves only that nextId went back to 1, not that entries were cleared. A one-line substitute keeps it at net 0: assert `store.expandText(chip)` returns the chip unchanged after clear(). This is a small correction to the proposal, not a reason to refute.
4. The doc block being deleted with resolveMedia carries the only statement of the orphan-gate rationale ("Orphaned chips (deleted from the text) are dropped, matching Claude Code's orphan gate"). resolveImages' current one-liner ("Image entries whose chip survives in `input`, in chip order.") implies it but does not say it. Moving that sentence onto resolveImages costs ~2 lines and is the right call; the proposal only says to repoint the {@link}.
5. The finding says the other `.isEmpty()` hits are "session.followUps in src/agent/, a different type" — accurate, but the full hit set also includes packages/cli/src/chat/tui/forms/_shared/useAsyncListForm.ts:135 (an unrelated `options.isEmpty` callback), src/transcript/ResidentStreamRegistry.ts:71 (a free function), and packages/agent/dist/types/.../FollowUpQueue.d.ts (build output). None touch DraftAttachmentStore, so the conclusion stands.

<details><summary>Verifier reasoning</summary>

Both methods are verifiably caller-free in production at HEAD, and git history shows exactly how they were orphaned rather than left deliberately. The stale `{@link resolveMedia}` in expandText's doc is a genuine (if small) correctness problem in the comment: it directs a reader to a method no production path executes, which is the kind of drift AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md "Exports are contracts" targets. The surface is CLI-internal with two importers, so there is no wire, settings, or SDK exposure, no ratchet edit, and no prior ruling to defeat. The deletion is bounded, the compiler and the two-file import graph prove it, and the net is a modest but real element reduction. Risk is low: the only behavioral surface touched is test coverage of clear(), and that is preserved with a one-line substitute.

</details>

### UserQuestion carries two guards that its own earlier returns already made unreachable

- **Slice**: b2 · **Kind**: delete · **Risk**: low · **Net**: -8 LoC (proposer claimed -9; verifier figure governs)
- **Files**: `packages/cli/src/chat/tui/modals/UserQuestion.tsx`

**Evidence**

(1) `submitAnswer` opens with `if (!question) { onDecide(userQuestionDecision(answers)); return; }` (UserQuestion.tsx:490-493). Four lines below, the component early-returns `if (!question) return <Text />;` (UserQuestion.tsx:503) — before `variantProps` is built (:505-512) and before any variant that could call `onSubmit` is rendered (:514-516). `submitAnswer` is reachable only through `props.onSubmit` on a rendered variant, and a variant only renders from a pass where `question` was defined and closed over. So the guard is dead, and the decision it would make (submit whatever answers exist, with no answer for the current question) is a behaviour nothing can trigger.

(2) In `boundedUserQuestionPromptLines`, the branch at :215 is entered only when `lines.length > maxDisplayLines` (:213 returns otherwise) with `lines = [...contextLines, ...questionLines]` (:212), and only when `questionLines.length >= maxDisplayLines`, which makes `visibleQuestionLines.length === maxDisplayLines` (:216). Therefore `hiddenRows = contextLines.length + questionLines.length - maxDisplayLines = lines.length - maxDisplayLines`, which is strictly positive on this path — so `if (hiddenRows <= 0) return visibleQuestionLines;` (:219) can never fire. The `?? { kind: 'overflow', text: '' }` fallback for `visibleQuestionLines[0]` (:223-226) is dead for the same reason: `maxDisplayLines > 0` is enforced at :198, so the slice has at least one element.

Both are internal to the function/component, so a direct test caller cannot revive them. No matching entry in the rounds 1-4 index; `UserQuestion` appears there only in round 3's approval-gate item (a different subject) and nothing in docs/proposals/ names `boundedUserQuestionPromptLines`.

**Proposal**

Delete UserQuestion.tsx:490-493 (the `!question` guard in `submitAnswer`, keeping the rest of the body), UserQuestion.tsx:219 (`if (hiddenRows <= 0) ...`), and collapse :223-226 to `visibleQuestionLines[0]` with a non-null assertion or a single destructure above the return. Keep the `if (!question) return <Text />` at :503 — that is the live guard.

**What we give up**

Two defensive branches that encode a state the render order forbids. If someone later moves the `!question` early return below `variantProps`, they reintroduce the case — and would get a type error on `question` at that point, which is the better signal.

**Verifier corrections — these override the evidence and proposal above**

1. Net LoC is -8, not -9, for the proposal exactly as written: 4 lines at :490-493, 1 line at :219, and 3 lines from collapsing the four-line `?? { ... }` (:223-226) to `line: visibleQuestionLines[0],`. ### BaseTextInput.discardDraft consults an image-paste queue that no input registering for Ctrl-C discard can ever have work in — InputBar owns that guard on the live path

- **Slice**: b2 · **Kind**: delete · **Risk**: medium · **Net**: -7 LoC (proposer claimed -6; verifier figure governs)
- **Files**: `packages/cli/src/chat/tui/input/BaseTextInput.tsx`, `packages/cli/src/chat/tui/panes/InputBar.tsx`, `packages/cli/src/chat/tui/App.tsx`

**Evidence**

Two copies of the same guard exist. BaseTextInput.tsx:488-500: `discardDraft` returns false when `latest.value.length === 0 && !imagePasteQueue.hasPending && !imagePasteQueue.hasDeferredAction`, else calls `imagePasteQueue.discardPending()` and clears. InputBar.tsx:161-171 restates it verbatim over its own queue and `draftValueRef`.

Only one of the two is live for the queue. BaseTextInput registers through `useActiveDraft(discardDraft, focus)` (BaseTextInput.tsx:501), and `useActiveDraft` no-ops unless the context registry is present (activeDraft.tsx:52-57). App.tsx:777-779 supplies the registry only when `active={foregroundOpen || reverseSearchOpen}`. In both of those states the InputBar's own BaseTextInput has `focus=false`: `focus={keyboardActive && !disabled && !reverseSearchOpen}` (InputBar.tsx:465) and `inputDisabled = appInputDisabled || childInputHidden` with `appInputDisabled = foregroundOpen || childListFocused` (App.tsx:225,229) feeding `disabled` (App.tsx:793). So the instances that actually register are the modal/form inputs — ConfirmCard.tsx:101, ExternalInquiry.tsx:313, UserQuestion.tsx:425, ConfigForm.tsx:217, ApiKeyEntryForm.tsx:88, ReverseSearch.tsx:59 — and `grep -rn imagePasteQueue|onImagePaste packages/cli/src` shows InputBar.tsx:477,487 as the only site that passes either prop. Every registering instance therefore runs on the fallback queue created at BaseTextInput.tsx:396-399, into which nothing is ever tracked (`track` is called only from the Ctrl-V branch at :603, gated on `props.onImagePaste`), so `hasPending`/`hasDeferredAction` are permanently false and `discardPending()` is a no-op.

The queue-aware discard that matters runs through the other copy: App.tsx:714-720 tries `activeDraftRegistry.discard()` first and falls back to `inputBarRef.current?.discardDraft()`, which is InputBar's copy (InputBar.tsx:161-175 via `useImperativeHandle`).

Not in the rounds 1-4 index (no ImagePasteQueue/discardDraft entry) and no hit in the survey docs.

**Proposal**

Reduce BaseTextInput.tsx:488-500 to the value check plus the clear (`if (syncLatestExternalValue().value.length === 0) return false; applyEdit({ value: '', cursor: 0 }); return true;`), dropping the three `imagePasteQueue` interactions and the prop from its dep array. Leave InputBar.tsx:161-171 exactly as is — that is the copy App.tsx:720 reaches, and it is the one with a real queue. Keep the fallback queue instance at BaseTextInput.tsx:396-399: `submitAfterImagePastes` and the `hasDeferredAction` keystroke gate still read it unconditionally.

**What we give up**

The generic input would no longer defend against a queue it might be handed in some future wiring where a paste-capable input is also the registered draft owner. That wiring does not exist today, and the guard is one line to restore. Marked medium because the proof rests on the App-level focus invariant rather than on types.

**Verifier corrections — these override the evidence and proposal above**

1. App.tsx:713-720 is not a bare fallback: `activeDraftRegistry.discard() || (appDraftDiscardActive({inputDisabled, reverseSearchOpen, childListFocused}) && (inputBarRef.current?.discardDraft() ?? false))`. appDraftDiscardActive (appInteractionPolicy.ts:110-120) returns `!inputDisabled && !reverseSearchOpen && !childListFocused`, so the InputBar path runs only when the registry is inactive. This strengthens rather than weakens the claim; the finding omitted it.
2. The proof that the fallback queue stays empty needs one more link than the finding gives. It is not only that `track` is gated on `props.onImagePaste` (:603); `deferUntilIdle` (imagePasteQueue.ts) returns false and stores nothing when `!hasPending`, so no submit path can set `deferredAction` either. Without that, `submitAfterImagePastes` (:506) would look like a second writer.
3. Minor line-number drift: `useActiveDraft` is activeDraft.tsx:51-58 (effect body 54-57), not 52-57; ActiveDraftScope is 36-47 and supplies `undefined` to the context when inactive.
4. The finding does not mention that the same permanently-false read appears at BaseTextInput:539 and :652 (`imagePasteQueue.hasDeferredAction` keystroke and paste gates) for fallback-queue instances. Keeping them, as the proposal does, is defensible because they are single-expression reads on the hot input path that the queue-owning InputBar instance genuinely needs, but the asymmetry is a judgment call, not something the evidence proves.
5. The residual risk is stated slightly too softly. Removing the guard makes a generic reusable input's correctness depend on an App-level focus/disabled invariant that no type, test, or comment enforces. If the deletion lands, it should carry a one-line comment at the fallback-queue site (396-399) recording that only InputBar supplies a real queue and that a queue-bearing input must never be the registered active draft. Medium risk is the right label.
6. Claimed net -6 is a slight undercount.

<details><summary>Verifier reasoning</summary>

Independently re-read every cited line. The invariant chain closes: the registry only exists when foregroundOpen || reverseSearchOpen; foregroundOpen forces appInputDisabled -> inputDisabled -> disabled, and reverseSearchOpen is read from the same signal in both App and InputBar, so InputBar's BaseTextInput has focus=false in exactly the states where useActiveDraft could register it. Every other BaseTextInput instance gets the fallback queue, into which neither track nor deferUntilIdle can ever put work. So all three imagePasteQueue interactions inside BaseTextInput.discardDraft are constant-false reads plus a no-op call, while the identical live guard sits in InputBar over a real queue. Not previously recorded, no ruling, no comment defending it, no external contract, no test churn.

</details>

### StatusBar's subscription-quota poll catches a rejection getUsage cannot produce, and the arm it runs is what the real failure path already renders

- **Slice**: b2 · **Kind**: delete · **Risk**: low · **Net**: -5 LoC
- **Files**: `packages/cli/src/chat/tui/panes/StatusBar.tsx`

**Evidence**

StatusBar.tsx:238-242 attaches `.catch(() => { if (desiredUsageProviderRef.current === provider) setSubscriptionQuotaRead(undefined); })` to `subscriptionUsage.getUsage(provider)`.

`getUsage` cannot reject. Its class doc says so — SubscriptionUsageService.ts:99-101: "always resolve to a snapshot instead of exposing provider transport failures to extension or CLI consumers" — and the code holds it: the only await outside a try is `adapter.resolveVariant?.()`, wrapped at SubscriptionUsageService.ts:187-192 returning `this.unavailable(provider, 'request_failed')`; every transport path goes through `fetchUsage`, whose body is one try/catch (SubscriptionUsageService.ts:262-290) that maps SyntaxError / CodexAuthError / SubscriptionUsageHttpError / anything else onto an `unavailable` snapshot. The cache/pending plumbing in between (:196-224) does no throwing work. StatusBar.tsx:74 constructs the service itself (`new SubscriptionUsageService()`), so no injected implementation can widen the contract.

The arm is also behaviourally redundant: statusBarDisplay.ts:219-222 renders nothing for a non-`available` snapshot (`if (snapshot?.state !== 'available') return undefined`), so storing the real `unavailable` snapshot and clearing to `undefined` produce the identical status bar. Note the contrast with the sibling poll ~40 lines above in the same file (StatusBar.tsx:183-201), which is the block that genuinely can reject and does surface it with a latched `[warn]` to stderr — that one is correct and must stay.

No entry in the rounds 1-4 index for StatusBar quota/subscriptionQuotaRead; round 4A's StatusBar entry was about the key-hint width table (refuted) and is unrelated.

**Proposal**

Drop the `.catch(...)` from the `getUsage` chain at StatusBar.tsx:238-242, leaving the `.then` with its `desiredUsageProviderRef` staleness guard. `void`-ing the promise stays correct because the chain can no longer reject. Do not replace it with a logging catch: there is no failure to log, and the `unavailable` snapshot is already the designed carrier of that information.

**What we give up**

Nothing observable. If a future refactor makes getUsage rejectable, the loss is an unhandled rejection instead of a silently cleared chip — which is the louder failure the repo's silent-degradation rule prefers anyway.

**Verifier corrections — these override the evidence and proposal above**

1. Line-range imprecision (all minor, none a misread): the class doc is the block at SubscriptionUsageService.ts:99-102 with the quoted sentence on 100-101, not 99-101. The resolveVariant guard is `try/catch` at 189-193 (return at 192), not "wrapped at 187-192" — 187-188 are the adapter lookup and `let variant` declaration. `fetchUsage` spans 262-292 (the file is 293 lines), not 262-290. The `state !== 'available'` guard is statusBarDisplay.ts:222 inside `subscriptionQuotaSegment` (219-238); "219-222" covers signature-plus-guard, which is fine but should be cited as :222.

2. "The chain can no longer reject" is imprecise. The `.catch` today also covers a synchronous throw from the `.then` body (`setSubscriptionQuotaRead`), not only from `getUsage`. A React state update scheduled outside render does not throw synchronously in Ink's reconciler, so removal is still safe, but the claim should be stated as "`getUsage` cannot reject and the then-body cannot throw in practice", not as a property of the chain as a whole.

3. Missing evidence that strengthens the finding: the never-reject contract is pinned by a test, not only by a doc comment — src/test-kernel/controllers/modelAccess/SubscriptionUsageService.vitest.ts:579-609. Cite it in the PR; it is what makes this a contract rather than a current-implementation accident.

4. The "Give up" section is wrong on one fact. There is no `process.on('unhandledRejection')` handler anywhere in CLI production code (`grep` finds it only in src/test-kernel/**). Under Node's default `--unhandled-rejections=throw`, a future rejection would terminate the process and kill the whole TUI session, not merely leave a chip stale. That is a session crash over a usage-quota poll, which is not obviously "the louder failure the repo's silent-degradation rule prefers". It does not flip the verdict — the contract is documented and tested — but the honest framing is "the guard is unreachable under a tested contract", not "crashing would be better".

5. Provenance worth adding: `git log -L238,242:packages/cli/src/chat/tui/panes/StatusBar.tsx` shows the block arrived in 411b312d3e as part of a generalization refactor, so no prior incident is being undone.

<details><summary>Verifier reasoning</summary>

The central factual claim is verifiable and I verified it end to end rather than trusting the write-up: `getUsage` has no unguarded throw or reject path, its class doc states the guarantee, StatusBar constructs the service itself so the contract cannot be widened by injection, and a dedicated test asserts `.resolves` for both sync-throw and rejected-promise failure modes. The `.catch` arm is therefore unreachable code, and even if it ran it would produce a status bar identical to storing the `unavailable` snapshot, since the only consumer returns undefined for any non-`available` state. No dedupe hit, no dated ruling, no self-documenting comment, no external contract, no ratchet. Cost is a clean -5 with one modified line and zero additions. The finding correctly distinguishes this from the sibling route poll at :183-201, which genuinely can reject and correctly latches a `[warn]` — refuting that distinction would have been the strongest kill and it does not hold. Remaining issues are citation-offset nits and one overstated "give up" framing about unhandled rejections, which I record as corrections rather than grounds for refutation.

</details>

### EditApproval mirrors ConfirmCard's feedback-mode state in a ref whose value is always the negation of the argument it is compared against

- **Slice**: b2 · **Kind**: delete · **Risk**: low · **Net**: -2 LoC (proposer claimed -4; verifier figure governs)
- **Files**: `packages/cli/src/chat/tui/modals/EditApproval.tsx`, `packages/cli/src/chat/tui/modals/ConfirmCard.tsx`

**Evidence**

EditApproval keeps `feedbackModeRef` (EditApproval.tsx:85) purely to test `if (feedbackModeRef.current && !active && feedbackWasCompactRef.current)` inside `handleFeedbackModeChange` (:143-145), writing it back at :147.

Its producer only ever reports transitions. ConfirmCard's `onFeedbackModeChange` fires exclusively from `setFeedbackActive` (ConfirmCard.tsx:87-90), which has two call sites: `setFeedbackActive(false)` at :117, reachable only inside `if (feedbackMode)` (:115) which returns at :120; and `setFeedbackActive(true)` at :140 for the `'feedback'` action, which the same `if (feedbackMode) { … return; }` makes reachable only when feedbackMode is false. `feedbackMode` starts false (:77) and ConfirmCard is an unkeyed child of EditApproval (EditApproval.tsx:165), so the two mount and unmount together. Calls therefore strictly alternate true, false, true, … and at every call `feedbackModeRef.current === !active`, making the first conjunct a tautology and the ref a pure mirror of the argument.

The other two refs in this component are not mirrors and must stay: `feedbackWasCompactRef` (:86) latches a fact the argument does not carry (whether the diff was compact while feedback was open, set from the effect at :133-137 as well as at :140-142), and `feedbackExitCount` (:84) is the scroll reset key at :117.

No entry in the rounds 1-4 index for EditApproval feedback state; round 1's `compactRows` correction touched EditApproval only as a non-passing importer of a scroll-bounds parameter.

**Proposal**

Delete `feedbackModeRef` (EditApproval.tsx:85) and its write at :147, and simplify the condition at :143 to `if (!active && feedbackWasCompactRef.current) setFeedbackExitCount((count) => count + 1);`. `handleFeedbackModeChange`'s dep array is unaffected (it never depended on the ref).

**What we give up**

Protection against ConfirmCard someday emitting a redundant `onFeedbackModeChange(false)`. That would be a bug in ConfirmCard's own toggle, and this ref hides it rather than reporting it; the worst symptom without the ref is one extra scroll-position reset.

**Verifier corrections — these override the evidence and proposal above**

1. netLoc is −2, not −4. Only two whole lines disappear: the declaration at EditApproval.tsx:85 and the write at :147. The condition at :143 shortens in place and stays one line; the `useRef` import stays (feedbackWasCompactRef still needs it).

2. The proposal's suggested brace-less one-liner does not survive prettier: `      if (!active && feedbackWasCompactRef.current) setFeedbackExitCount((count) => count + 1);` is ~92 columns, so prettier re-wraps it. Keep the existing braced three-line form and just drop the first conjunct — same line count either way.

3. Line citation off by one: `feedbackExitCount` is read inside the `scrollResetKey` memo at :116 (the memo spans :112-121), not :117 (:117 is `hunks,`). Its declaration at :84 and dep-array entry at :120 are cited correctly.

4. The stated justification is weaker than it needs to be. "At every call `feedbackModeRef.current === !active`" is true only because ConfirmCard's two call sites are mutually exclusive through a `feedbackMode` value read from a render closure; two handler invocations batched before a re-render would read that value stale. The finding is still right, but for a better reason: `feedbackWasCompactRef.current ⟹ feedbackModeRef.current` is a local invariant of EditApproval alone (see refutation), so the first conjunct is dead no matter how ConfirmCard behaves. Use that in the PR body — it makes the change provably behavior-preserving without an argument about Ink's input batching.

5. Minor: the finding says ConfirmCard "is an unkeyed child of EditApproval… so the two mount and unmount together". True, but note EditApproval itself is also unkeyed in ApprovalModal.tsx:38-44, so consecutive queued approvals reuse the instance and both feedback states persist across payload changes. That does not affect the conclusion (the ref and ConfirmCard's state persist in lockstep), but the mount/unmount framing is not the reason the invariant holds.

<details><summary>Verifier reasoning</summary>

Re-read both files at HEAD and confirmed every structural claim. The guard `feedbackModeRef.current && !active && feedbackWasCompactRef.current` at EditApproval.tsx:143 can never be decided by its first conjunct: `feedbackWasCompactRef` is only ever set true while `feedbackModeRef` is true (:141 immediately before :147, and the effect at :133-137 keyed off the `feedbackMode` state that :148 keeps identical to the ref), and it is cleared at :146 one line before the ref is cleared at :147. So the third conjunct implies the first, unconditionally and without any assumption about ConfirmCard's emission pattern. The ref is a pure mirror with no readers other than that dead test. No duplicate in the round 1-4 index or the survey docs, no dated ruling, no comment defending it, no test rendering the component, no external contract. The change is a two-line deletion with no new code, so it is not churn. Only the cost figure and one line citation are wrong, neither fatal.

</details>

### orderedStaticTranscriptEntries re-asks the finalized question it just answered, through a single-caller helper

- **Slice**: b3 · **Kind**: consolidate · **Risk**: low · **Net**: -16 LoC (proposer claimed -12; verifier figure governs)
- **Files**: `packages/cli/src/chat/tui/panes/transcriptEntries.ts`

**Evidence**

In `orderedStaticTranscriptEntries` (packages/cli/src/chat/tui/panes/transcriptEntries.ts:256-288) the loop body is:

```ts
for (const [index, entry] of entries.entries()) {
  if (!isFinalizedTranscriptRow(entry, index, finalizedFrontier)) break;   // :267
  if (!isStaticTranscriptEntryAt(entries, index, finalizedFrontier, status)) continue;  // :268
  …
}
```

`isStaticTranscriptEntryAt` (:212-225) is:

```ts
const row = rows[index];
return (
  row !== undefined && // :220
  isFinalizedTranscriptRow(row, index, finalizedFrontier) && // :221
  isRenderableTranscriptEntry(row) &&
  !userPromptAwaitsLiveContinuation(rows, index, status)
);
```

Two of its four conditions are already settled at the call site: :221 restates the guard the caller evaluated one line earlier at :267, and :220 cannot be false because `entry` comes from `entries.entries()`. The helper also re-indexes `rows[index]` to recover the row the caller already holds, and it re-threads `finalizedFrontier` purely to feed the redundant check.

It is a single-caller extraction: `grep -rn isStaticTranscriptEntryAt` over the repo returns exactly the definition at :212 and the one use at :268 — no export, no test reference. AGENTS.md's design guardrails ban single-caller helpers, and CLAUDE.md's "Abstraction discipline" calls for collapsing them.

The sibling paths in the same file already inline the equivalent predicate rather than routing through this helper: `splitTranscriptEntries` (:310-345) and `incrementalStaticTranscriptEntries` (:452-469) each check finalized, then renderable, then the live-user-prompt deferral inline. Only the full-rebuild path takes the detour, and it pays for the duplicated finalized check on every row of every rebuild.

Dedupe: no hit for `isStaticTranscriptEntryAt` in any docs/proposals survey doc. Round 3's refuted "splitTranscriptEntries computes a `finalized` bucket on every live-region frame that no production caller reads" is a different function and a different claim (a discarded output, not a duplicated guard).

**Proposal**

Delete `isStaticTranscriptEntryAt` (:211-225) and replace the call at :268-270 with the two checks it uniquely contributes:

```ts
if (!isRenderableTranscriptEntry(entry)) continue;
if (userPromptAwaitsLiveContinuation(entries, index, status)) continue;
```

This leaves the loop reading in the same order as the other two walks in the file (finalized → renderable → live-prompt deferral) and drops one `isFinalizedTranscriptRow` call and one array index per row per rebuild. The doc comment on :176-182 for `isFinalizedTranscriptRow` and the one on :211 fold into a single inline comment.

**What we give up**

Nothing. The composite predicate has one caller, and the two conditions removed are provably already true at that caller. ConversationTranscript.vitest.ts exercises `orderedStaticTranscriptEntries` and will catch an ordering change.

**Verifier corrections — these override the evidence and proposal above**

1. NET LOC UNDERSTATED. Claimed -12; honest is about -16. The helper block is :211-225 = 15 lines, plus its trailing blank line = 16 removed. The call site `:268-270` (3 lines, prettier-wrapped) becomes 2 lines = -1 more. That is -17 raw; budget +1 for a one-line comment at the call site preserving the "belongs in append-only scrollback" intent, landing at -16.

2. THE :176-182 DOC MUST NOT BE FOLDED. The proposal says "The doc comment on :176-182 for `isFinalizedTranscriptRow` and the one on :211 fold into a single inline comment." Wrong. `isFinalizedTranscriptRow` has three live callers after this change (:267, :311, :454) and its doc is the only place explaining the two halves of "finalized" — the projector's `isSelfSettledRow` versus the fold's `StreamSlice.finalizedFrontier` promotion cursor. Delete only the `:211` line. My -16 assumes :176-182 stays.

3. THE `row !== undefined` REASONING IS RIGHT, THE IMPLIED CAUSE IS NOT. `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` is not enabled — tsconfig.json:167 sets only `"strict": true`, and there is no `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` key in tsconfig.json or packages/cli/tsconfig.json. So `rows[index]` is already typed `TranscriptRow`, and `:220` is a redundant _runtime_ check, not a type-narrowing necessity the inlined form has to replace. (The `!` assertions at :277, :444, :453 in the same file are likewise decorative under this config.) Conclusion unchanged, warrant corrected.

4. THE "SIBLING PATHS INLINE THE EQUIVALENT PREDICATE" CLAIM IS LOOSE. `splitTranscriptEntries` (:310-345) does not check finalized-then-renderable: it computes `entryFinalized` first only to maintain the `canPromoteToStatic` barrier (:319-321), then checks `isRenderableTranscriptEntry` at :322, then the deferral at :323, and only consults `entryFinalized` for bucketing at :327. And `incrementalStaticTranscriptEntries` (:452-469) never calls `userPromptAwaitsLiveContinuation` at all — it hand-inlines the rule at :461-466 against a precomputed backward `hasLaterRenderable` array. The structural point (only the full-rebuild path routes through a composite helper) survives; "same order in all three" does not.

5. THE PERF FRAMING OVERSELLS. "pays for the duplicated finalized check on every row of every rebuild" is literally true but negligible — one extra predicate call and one array index per row on a path that only runs on cursor mismatch (fold rebuild, owner switch, hard reset), the ordinary tick going through `incrementalStaticTranscriptEntries`. Round-3:2776 records that the 2026-05-31 TUI performance audit graded this exact path LOW. Sell this on element count and the single-caller ban, not on speed.

6. ROUND 3 DID RULE ON THIS FILE. The finding's dedupe says "Round 3's refuted [claim] is a different function and a different claim" — correct, but it should cite that the same round-3 entry independently confirms the three-predicate composition, which strengthens rather than threatens this finding. Worth quoting in the PR so a reviewer does not mistake this for a re-litigation of the refuted merge.

<details><summary>Verifier reasoning</summary>

The structural claim is exactly true and I confirmed it by re-reading the file rather than trusting the excerpt. `isStaticTranscriptEntryAt` has one caller, is unexported, and two of its four conjuncts are dead at that caller — `:221` restates the very predicate `:267` evaluated one line earlier with identical arguments, and `:220` guards against a hole in an array that `:267` already dereferenced. What remains is two predicates the caller can name directly.

What makes this survive where its round-3 sibling died is cost asymmetry. The refuted claim required rewriting 18 assertion sites across three suites to drop `splitTranscriptEntries`' `finalized` bucket, netting +24 LoC at best. This one has zero test surface: `grep` returns no test reference to the helper, and `ConversationTranscript.vitest.ts` drives `orderedStaticTranscriptEntries` from the outside, so it validates the inlining for free. The diff is one function deletion and a two-line call-site substitution inside a single file — no type moves, no ratchet, no wire, no settings key.

The equivalence is provable rather than empirical, which is what makes the low risk honest: the loop breaks on the first non-finalized row, so the redundant conjunct cannot change the candidate set, and the surviving two are applied in the order `userPromptAwaitsLiveContinuation`'s own doc at :191 demands. The one real trap the proposal walks into is collateral: it suggests folding away the :176-182 doc on `isFinalizedTranscriptRow`, a function that keeps three callers and whose doc is the only written explanation of the projector/fold split behind "finalized." Delete :211 only.

This is a small win, and I want to be honest that it is small — around -16 lines and one element. It clears the bar because CLAUDE.md:185-187 and AGENTS.md:645 name single-caller extractions specifically, the cost is real and negative, and nothing has to be built to replace what goes away.

</details>

### One of statusBarBindingsText's 15 fallback rows is provably unreachable, and two more differ from later rows only by an inert gate

- **Slice**: b3 · **Kind**: delete · **Risk**: low · **Net**: -2 LoC (proposer claimed -8; verifier figure governs)
- **Files**: `packages/cli/src/chat/tui/panes/statusBarDisplay.ts`

**Evidence**

`statusBarBindingsText` (packages/cli/src/chat/tui/panes/statusBarDisplay.ts:610-699) builds a 15-entry widest-first cascade and hands it to `firstRowThatFits` (:590-602), which returns the first candidate whose `textDisplayWidth` fits.

**Row 14 (:690, `transcriptAvailable && statusBarBindingRow([fullOutput, ctrlC])`) can never be selected.**

- When `childNavigationAvailable` is false, `childList` is `undefined` (:624-626), so row 11 (:687, `transcriptAvailable && statusBarBindingRow([childList, fullOutput, ctrlC])`) produces the byte-identical string under the identical `transcriptAvailable` gate, and it is earlier in the array. If row 11 fits it wins; if it does not, row 14 has the same width and does not fit either.
- When `childNavigationAvailable` is true, row 13 (:689, `childNavigationAvailable && childList`) is earlier and is strictly narrower: `childList` is `Tab sessions` (12 columns — `SESSION_LIST.openAction` is `'sessions'`, src/shared/copy/nestedRuns.ts:71) versus row 14's `Ctrl-T transcript` + separator + `Ctrl-C …` (≥30 columns).
