### Signal-exit persistence swallows both transcript flush and usage-accounting shutdown failures with bare `catch {}`

- **Slice**: b3 · **Kind**: amend · **Risk**: low · **Net**: 2 LoC (proposer claimed 6; verifier figure governs)
- **Files**: `packages/cli/src/chat/tui/sessionExitController.ts`

**Evidence**

`persistBeforePlatformShutdown` (packages/cli/src/chat/tui/sessionExitController.ts:185-196) is the only persistence step on every signal exit path (SIGINT force-exit, SIGINT preserve-exit, SIGTERM, SIGHUP — reached from :218, :231, :249 through `beginTeardown`'s signal arm at :306-316). Both awaits are wrapped in an empty catch:

```ts
try {
  await ctx.flushArtifacts();
} catch {
  // Signal exit remains best-effort, but platform shutdown must still run.
}
try {
  await runPlatformShutdown();
} catch {
  // process.exit below remains the terminal owner when shutdown fails.
}
```

What is lost is not cosmetic. `flushArtifacts` is documented three lines above (:179-184) as "Materialize buffered trace chunks, then drain the debounced StreamLog disk writes so the tail of the session isn't lost (SAVE_DEBOUNCE_MS window)" — persisted transcript data. `runPlatformShutdown` is documented at :169-176 as the path that runs "lifecycle shutdown (notably UsageLogService.dispose(), which flushes any queued usage entries)" — accounting data. Worse, `beginTeardown` prints the resume hint at :313 _before_ calling this, so on a failed flush the user is handed a `texra resume <id>` command for a session whose tail was never written, with no indication anything went wrong.

The comments defend _continuing_ past the failure, which is correct — they say nothing about why the cause is discarded, and the same function's own sibling path proves the repo's bar: the graceful arm captures a disposal failure and reports it with `log.error(...)` at :354-358. `const log = createLog('cli.sessionExit')` is already at :57 and used nowhere else in the signal arm.

Secondary drift in the same handler pair: `handleSigterm` hardcodes `handleTermSignal(143)` at :251 even though `CliExitCode.Terminated = 143` exists in packages/cli/src/runtime/exitCodes.ts:9 and is already imported in this file (used as `CliExitCode.Interrupted` at :220, `CliExitCode.AgentError` at :360); `packages/cli/src/runtime/initPlatform.ts:125` is the only user of the named constant. SIGHUP's 129 (:252) has no enum row at all.

Dedupe: no hit for `persistBeforePlatformShutdown` in any docs/proposals survey doc; nothing in the rounds 1-4 index touches CLI exit teardown. Distinct from round 4B's shipped "Run-workspace preparation failure is swallowed at debug" and "OpenAI streaming totalUsage() fallback failure logs at debug" — different files, different call sites.

**Proposal**

Make both failures loud without changing control flow: `catch (error) { log.warn(\`Transcript flush failed during signal exit; the session tail may be missing: ${toErrorMessage(error)}\`); }` and `catch (error) { log.warn(\`Platform shutdown failed during signal exit; queued usage entries may be unflushed: ${toErrorMessage(error)}\`); }`. `toErrorMessage`is already imported at :32. Optionally, in the same PR, swap the`143`literal at :251 for`CliExitCode.Terminated`and add a`Hangup: 129`row to`CliExitCode` for :252. Do NOT delete either catch — process.exit must still run.

**What we give up**

Nothing. Both exits still proceed and still call process.exit with the same code; the only change is that the cause reaches the log instead of being discarded.

**Verifier corrections — these override the evidence and proposal above**

1. FALSE: "runPlatformShutdown ... accounting data [is discarded]" / "the cause is discarded". `runCliPlatformShutdownSequence` (initPlatform.ts:94-107) catches `lifecycle.runShutdown()` and `flushNdjsonStdout()` internally and never rethrows; `createLifecycleHost.runPhase` (src/platform/defaults/lifecycleHost.ts:82-104) routes every handler failure — `UsageLogService.dispose()` included — to `onError`, which the CLI logs at ERROR via `cli.lifecycle` (initPlatform.ts:257-265). Usage-accounting failure is already loud. The finding's own title claim of "usage-accounting shutdown failures" swallowed here is wrong.

2. WRONG FIX: the proposed `catch (error) { log.warn('Platform shutdown failed during signal exit; queued usage entries may be unflushed: ...') }` at :193 is unreachable — it would never print. The correct treatment of :192-195 is DELETE (checklist §15 M6, "defensive wrapper around code that cannot throw"), leaving `await runPlatformShutdown();`. Keeping it and adding a log would ship dead code into the exact spot the finding is criticizing.

3. OVERSTATED: "the only persistence step on every signal exit path". It is the only persistence step _inside the controller's_ signal arm; the underlying `StreamLogStore` also does periodic and debounced writes, so a failure here loses the un-drained tail, not the whole session. The finding's own :179-184 quote says exactly this ("the tail of the session isn't lost"), so the body is right and only the summary line overreaches.

4. INCOMPLETE: the cause `catch (error)` will surface is usually the generic `Transcript flush failed after 3 retries; N stream(s) remain dirty.` (StreamLogStore.ts:1259-1265), because `runWriteBatch` (StreamLogStore.ts:1266+) already discards each underlying ENOSPC/EACCES with its own bare catch. The warn is still worth adding (today there is zero output), but it will not name the real I/O error. If the PR wants the actual cause, that inner catch is the second half of the fix — and it is a separate site, not covered by this finding.

5. MISLEADING: "`toErrorMessage` is already imported at :32" — true, but it is currently used only at :356, so if the second catch is deleted and only one warn added, the import stays single-use as before. No import churn either way.

6. SEVERITY FRAMING: §15 classes the surviving site as M2 (silent swallow), not as a violation of the L1 "process exit" allowance — the catch is legitimate, only the discarded cause is not. Worth stating in the PR body so a reviewer does not read the fix as removing an L1 guard.

7. The `143`/`129` riders are correct as stated and are cosmetic, not defects: `CliExitCode.Terminated = 143` at exitCodes.ts:9 with initPlatform.ts:125 its sole consumer; no `Hangup` row exists. Keep them in the same PR only as a rider; they are not what makes this finding survive.

<details><summary>Verifier reasoning</summary>

Half the finding is a misread that would have shipped an unreachable log line, but the other half is a genuine, verified silent swallow of real persisted-transcript failure on the path that simultaneously promises the user a resumable session — and defect findings are judged on whether the defect is real, not on cost. It survives on the flushArtifacts catch alone, with the shutdown catch reclassified from "swallows accounting data" to "unreachable defensive wrapper, delete it".

</details>

- **Files**: `packages/cli/src/commands/agents.ts`, `packages/cli/src/runtime/agents.ts`

**Evidence**

packages/cli/src/commands/agents.ts:32-34 reads:

```ts
if (options.includeHidden !== true) {

```

and `loadCliAgentList` opens with the identical call on the identical branch — packages/cli/src/runtime/agents.ts:218-219:

Same `options` object is passed straight through (agents.ts:35), so the caller's branch and the callee's branch are the same predicate over the same value, with byte-identical arguments in the `false` arm. `loadAgents` (src/agent/index/agentRegistry.ts:107-113) joins any in-flight load and returns early when the catalog already covers the requested remoteness, so the duplicate is a no-op rather than a second scan — but it is still a guard clause duplicated at both caller and callee.

Dedupe: `loadAgents`/`loadCliAgentList`/`listAgents` return zero hits in all four survey docs (`docs/proposals/2026-08-25-simplification-survey-49-candidates.md`, `2026-08-26-simplification-survey-round2.md`, `2026-08-26-simplification-survey-round3.md`, `2026-08-25-cli-controller-seam-audit.md`) and zero in rounds1234-index.md. Round 2 touched `src/agent/index/agentRegistry.ts` only inside the KVStoreCache batch.

**Proposal**

Delete packages/cli/src/commands/agents.ts:32-34 and drop `loadAgents` from the `@agent/index` import at :3, leaving `getCustomAgentScanIssues`. `loadCliAgentList` becomes the single owner of "load the registry at the right remoteness for this listing". **What we give up**

Also give up if `loadAgents` stops being idempotent.

**Verifier corrections — these override the evidence and proposal above**

1. Net LoC is -3, not -4. Deleting :32-34 removes three lines; line 3 is _edited_, not removed, because `getCustomAgentScanIssues` stays and `import { getCustomAgentScanIssues } from '@agent/index';` still fits on one line under prettier.

2. The finding omits its own best evidence. Provenance, not symmetry, is the argument: `17ede52fe3` added `await loadAgents({ includeRemote: false })` immediately above `await seedCliRosterFromDefaultTeam()` as that call's precondition; `c9407853f8` (#8403) removed the seeding call and left the precondition orphaned. The PR description should lead with this rather than with "guard clause duplicated at both caller and callee".

3. The finding never checked the test suite, which is the one place this could have blocked. `src/test-kernel/cli/AgentsCommand.vitest.ts:123-124` asserts `expect(agentCatalogMock.loadAgents).toHaveBeenCalledWith({ includeRemote: false })`. It survives deletion because (a) the assertion is `toHaveBeenCalledWith`, not `toHaveBeenCalledTimes` — I grepped, there is no `toHaveBeenCalledTimes` on `loadAgents` anywhere — and (b) the suite's `vi.mock('@cli/runtime/agents')` at :19-22 spreads `importOriginal()` and overrides only `resolveCliAgent`, so the real `loadCliAgentList` still runs and still calls the mocked `@agent/index` `loadAgents`. Same for the `includeHidden: true` assertion at :292 (`toHaveBeenCalledWith(undefined)`). Zero test edits needed — but the PR should say so, since a call-count assertion there would have been a genuine blocker.

4. Nit on the give-up clause: "if `loadAgents` stops being idempotent" is the wrong trigger. If it stopped being idempotent, the correct fix would still be one call, not two — the pre-call would then be an active double-scan bug rather than a no-op. The only real give-up is a reordering that puts a load-state consumer between :31 and :35.

<details><summary>Verifier reasoning</summary>

Every cited line reproduces on HEAD. The two predicates are exact complements over the same by-reference `options`, the arguments are byte-identical in the taken arm, and the two calls are adjacent with no interleaving statement, so the pre-call cannot influence anything the callee does not already do. `loadAgents` short-circuits on `catalog && !includeRemote`, so it is a no-op at runtime as well as semantically. Git history closes it: the pre-call existed only to precede `seedCliRosterFromDefaultTeam()`, which #8403 deleted without removing its precondition — a dated cause that has expired, which is the opposite of criterion 2 firing. No survey-doc or index hit, no ratchet or knip movement, no NDJSON/result-contract exposure, and the existing tests assert call arguments rather than call counts so they pass unchanged. The one thing the finding got wrong is arithmetic: the import line is edited, not deleted, so -3.

### reconcileSynthetics applies the raw kind Set where the other two fold paths call isWorkflowOperationalRow, contradicting the comment that claims one membership rule

- **Slice**: b4 · **Kind**: consolidate · **Risk**: low · **Net**: -1 LoC (proposer claimed -3; verifier figure governs)
- **Files**: `packages/cli/src/chat/tui/state/transcriptFold.ts`

**Evidence**

transcriptFold.ts:73-79 defines the container filter for workflow-operational streams:

```ts
function isWorkflowOperationalRow(row: TranscriptRow): boolean {
  if (row.kind === 'log') return row.level !== 'debug';
  return WORKFLOW_OPERATIONAL_KINDS.has(row.kind);
}
```

The log path uses it (`applyChangedLogEntry`, :690-693) and the compaction path uses it (`reconcileCompactionRows`, :723) — where the comment at :721-722 states outright: "Same container filter the log and local paths apply, so a workflow-agent stream has one membership rule rather than three."

The local (synthetic) path named in that comment does NOT use it. `reconcileSynthetics` at :751-760 reaches past the helper into the raw Set:

```ts
const wOO = state.workflowOperationalOnly;
...
if (row.origin === 'local' && (!wOO || WORKFLOW_OPERATIONAL_KINDS.has(row.kind))) {
```

So the comment's claim is false as written — there are two rules, not one. The behavioural gap is exactly the `'log'` kind, and local rows never carry it: `localTranscriptRow` (packages/cli/src/chat/tui/state/transcript.ts:42-77) mints only `'assistant' | 'error' | 'user'`, and those three are the only kinds any of the eleven `appendLocal*Transcript` call sites can produce (grepped: chatSessionController.ts:325/507/534/543/633, App.tsx:465, runChatTui.tsx:299/302/311/430/472/491, chatSubmitDriver.ts:209/210/229/260/315/332/359, sessionSignalsAdapter.ts:102, handleSlashCommand.ts:36, registerBuiltins.tsx:152/172/384, slashForms.tsx:20). So today the two spellings are behaviourally identical and the swap is a pure consolidation, not a behaviour change.

Dedupe: `reconcileSynthetics`, `isWorkflowOperationalRow`, and `WORKFLOW_OPERATIONAL_KINDS` return zero hits across all four survey docs and rounds1234-index.md. Round 3's transcriptFold ruling ("Does the CLI need its own 1,447-line transcript fold…", a KEEP) is about whether the fold should exist at all, not about its internal filter spellings.

**Proposal**

In transcriptFold.ts:753-757 replace `(!wOO || WORKFLOW_OPERATIONAL_KINDS.has(row.kind))` with `(!wOO || isWorkflowOperationalRow(row))`, and drop the now-single-use `wOO` local. That makes the comment at :721-722 true and leaves one membership function with three callers. Behaviour is provably unchanged for every row shape `localTranscriptRow` can produce; if a future local row ever carries `kind: 'log'`, it then follows the same debug-level rule as every other path instead of being dropped silently.

**What we give up**

Give up if the divergence is deliberate — i.e. if someone can point to a decision that local rows must be filtered more strictly than log rows on operational-only workflow streams. In that case the fix is the reverse direction: correct the comment at :721-722 rather than the code, since it currently asserts an invariant the module does not hold.

**Verifier corrections — these override the evidence and proposal above**

1. Claimed net -3 LoC is wrong; the honest figure is -1. Only the `const wOO = state.workflowOperationalOnly;` line at :751 disappears. The `if (...)` at :753-757 stays three lines: inlining gives `(!state.workflowOperationalOnly || isWorkflowOperationalRow(row))` at 71 columns, and the full single-line condition would exceed 80, so prettier keeps the multi-line break. No other line is removable.

2. "So the comment's claim is false as written" overstates it. The comment says the paths apply the "same container filter" so the stream has "one membership rule rather than three". For every row shape `localTranscriptRow` can mint (`assistant`, `error`, `user` — none of which is `'log'`), the two spellings return identical results, so the comment is semantically true today and only structurally loose. The finding's own dead-`'log'` analysis proves this, which weakens "there are two rules, not one" to "there are two spellings of one rule".

3. The eleven `appendLocal*Transcript` call-site enumeration is unnecessary and unverified in detail. The load-bearing proof is narrower and stronger: `origin: 'local'` is set in exactly one place repo-wide (`packages/cli/src/chat/tui/state/transcript.ts:51`), inside `localTranscriptRow`, whose `kind` parameter is typed `'assistant' | 'error' | 'user'`. No call-site census is needed.

4. Minor: the helper is at :76-79; :73-75 is its doc comment. "transcriptFold.ts:73-79 defines the container filter" is fine as a range but the function itself starts at :76.

5. The claim that `isWorkflowOperationalRow` ends with "three callers" is correct as stated (post-fix sites :691, :723, :756) — verified, no correction needed.

<details><summary>Verifier reasoning</summary>

The finding is factually accurate on every load-bearing point I could check independently at HEAD: the two spellings exist, the comment claims three paths use one filter when only two call the helper, and the divergence is unreachable today because the single `origin: 'local'` minting site cannot produce `kind: 'log'`. Dedupe is clean across the index and all four survey docs, and round 3's transcriptFold KEEP is scoped to cross-host extraction and NDJSON routing, not to this internal filter. No external consumer, no ratchet, no settled surface. What does not survive scrutiny is the size claim: -3 becomes -1, because only the `wOO` declaration goes and prettier keeps the condition on three lines. The value here is not LoC — it is removing a second spelling of a membership rule and making an existing in-code invariant comment structurally true, with a latent silent-drop hazard closed as a side effect. Inside the commit-queue slot it disables the plan (:802-805), prepares the personal client (:807), rolls back on failure (:808-819), and then calls `applyRetryCredentialCommit(decision, signal, codingPlanRollbackConfig(...))` (:820-828) — whose doc comment (:675-679) promises it "rolls back everything it wrote (plus the already-disabled coding plan, when one is supplied)".

That third argument can never be consumed. `applyRetryCredentialCommit` (:681-733) computes `oauth = oauthCliPreference(decision.disableQuotaRoute)` (:687), and `oauthCliPreference` returns `undefined` unless the id is `'chatgpt'` or `'grok'` (:663-673). `QuotaFallbackRouteId` is the disjoint union `OauthQuotaFallbackRouteId ('chatgpt'|'grok') | CodingPlanSubscriptionId` (src/shared/quotaFallbackRoutes.ts:17-19), and `isCodingPlanQuotaRoute` narrows to `CodingPlanSubscriptionId` (src/shared/quotaFallbackRoutes.ts:93-97). So on this branch `oauth` is always `undefined`, the `try` body reduces to `return;` (:690-701), and the `catch` that consumes `codingPlanRollback` (:702-732) is dead — the only statement that can throw, `signal.throwIfAborted()` (:686), sits OUTSIDE the try.

Dedupe: grepped `docs/proposals/2026-08-25-simplification-survey-49-candidates.md`, `2026-08-26-simplification-survey-round2.md`, `2026-08-26-simplification-survey-round3.md`, and `2026-08-25-cli-controller-seam-audit.md` for `applyRetryCredentialCommit`, `switchRetryToPersonalCredentials`, `codingPlanRollback` — zero hits. The only round-2/3 mentions of this file are subscribeApprovals.ts:646 (AggregateError, ruled a non-duplicate keep) and the policy-gate finding at round3:706-766 (`decideWithPolicy`/`settleRetry`), neither of which touches this function. Not in rounds1234-index.md. Not policy-protected.

Reachability of the resulting bug: `reservation.signal` aborts when a newer retry replaces this one or approvals are cleared (`clearRetryApprovalsForStream`, :371). If that lands after :807 resolves but before :686 runs, `throwIfAborted` throws past the rollback, `requestRetryInteraction`'s catch returns `{action:'cancel'}` (:496-498), and the coding-plan preference stays disabled with no message. The suite already pins the sibling case — `src/test-kernel/cli/TuiApprovalRetry.vitest.ts:990` 'restores the coding-plan preference when cancellation interrupts client preparation' covers an abort during :807 (handled by the :808 catch) — so restoring on cancel is the established intent; only this one step escapes it. No test covers the commit-step abort: grep for `codingPlanRollback`/`rollbackChangedSettings` across `src/test-kernel/cli/` returns nothing, and the one rollback-after-commit test (:1233 'reports any preference that cannot be restored after commit fails') drives the ChatGPT/oauth path.

**Proposal**

Move `signal.throwIfAborted()` from subscribeApprovals.ts:686 to the first statement inside the `try` at :690, so an abort at the commit step runs `rollbackChangedSettings` with the supplied `codingPlanRollback` and rethrows through `throwWithRollbackFailures`. That makes the third parameter and its doc comment true for the first time; net LoC ~0. If the maintainer instead decides a cancelled retry should leave the plan disabled (the current behaviour), then delete the `codingPlanRollback` parameter (:684), the argument at :822-827, and the `codingPlanRollback` half of the rollback array (:729) and correct the doc comment at :678-679 — about -10 LoC. Do not do both. Either way the fix belongs with a regression test that aborts `reservation.signal` between client preparation and the commit call.

**What we give up**

If a maintainer states that a cancelled coding-plan retry is meant to leave the plan disabled AND agrees the parameter should stay as future-proofing, drop the finding. Also drop it if `QuotaFallbackRouteId` ever gains an id that is both a coding-plan id and an oauth id (it cannot today — the union is disjoint by construction), since `oauth` would then be reachable on this branch.

**Verifier corrections — these override the evidence and proposal above**

1. Doc comment span is :675-680, not :675-679 (` */` is on 680). All other line citations verified exact: :681-733, :686, :687, :690-701, :702-732, :729, :663-673, :779-789, :802-805, :807, :808-819, :820-828, and quotaFallbackRoutes.ts:17-19 / :93-97.

2. THE RACE IS FAR NARROWER THAN STATED. The finding says the bug fires "if that lands after :807 resolves but before :686 runs" as if that were an ordinary window. It is a 2-3 microtask window, not a real interval: `prepareRetryClient` -> `runRetryTask` rejects on abort, so any abort delivered before its promise resolves is caught by the :808 catch and rolled back (that is the :990 test). After resolution, the continuation, the skipped catch, the call, and `throwIfAborted()` all run with no `await` between them, so only an abort dispatched from an already-queued microtask can interleave — a macrotask-delivered abort (the normal path for `clearRetryApprovalsForStream`) cannot. The finding should be sold on the dead parameter and false doc, not on the field reachability of the cancel.

3. THE PROPOSED FIX IS PARTIAL, WHICH THE FINDING DOES NOT SAY. When `oauth` is undefined, `applyRetryCredentialCommit` contains no `await` at all — it returns synchronously. So an abort landing _after_ :686 passes also leaves the plan disabled: the outer `runRetryTask` rejects, `requestRetryInteraction` returns `{action:'cancel'}` (:496), and no rollback runs anywhere. Moving `throwIfAborted()` into the `try` closes only the sub-window before :686; it does not make "a cancelled coding-plan retry never leaves the plan disabled" true.

4. MISSING CONTEXT THE FIX MUST RECONCILE WITH: subscribeApprovals.ts:485-487 already documents this class of late cancel — "A cancel landing while the last preparation step was already resolving has no await left to reject, so the entry's own state decides" followed by `if (reservation.signal.aborted) return { action: 'cancel' };`. This does not defeat the finding, but it is the closest thing to an intent statement in the file and it was not cited.

5. "RESTORING ON CANCEL IS THE ESTABLISHED INTENT" IS ONLY HALF TRUE. The oauth branch has the same shape: once `oauth.setPrefer(false)` succeeds, a later abort leaves the OAuth preference off with no rollback. So "a committed switch persists through a late cancel" is the existing behavior on both branches; the :990 test establishes intent for failures _before or during_ preparation only. That symmetry is why option B (delete the parameter) is a legitimate reading, not a strawman — the maintainer call is genuine.

6. Give-up condition verified sound: `CodingPlanSubscriptionId` is `'glmCodingPlan' | 'kimiCode'` and cannot be `'chatgpt' | 'grok'` today, so `oauth` is unreachable on this branch by construction.

7. Minor: TypeScript/lint cannot catch this because `codingPlanRollback` is syntactically referenced at :729 — worth stating, since it explains how the dead argument survived review.

I re-derived the reachability myself rather than trusting the write-up. `decision` reaches `applyRetryCredentialCommit` unmodified from the branch that already narrowed `decision.disableQuotaRoute` to a coding-plan id (:779-789), and `oauthCliPreference` (:663-673) returns `undefined` for anything that is not `'chatgpt'` or `'grok'`. That makes the third parameter dead code and the doc comment at :677-679 false: a real defect at zero LoC, which the brief says not to refute for being unprofitable. Since a committed OAuth switch already survives a late cancel the same way, the maintainer could reasonably pick the deletion option instead. Either way the current state — a documented rollback that provably never runs — is wrong and should not stay.

### runOrchestrationTui returns five action kinds it can never return, and the launcher loop carries five dead switch arms for them

- **Slice**: b5 · **Kind**: consolidate · **Risk**: low · **Net**: -5 LoC (proposer claimed -2; verifier figure governs)
- **Files**: `packages/cli/src/commands/orchestrate.ts`, `packages/cli/src/runtime/orchestration.ts`, `packages/cli/src/orchestration/runOrchestrationTui.tsx`

**Evidence**

`CliOrchestrationAction` (runtime/orchestration.ts:39-65) includes `browse-resumes`, `browse-agents`, `browse-teams`, `browse-accounts` and `configure-model-access`. Those five values are produced only as launcher Select item values (orchestration.ts:162, 179, 186, 196, 323 — all inside `buildCliOrchestrationItems`/`modelAccessItem`; `buildCliAgentItems` emits `chat`, `buildCliResumeItems` emits `resume`, `buildCliAccountItems` emits `account`). Inside the TUI, `onItemSelect` intercepts all five before `finish` can be reached (runOrchestrationTui.tsx:356-376: each is an `if (action.kind === …) { setStep(...); return; }`), and `finish` — the only path that resolves `renderCliPrompt` (:342-345) — is otherwise reached from the resume picker (`onSelect={finish}`, kind `resume`), the model-access picker (kind `set-model-access`), the model picker (kind `chat`/`preset`), and `goBack` (kind `exit`). So `runOrchestrationTui` can only ever return `chat`, `preset`, `resume`, `set-model-access`, `configure-settings`, `account`, `help`, `exit`. Yet orchestrate.ts:318-323 handles the five navigation kinds with `continue launcher` — unreachable arms that exist purely to keep the `switch` exhaustive over a union that is wider than the function's real range. (`configure-settings` at orchestration.ts:202 is genuinely live: `onItemSelect` does not intercept it, so it escapes to orchestrate.ts:324-331.) Dedupe: no round 1-4 title mentions orchestration actions, the launcher union, or `runOrchestrationTui`; grepped all four survey docs in docs/proposals/ for `CliOrchestrationAction`, `browse-teams`, `runOrchestrationTui` — no hits.

**Proposal**

Split the union in runtime/orchestration.ts: keep `CliOrchestrationAction` as the Select item value type, and add `CliOrchestrationResolvedAction = Exclude<CliOrchestrationAction, { kind: 'browse-resumes' | 'browse-agents' | 'browse-teams' | 'browse-accounts' | 'configure-model-access' }>`. Type `runOrchestrationTui`'s return and `OrchestrationAppProps.onResolve`/`finish` as the resolved type (the compiler then proves the five interceptions in `onItemSelect` are total), and delete the five dead arms at orchestrate.ts:318-323. The launcher `switch` stays exhaustive without a `default:`.

**What we give up**

The ability to hand a browse action back to the launcher loop from the TUI — a capability nothing uses today. Any future step that wants to bounce back out would have to widen the resolved type explicitly, which is the point.

**Verifier corrections — these override the evidence and proposal above**

1. NET LoC IS WRONG AS PROPOSED. The claimed -2 does not survive pricing the type work. Prettier-formatted, the `Exclude<CliOrchestrationAction, { kind: 'browse-resumes' | ... }>` alias plus its doc comment is roughly 12-13 lines in `runtime/orchestration.ts` against 5 deleted lines in `orchestrate.ts` — net about +8 to +10, not -2. The deletion-only variant is the only net-negative shape: about -5.

2. THE PROPOSAL BREAKS A TYPE-CHECKED CALL SITE IT DOES NOT MENTION. `runOrchestrationTui.tsx:420-427` passes `onSelect={finish}` directly to the resume picker. `Select<T>` (`packages/cli/src/tui/ui/Select.tsx:33-36`) infers `T` from `items: ReadonlyArray<SelectItem<T>>`, and `props.resumeItems` is `readonly CliOrchestrationItem[]`, so `T = CliOrchestrationAction`; `onSelect` is a function _property_ (`readonly onSelect: (value: T) => void`), hence contravariant under strictFunctionTypes. Narrowing `finish` to the resolved type makes that prop assignment an error. Fixing it needs either a wrapper lambda with a cast, a narrower `resumeItems` prop type, or a generic `CliOrchestrationItem<T>` — none of which the proposal budgets for, and each adds more than the 5 lines it removes. The claim that "the compiler then proves the five interceptions in `onItemSelect` are total" is true only for the `else { finish(action) }` tail at :382; it is not free elsewhere.

3. THE DELETION NEEDS NO TYPE WORK AT ALL, contrary to the framing that the arms "exist purely to keep the `switch` exhaustive". The switch has no `default:` and is the last statement inside `launcher: while (true)` (orchestrate.ts:165 through :382), so falling out of it is byte-for-byte the same control flow as `continue launcher`. And nothing forces exhaustiveness: `eslint.config.mjs` configures no `@typescript-eslint/switch-exhaustiveness-check`, no `default-case`, and no `noFallthroughCasesInSwitch` appears in `tsconfig.json`. So `git rm` on those five lines compiles and lints today.

4. RISK IS LOW, NOT MEDIUM. One file, five unreachable lines, no persisted data, no wire contract, no settings key, and the two vitest references are to item values the change preserves.

5. ONE COUNTERWEIGHT THE FINDING SHOULD STATE. Deleting the arms without narrowing the type turns five explicitly-handled kinds into an implicit fall-through, which is the shape CLAUDE.md calls out ("a `default: return` that quietly drops an unknown event"). It is harmless here because the kinds are unreachable, but the PR should say so in a one-line comment on the switch, or the reviewer will read it as a silent drop. That comment is the honest price of the -5.

6. Minor: the finding lists `help` in `runOrchestrationTui`'s real range without noting where it comes from — it is a launcher item at `orchestration.ts:207`, not intercepted, handled live at orchestrate.ts:376-380. That is correct, just unevidenced. All five production line cites (162/179/186/196/323) and the `configure-settings` cite (:202) check out verbatim.

<details><summary>Verifier reasoning</summary>

The core factual claim is independently verified: `runOrchestrationTui` cannot return `browse-resumes`, `browse-agents`, `browse-teams`, `browse-accounts`, or `configure-model-access`, because `onItemSelect` intercepts all five before any path to `finish`, `finish` is the only resolver of `renderCliPrompt`, and the launcher loop has exactly one producer for `action`. Five switch arms in `orchestrate.ts` are therefore dead. Not a duplicate of rounds 1-4, not covered by any dated ruling, no self-explaining comment, no external contract, no settled surface.

What does not survive is the proposal's shape and its price tag. The `Exclude` alias is net-additive and, worse, collides with `Select`'s contravariant `onSelect` prop at the resume picker, which the finding never inspected. The profitable version is the plain five-line deletion — behavior-identical because the switch is the loop's last statement and no exhaustiveness rule is configured — plus one comment line so the fall-through does not read as a silent drop. That lands at about -5 LoC at low risk, which clears this survey's thinness bar (round 1 shipped an orchestrate.ts batch verified at about -2). Ship the deletion; drop the type-narrowing half unless someone independently wants the type honesty and is willing to pay +10 for it.

</details>

### orchestrationLauncherLayout's last layout candidate and its post-loop fallback compute the identical result

- **Slice**: b5 · **Kind**: delete · **Risk**: low · **Net**: -1 LoC (proposer claimed -3; verifier figure governs)
- **Files**: `packages/cli/src/orchestration/runOrchestrationTui.tsx`

**Evidence**

`orchestrationLauncherLayoutCandidates` ends by pushing `{ statusLines: [], footerHints: [] }` (runOrchestrationTui.tsx:199). For that candidate the loop body at :220-222 computes `detailRows = orchestrationBlockRowCost([], cols) + orchestrationBlockRowCost([], cols)`, and `orchestrationBlockRowCost` returns 0 for an empty array (:113-119), so `chromeRows` is exactly `baseRows`. That is byte-identical to the post-loop fallback at :239-243, which calls `computeSelectWindowSize({ availableRows, itemCount, chromeRows: baseRows })`. The two return objects are also identical: the loop returns `{ statusLines: candidate.statusLines /* [] */, footerHints: candidate.footerHints /* [] */, ...selectWindow }` (:231-235) and the fallback returns `{ statusLines: [], footerHints: [], ...selectWindow }` (:244-248). The only difference is that the loop returns it conditionally (`>= targetVisibleItems`) and the fallback unconditionally — so whichever way the check goes, the caller receives the same value. Dedupe: grepped rounds1234-index.md for 'orchestration', 'launcher layout', 'statusLines' — no match; grepped docs/proposals/2026-08-25-simplification-survey-49-candidates.md, 2026-08-26-simplification-survey-round2.md, 2026-08-26-simplification-survey-round3.md and 2026-08-25-cli-controller-seam-audit.md for `orchestrationLauncherLayout` and `LauncherLayoutCandidate` — no hits. src/test-kernel/cli/Orchestration.vitest.ts:196-359 exercises the function through its public shape only, never the candidate list.

**Proposal**

Delete the `candidates.push({ statusLines: [], footerHints: [] })` line at runOrchestrationTui.tsx:199 and let the post-loop fallback at :239-248 be the single owner of the "nothing fits, drop all detail" outcome. Behavior is provably unchanged; the loop just stops re-deriving the fallback one iteration early.

**What we give up**

Nothing. The two paths are the same computation; only one call site of `computeSelectWindowSize` for the empty-detail case survives instead of two.

**Verifier corrections — these override the evidence and proposal above**

1. Net LoC is -1, not -3. `candidates.push({ statusLines: [], footerHints: [] });` at runOrchestrationTui.tsx:199 is a single 52-column statement that prettier keeps on one line, and nothing else becomes deletable: `orchestrationLauncherLayoutCandidates` still returns every other candidate, the post-loop fallback (:239-248) stays, and both `OrchestrationLauncherLayoutCandidate` and `orchestrationBlockRowCost` keep their other users.

2. The evidence asserts equivalence without establishing that `computeSelectWindowSize` is pure — that is the load-bearing premise. It holds (packages/cli/src/tui/selectWindow.ts:30-79 is a pure three-branch function over its three numeric inputs), but the finding should cite it rather than assume it.

3. The evidence never addresses referential identity of the returned `statusLines`/`footerHints` arrays. The loop returns the candidate's own `[]` literal and the fallback returns a different `[]` literal, so the objects are structurally, not referentially, identical. This is harmless here — `layout` is recomputed unconditionally on every render at :333 and no memo/dependency array keys on those fields — but "the caller receives the same value" is only true up to structural equality.

4. Minor framing: line 199 is not an arbitrary extra candidate, it is the `count === 0` slot the truncation loop at :187 deliberately skips (`count > 0`). Stating that in the PR is worth a sentence, because the loop bound is what makes the push look intentional at a glance.

5. The claim that the vitest suite "exercises the function through its public shape only, never the candidate list" is right, but understates the useful detail: the `rows: 10` case at :255-264 is precisely a case where the empty candidate is generated, rejected by the `>= targetVisibleItems` guard, and answered by the fallback — a concrete demonstration of the redundancy, and the regression test the PR can point at.

<details><summary>Verifier reasoning</summary>

The equivalence argument is provable and I reproduced it end to end rather than taking it on trust: orchestrationBlockRowCost returns 0 on an empty array, so the final candidate's chromeRows is exactly baseRows, and computeSelectWindowSize is a pure function of (availableRows, itemCount, chromeRows), so it returns the identical SelectWindowSize the post-loop fallback computes. The two return objects are structurally identical, and no consumer depends on array identity because layout is recomputed every render with no memo keyed on it. Therefore the final loop iteration can only either return the fallback's value or fall through to the fallback, which returns that same value. This is genuinely dead code, not a defensive belt.

None of the kill criteria apply: no dedupe hit in the rounds index or the four survey docs, no dated ruling anywhere touching this function, no self-justifying comment or guard on either site, no external contract (this is in-process TUI row math, nowhere near cliOutput.ts or emitCliResult), no ratchet or settled surface, and the cited lines survive my own re-read.

The one real error is the price: this is -1 LoC, not -3. I considered killing it on criterion 7, but the criterion targets claims whose true cost is positive or whose shape is churn — a bare one-line deletion with no addition, no relocation, and no test change is neither. It is a low-value but honest cleanup, so it survives with a corrected number. Risk is low: pure function, single call site at :333, and the one test that lands on this path (Orchestration.vitest.ts:255-264) stays green because it already reaches the fallback today.

</details>

### The launcher header is measured as "TeXRA v<x>" but rendered as "{ T } TeXRA v<x>", so the layout under-reserves rows at narrow widths

- **Slice**: b5 · **Kind**: amend · **Risk**: low · **Net**: 0 LoC
- **Files**: `packages/cli/src/orchestration/runOrchestrationTui.tsx`

**Evidence**

runOrchestrationTui.tsx:315-320 sets `title = `TeXRA v${props.version}`` for the launcher step under the comment "The launcher renders its own branded header; measure the same rows." `headerLines = [title, subtitle]` (:322) feeds `orchestrationLauncherLayout` (:333-340), which wraps each header line to `columns - 2` via `orchestrationWrappedLineRows` (:102-110) to compute `baseRows` (:207-210). But the launcher does not render that string: :478-491 renders `<Box gap={1}><Text bold>{'{ T } TeXRA'}</Text><Text dimColor>v{props.version}</Text></Box>` — 11 chars plus a 1-column gap plus `v` + version, i.e. 7 columns wider than the measured `TeXRA v<version>`. For a version like `0.40.6`, measured width is 13 and rendered width is 20, so at terminal widths 15-21 the measurement reports one header row while the render takes two, and `computeSelectWindowSize` gets a `chromeRows` that is one short — the select window overflows the frame. The comment states the invariant the code violates, so this is the comment being defeated by the code, not the reverse. Dedupe: no round 1-4 entry touches launcher header measurement; grepped the four survey docs for `headerLines`, `orchestrationWrappedLineRows`, `{ T } TeXRA` — no hits.

**Proposal**

Make the launcher's measured title the string it actually renders: `title = `{ T } TeXRA v${props.version}``, and keep the styled `<Box>` render as the presentation of that same text (or hoist the literal `'{ T } TeXRA'` into a constant used by both the measurement and the `<Text bold>`). One-line change; the comment at :315-316 then becomes true.

**What we give up**

Nothing. At wide terminals the measurement is unchanged (both wrap to one row); only the narrow-width case stops mismeasuring.

**Verifier corrections — these override the evidence and proposal above**

Three arithmetic errors, all in the same direction:

1. "7 columns wider than the measured" is wrong; it is 6. Rendered = `{ T } TeXRA` (11) + gap (1) + `v` + version. Measured = `TeXRA` (5) + space (1) + `v` + version. Difference = 12 - 6 = 6.

2. "measured width is 13 and rendered width is 20" — measured 13 is right (5+1+1+6); rendered is 19, not 20 (11+1+1+6).

3. "at terminal widths 15-21" overstates the top of the window by one. `textColumns = columns - 2`, so measured stays one row for `columns >= 15` and the render stays one row for `columns >= 21`. The divergent window is columns 15 through 20 inclusive. At 21 both are one row.

4. Understated in the other direction: the mismeasure is not confined to that window. Below 15 both strings wrap, but by different amounts — at columns 8 (`textColumns` 6) the measurement gives 3 rows and the render needs 4 — so `chromeRows` is short there too.

5. The proposed fix is directionally right but only approximately exact. A single wrapped string `{ T } TeXRA v<version>` and a nowrap flex row of two Text nodes with `gap={1}` do not break identically at every width (Yoga shrinks the two children independently rather than reflowing one string), so the fix makes the measurement correct at the one-row/two-row boundary that matters, not provably exact at every sub-21 width. Worth stating in the PR rather than claiming exact parity.

6. Honest impact framing, absent from the finding: columns 15-20 is a terminal where the launcher is already unusable — the 41-character subtitle alone wraps to three or four rows and seven items compete for what is left. The value here is that the invariant the comment asserts becomes true and the two strings stop being able to drift, not that a user-visible overflow gets fixed at any width anyone runs.

Also minor: the title citation is `:316-317` (comment then assignment), not `:315-320`.

<details><summary>Verifier reasoning</summary>

The claim is a measure-vs-render drift, and both halves are verifiable at HEAD. `orchestrationLauncherLayout` computes `baseRows` by wrapping `headerLines` to `columns - 2`, which is exactly the content width `WizardStepShell` gives the header (`paddingX={1}`), so the measurement basis is right; only the measured string is wrong. `computeSelectWindowSize` turns `chromeRows` straight into `selectRows = availableRows - chromeRows`, so a header row the measurement misses is a list row the frame does not have — the failure mode described is the real one, not invented.

What keeps this from being a strong finding is magnitude, not truth. The window where the two disagree by one row is columns 15-20, a terminal where the launcher is already broken for other reasons. So the finding earns its place as a correctness/consistency fix with a true zero-LoC cost and a comment that stops lying, not as a bug report. Under the rule that a real defect survives at zero LoC, and with no ruling, no duplicate, no external consumer, and no settled surface in the way, it stands — with the arithmetic corrected (6 columns, width 19, window 15-20) and the impact stated honestly.

</details>

### install-github-action opens the GitHub App installer in a browser before two guards that can still abort the command

- **Slice**: b5 · **Kind**: amend · **Risk**: low · **Net**: 0 LoC
- **Files**: `packages/cli/src/commands/installGithubAction.ts`

**Evidence**

`runInstallGithubAction` calls `await openGitHubAppInstaller(slug)` at installGithubAction.ts:186, which spawns a browser at `https://github.com/apps/texra-ai-bot/installations/new` via `tryOpenBrowser` (:148) and prints "Opened the TeXRA GitHub App installer…". Two later guards can still abort with `CliExitCode.Usage` and do nothing else: the existing-branch guard at :191-197 ("Branch \"…\" already exists. Pass --branch <name> or --force.") and the unresolvable-base guard at :203-209 ("Could not resolve base branch …"). So a user who runs the command twice, or with a stale `--base`, gets a browser tab for an app install they did not ask to complete plus an error telling them the command did nothing. The pre-existing-workflow guard at :177-182 is correctly ordered before the browser open, which shows the intended ordering; the other two drifted past it. There is no comment claiming the early position is deliberate.

**Proposal**

Move the `await openGitHubAppInstaller(slug)` call from :186 to just after the checkout success check at :212-217, where the command is committed to writing the workflow file. `slug`/`url` still resolve at :184-185 for the guards and `printSecretChecklist`. No new code; one statement relocates below two guards.

**What we give up**

Nothing. On the success path the installer still opens before any commit/push output, so the user sees the same sequence.

**Verifier corrections — these override the evidence and proposal above**

1. "`slug`/`url` still resolve at :184-185 for the guards" is wrong: neither the branch-exists guard (:191-197) nor the base-resolution guard (:203-209) reads `slug` or `url`. They resolve there only for openGitHubAppInstaller, printSecretChecklist (:132-143), and the push/PR paths (:286-311). Nothing about the guards constrains where :184-185 sit.
2. "a browser tab for an app install they did not ask to complete" overstates it. The command is literally named install-github-action and described as "Install the TeXRA GitHub App and scaffold code review" (:358-359), so the user did ask for the app install. The defect is narrower and still real: an externally visible side effect fires before two validations that then abort having done nothing else, and it fires inconsistently with the :177 guard, which aborts before the same side effect.
3. The "runs the command twice" repro needs a qualifier the finding omits: it only reproduces after a first run that succeeded (or otherwise got past :186), because restoreBranch puts the user back on a branch where the workflow file is absent, so the :177 guard does not catch it. A second run in the same working tree while still on the install branch hits :177 instead and never opens the browser.
4. "Nothing" under Give up is slightly generous. Post-move, the browser opens after `git checkout -b` has already run, so a user who quits at the browser prompt is left on the new branch rather than on their original one. That is still strictly better than today (today they get the tab and no branch at all), but it is a behavior change worth one line in the PR description.
5. The finding should name src/test-kernel/cli/InstallGithubAction.vitest.ts as touched-adjacent coverage so the implementer does not assume the file is untested; the move needs no test edit.

<details><summary>Verifier reasoning</summary>

Verified against HEAD by reading the whole 391-line file rather than the cited spans alone. The ordering claim is exactly as stated, the inconsistency with the :177 guard is real, no comment or commit message defends the current position, and the repro survives the obvious "wouldn't the first guard catch it?" objection. It is a genuine, low-severity UX defect: a browser launch is a user-visible side effect and it precedes two Usage-code aborts. The fix is a pure statement relocation with no LoC cost and no test churn, so neither the cost nor the churn kill applies, and the defect rule forbids refusing it for being unprofitable. Four factual sloppinesses in the write-up (the guards do not use slug; the "did not ask" framing; the missing repro precondition; the un-noted post-move branch-state change) are corrections, not kills.

</details>

### `texra config agents` calls readCliAgentRoster purely for its loadAgents side effect and throws away a whole roster snapshot plus a config-file read

- **Slice**: b5 · **Kind**: amend · **Risk**: low · **Net**: 1 LoC (proposer claimed 0; verifier figure governs)
- **Files**: `packages/cli/src/commands/config.ts`, `packages/cli/src/runtime/agentRoster.ts`

**Evidence**

config.ts:98 is a bare `await readCliAgentRoster();` whose result is discarded, immediately followed by `const roster = createWorkspaceAgentRosterController();` on :99. `readCliAgentRoster` (runtime/agentRoster.ts:24-41) does six things: `loadAgents({ includeRemote: false })`, builds its own `createWorkspaceAgentRosterController()`, takes `roster.snapshot()`, reads `platform().workspace.getWorkspacePath()`, `await loadWorkspaceCliConfig(cwd)` (a `.texra/config.json` read + JSON parse + per-field Zod validation whose `warnings` array is dropped on the floor by this reader), and a `byCategory` walk of `getEnabledAgentKeys`. Only the first of those — loading the registry so the controller on :99 can resolve agent keys — is needed here; every other product is discarded. The same function is then called again for real at config.ts:167 to build the emitted record. Reading it as "read the roster" hides that this line is a registry warm-up. Dedupe: rounds1234-index.md has "Delete AgentRosterSnapshot.agents" (round 1, a field on the snapshot) and "Collapse the identity-only getAgents/getVisibleAgents seam" (round 1 refuted) — neither touches this call site; grepped the four survey docs for `readCliAgentRoster` and `configureAgentRoster` — no hits.

**Proposal**

Replace config.ts:98 with the explicit prerequisite `await loadAgents({ includeRemote: false });` (already imported in this package's neighbours; `@agent/index` is imported at config.ts:3-6). The line then says what it does, one workspace config-file read and one discarded snapshot disappear from every `texra config agents` invocation, and the honest read at :167 remains the single roster reader.

**What we give up**

Nothing observable. If a future `loadAgents` option divergence matters, the explicit call is the place it becomes visible rather than being inherited from an unrelated reader.

**Verifier corrections — these override the evidence and proposal above**

1. netLoc is +1, not 0. `loadAgents` has to join the multi-line named-import block at config.ts:3-6, which adds a line; line 98 is a swap. The finding's "0" ignores the import.

2. The finding never mentions the host @agent import ratchet, which is the obvious objection to adding an `@agent/index` symbol from a host. It is safe, but for a reason worth stating: config/ratchets/host-agent-import-baseline.json is set-based over _distinct specifiers_ ("The ratchet is set-based: a live specifier absent from a package's list is a new edge and fails"), and `"cli"` already lists `@agent/index`. Adding a symbol to an already-listed specifier widens nothing.

3. Missed prior art: docs/proposals/2026-08-03-ssot-consolidation-plan.md §A6 ("CLI config: one parse, one table, no `.catch`") already flags `loadWorkspaceCliConfig` re-reading `.texra/config.json` "three times per process (`cliContext.ts:390`, `chatDefaults.ts:78`, `agentRoster.ts:37`)". Not a refutation (different fix, still unimplemented — cliConfig.ts:352-363 has no memo), but it means "one workspace config-file read disappears" is a benefit A6 would also deliver. The durable value of this finding is the honest call site, not the saved I/O.

4. The waste is smaller than the framing implies. `AgentRosterSnapshot.agents` no longer exists at HEAD — `snapshot()` (AgentRosterController.ts:209-231) returns selection/effectiveSelection/defaultTeamId/missingTeamId/unresolvedNames only, so the round-1 "Delete AgentRosterSnapshot.agents" item already shipped and the discarded snapshot does NOT double-resolve `getVisibleAgents` across both categories any more. What is actually wasted: two `getEffectiveSelection()` state reads, one unresolved-name walk, one `byCategory` getEnabledAgentKeys walk, one `getWorkspacePath()`, and one config-file read + parse + per-field Zod validation.

5. The proposal should cite the in-package precedent rather than "already imported in this package's neighbours": packages/cli/src/chat/tui/forms/AgentRosterForm.tsx:115-118 does exactly `await loadAgents({ includeRemote: false })` followed by `createWorkspaceAgentRosterController()`. There are 8 `loadAgents({ includeRemote: false })` call sites in packages/cli/src; this is the house idiom.

6. Unstated test consequence, which I verified rather than assumed: src/test-kernel/cli/ConfigCommand.vitest.ts mocks `@cli/runtime/agentRoster` wholesale (:38-41) while spreading the real `@agent/index` (:25-36), so today the `configureAgentRoster` path never reaches `loadAgents`. After the change it calls the real one with `initLocalCliPlatform` mocked to a no-op. It still passes (7/7) because `loadAgents`' cache/in-flight guard at agentRegistry.ts:107-114 short-circuits, but the finding claimed "nothing observable" without checking this.

<details><summary>Verifier reasoning</summary>

The core claim is factually correct on every line I re-read, and the fix is a one-line honesty change with no behavior delta. It is not a defect in the wrong-output sense, so it has to earn its place as an amend: it does, narrowly. `await readCliAgentRoster();` with a discarded result is a genuinely misleading call site — it reads as "load the roster record" when the only thing it contributes is registry warm-up, and the real read happens 69 lines later at :167. Replacing it with the call the code actually depends on makes the prerequisite explicit and matches the idiom used at 8 other CLI sites including AgentRosterForm.tsx:115. The incidental win (dropping one `.texra/config.json` read + parse + Zod pass and one pure snapshot per `texra config agents`) is real but small and partly overlaps the unimplemented §A6 memoization plan, so I would not sell it on performance. I checked the three things that would have killed it: a persistence side effect inside `snapshot()` (none — pure reads, `repairLegacySelection` is gone from HEAD), a ratchet widening (none — set-based over specifiers, `@agent/index` already listed for cli), and the mocked test suite (applied the patch, 7/7 pass, reverted clean). At +1 LoC this is at the thin end of what is worth a PR; it is worth doing only if batched with other CLI-command cleanups, never as a standalone PR.

</details>

### CLI model surface: three exported names for one 'no models available' string, and a guard the resolver it calls already enforces

- **Slice**: b6 · **Kind**: consolidate · **Risk**: low · **Net**: -18 LoC (proposer claimed -14; verifier figure governs)
- **Files**: `packages/cli/src/runtime/modelAccess.ts`, `packages/cli/src/runtime/enabledModels.ts`, `packages/cli/src/runtime/cliConfig.ts`, `src/test-kernel/cli/ModelAccess.vitest.ts`

**Evidence**

(a) The alias chain. modelAccess.ts:84 defines `NO_RUNNABLE_MODEL_ACCESS_COPY`. :111-115 `formatCliNoRunnableModelsMessage` composes it with the recovery line. :164-166 `modelAccessLaunchBlockDescription()` is a zero-argument function whose entire body is `return NO_RUNNABLE_MODEL_ACCESS_COPY;`. :168-172 `emptyModelListMessage(options)` is an exact identity forward to `formatCliNoRunnableModelsMessage(options)` — same parameter type, same return, no added logic.

Grepped every consumer (`grep -rn 'emptyModelListMessage|modelAccessLaunchBlockDescription|formatCliNoRunnableModelsMessage' packages src`, excluding dist): `emptyModelListMessage` has ONE production caller (chat/tui/forms/ModelListForm.tsx:105) plus ModelAccess.vitest.ts:437. `modelAccessLaunchBlockDescription` has ONE production caller (orchestration.ts:134) plus ModelAccess.vitest.ts:409. `formatCliNoRunnableModelsMessage` has ZERO direct production callers — it is only reachable through the alias, plus ModelAccess.vitest.ts:410/430. Three exports, two production call sites, one string.

(b) The duplicated guard. enabledModels.ts:69-74 reads `const model = resolveKnownCliModelId(modelInput); if (!model || !isCliSupportedModelId(model)) throw …`. But `resolveKnownCliModelId` (cliConfig.ts:76-100) returns only two kinds of value: `trimmed` when `isCliSupportedModelId(trimmed)` is already true (:79), or an element of `knownCliModelIds()` (:82), which is defined at :58-60 as `Object.keys(MODEL_CONFIGS).filter(isCliSupportedModelId)`. Every non-undefined return therefore satisfies `isCliSupportedModelId` by construction, so the second half of the caller's guard is statically unreachable. The other three call sites of the resolver get this right with a single `if (!resolved)`: runModel.ts:21-27, modelAccess.ts:202-204, modelAccess.ts:305-306.

Dedupe: grepped all five symbol names against rounds1234-index.md and the four docs/proposals survey files — no hit. Round 1's "Collapse modelOptionsByCategory" and round 3's "Availability (computeModelOptions) and dispatch (ModelFactory) restate the same route precedence — KEEP" are different subjects; the KEEP ruling is about route precedence, not about these copy helpers.

**Proposal**

Point ModelListForm.tsx:105 at `formatCliNoRunnableModelsMessage` and delete `emptyModelListMessage`; export `NO_RUNNABLE_MODEL_ACCESS_COPY` and let orchestration.ts:134 read it directly, deleting `modelAccessLaunchBlockDescription`. Drop the two now-orphan assertions in ModelAccess.vitest.ts:409/437 (the surviving :410 case still pins the composed string). Separately, drop `|| !isCliSupportedModelId(model)` from enabledModels.ts:70 so the resolver is the single owner of "is this a CLI model id". Both are in the same CLI model-access surface; keep them as one batch and do not expand into a general sweep of modelAccess.ts.

**What we give up**

The two deleted names read as intention-revealing at their call sites (`emptyModelListMessage` in a list form, `modelAccessLaunchBlockDescription` in a launcher). After the change, the launcher imports a SCREAMING_CASE constant instead of a function — slightly less symmetric with the neighbouring `formatCliModelAccessSummary` call. Dropping the enabledModels guard means a future change to `resolveKnownCliModelId` that widened its return set would no longer be caught here.

**Verifier corrections — these override the evidence and proposal above**

1. "The other three call sites of the resolver get this right with a single `if (!resolved)`" — there are FOUR other call sites, not three. The missed one is chatDefaults.ts:163, `return { model: resolveKnownCliModelId(mostRecent.record.model) };`, which applies no guard at all and propagates `undefined`. Doesn't change the verdict (that site relies on the same by-construction invariant), but the "three" count is wrong.
2. Test-edit scope is understated. ModelAccess.vitest.ts:409 is one line inside the it-block at :408-416 whose title is "formats no-runnable model reasons for launch and model picker views" — deleting the line leaves a title that now over-claims; retitle it. :437 is not a loose assertion: it is the entire 3-line it-block "formats empty model picker messages with caller-owned recovery actions" (:436-440), which goes away wholesale. Two names also drop from the import list (:4 emptyModelListMessage, :11 modelAccessLaunchBlockDescription).
3. Unmentioned coverage that strengthens the case: src/test-kernel/cli/Orchestration.vitest.ts:843 already asserts `view.items[0]?.description === 'No models are available'` end-to-end through buildCliOrchestrationItems, so deleting the :409 assertion loses no coverage of the launcher path at all.
4. Unmentioned required edit: config/ratchets/knip-baseline.json:880-885 lists `formatCliNoRunnableModelsMessage` as `production-dead`. Pointing ModelListForm.tsx:105 at it makes it live, so that row goes stale. scripts/check-dead-code-ratchet.mjs:130-139 only PRINTS resolved entries ("fixed!") and does not fail, so this is not a gate break — but the row should be deleted in the same PR to shrink the baseline.
5. Unmentioned line win: dropping the guard also orphans the `isCliSupportedModelId` import at enabledModels.ts:15 (grep confirms :70 is its only use in that file), so that import line goes too. `if (!model || !isCliSupportedModelId(model)) {` → `if (!model) {` is itself line-neutral.
6. Minor framing: the "give up" note says the launcher would import "a SCREAMING_CASE constant instead of a function". Accurate, but orchestration.ts:134 already binds it to a local (`const description = ...`), so the call site reads identically after the change — the asymmetry with the neighbouring formatter call is one import line, not a call-site regression.

<details><summary>Verifier reasoning</summary>

Both halves are verified true at HEAD by direct re-read, and neither is defended by a comment, a dated ruling, a prior round, or a frozen surface. Part (a) is a genuine three-names-one-string alias chain: an identity forward with a single caller and a zero-arg constant getter with a single caller, with the composer they wrap having no direct production caller at all — a fact the knip baseline independently records. Part (b) is a statically unreachable predicate that duplicates an invariant the resolver already establishes on all four of its return paths, and its removal leaves the resolver as the single owner of "is this a CLI model id", consistent with how the other call sites use it. Both are behavior-preserving (user-visible copy byte-identical), confined to one CLI surface, touch two production call sites plus one test file, and cross no wire contract, settings key, or persisted format. The finding's own scoping discipline (batch the two, do not expand into a general modelAccess.ts sweep) keeps it out of the §13 churn pattern. Corrections are all incidental: a miscounted call-site set, an understated test-block deletion, one unmentioned knip-baseline row, and one unmentioned orphan import.

</details>

### bashCompletion emits a `*)` fallback that bash can never reach, and it disagrees with the root case block emitted three lines above it

- **Slice**: b6 · **Kind**: delete · **Risk**: low · **Net**: -3 LoC (proposer claimed -5; verifier figure governs)
- **Files**: `packages/cli/src/runtime/completionBash.ts`, `packages/cli/src/runtime/completionZsh.ts`

**Evidence**

completionBash.ts:255-258 emits `case "$path" in` followed by `commands.map(commandCaseBlock)` and then `*) subcommands='${root?.subcommands.join(' ') ?? ''}'; flags='' ;;`.

The `*)` arm is unreachable for two independent reasons:

1. `commands` always contains the root: `collectCommands` (completionCommandTree.ts:160-186) returns `[current, ...children.flat()]` starting from `path = []`, so the root is the FIRST element. `commandCaseBlock` (completionBash.ts:179-184) keys it with `quote([commandKey([])])` = `quote([''])`. I verified with the installed shell-quote that `quote([''])` returns `''`, so the emitted first arm is `'') subcommands=…; flags=… ;;`, which bash matches against an empty `$path`.
2. `_texra_completion_path` (:223-240) initializes `path=""` and only ever assigns `path="$next"` inside `case " ${allCommandPaths.join(' ')} " in *" $next "*)` — i.e. `$path` is always either `""` or a member of `allCommandPaths`, and every member has its own case arm.

So the dead arm is also a drifted duplicate: it sets `flags=''` where the live `''` arm sets the root's real flag tokens. If it ever did run, top-level `--`-prefixed completion would silently return nothing. Deleting it also frees `const root = commands.find(…)` at :187, whose only reader is that arm.

zshCompletion gets the same structure right and shows the intended shape: :67-68 filters `command.path.length > 0` out of the case list precisely so `*)` (:98) owns the root. bash includes the root in the list AND keeps the fallback.

Dedupe: grepped `bashCompletion`, `commandCaseBlock`, `_texra_completion_path`, `completionBash` against rounds1234-index.md and the four survey docs. Round 3's only completion item is "Two citty command-tree walkers that disagree about lazily-resolved subcommands", which is already fixed (commandMeta/commandArgs/commandSubcommands are shared) and is a different symbol.

**Proposal**

Delete the `*)` arm at completionBash.ts:257 and the now-unread `const root` at :187. Completion.vitest.ts already runs the generated script through real `bash` probes (spawnSync at :41), so the existing suite verifies the root-level completion path unchanged; no new test needed.

**What we give up**

Nothing behavioral. The only loss is a defensive arm for a `$path` value the generator cannot produce; if a future change ever emits a command list without the root, bash's `case` would fall through with `subcommands`/`flags` unset instead of empty — same empty COMPREPLY.

**Verifier corrections — these override the evidence and proposal above**

1. LoC IS WRONG. Claimed -5; actual is -3. The deletion is exactly two production lines (packages/cli/src/runtime/completionBash.ts:187 `const root = commands.find(...)` and :257 the `*)` arm) plus one line of committed snapshot (src/test-kernel/cli/**snapshots**/Completion.vitest.ts.snap:146). No import drops with `root` (it uses `commands.find`, not a named import), so there is no extra saving.

2. TEST-COVERAGE CLAIM IS WRONG, AND IT MATTERS FOR IMPLEMENTATION. "Completion.vitest.ts already runs the generated script through real bash probes (spawnSync at :41), so the existing suite verifies the root-level completion path unchanged" is false. The six probes set COMP_WORDS at Completion.vitest.ts:192, :196, :200, :204, :254, :258 — `(texra run p)`, `(texra agents run r)`, `(texra chat --agent l)`, `(texra agents show p)`, `(texra run polish --input "paper")`, `(texra --cwd "paper")`. None of them produces an empty `$path` with a `-`-prefixed `$cur`, so no probe exercises the root flag list at all. What actually pins this change is the `toMatchSnapshot` test at :59-62 plus snapshot line :146, which MUST be regenerated (`vitest -u`) or the PR fails. An implementer following the finding's framing would skip the snapshot update and ship a red test. (Also trivial: the spawnSync call spans :40-41, not :41.)

3. completionZsh.ts DOES NOT BELONG IN Paths. Nothing changes in that file; it is cited only as the contrasting-correct shape. Listing it as a path implies an edit that must not happen — in particular `const root` at completionZsh.ts:65 is still live, feeding `rootSpecs` at :83-86 and the `*)` arm at :98, which in zsh IS reachable because :68 filters `command.path.length > 0` out of the case list. Deleting zsh's `root` by analogy would break root-level zsh completion.

4. LINE RANGE OFF BY ONE. `collectCommands` spans completionCommandTree.ts:160-185 (body returns at :184, brace at :185), not :160-186.

5. UNDERSTATED, NOT WRONG: the finding says only that `flags=''` disagrees. The `subcommands` halves also drift structurally — the `*)` arm hardcodes the root's subcommand list at generation time via `root?.subcommands.join(' ') ?? ''`, i.e. it is a second, hand-maintained copy of what `commandCaseBlock` already emits for the root, which is what let the `flags` half rot in the first place. That strengthens the case; nothing about it changes the fix.

<details><summary>Verifier reasoning</summary>

The core claim reproduces under independent verification by three separate routes (shell-quote behavior, the committed snapshot text, and live bash execution), the arm is provably unreachable given that collectCommands unconditionally prepends the root, and the arm is a drifted duplicate whose `flags=''` half would return nothing for top-level flag completion if it ever ran. Nothing defends it: no comment, no ruling, no ratchet, no external contract, no prior survey round. The removal is behavior-preserving — `flags` and `subcommands` are `local` in `_texra`, so a hypothetical unmatched `$path` yields the same empty COMPREPLY with the arm gone as with `flags=''` today. Two factual defects in the finding are worth flagging but do not kill it: the LoC is inflated from -3 to -5, and the stated verification path (bash probes) does not actually cover the root case — the snapshot test does, and it must be regenerated. Judged as a delete finding the profit is small; judged on its merits it is clean dead code with a latent inconsistency baked in, at essentially zero risk.

</details>

### Lifecycle-handler failures are suppressed in every CLI command, against the intent stated in their own comment

- **Slice**: b6 · **Kind**: defect · **Risk**: low · **Net**: 4 LoC
- **Files**: `packages/cli/src/runtime/initPlatform.ts`, `packages/cli/src/runtime/supabaseAuth.ts`, `src/test-kernel/cli/CliInitPlatform.vitest.ts`

**Evidence**

NARROWED 2026-08-27 after maintainer review. The original finding claimed all platform-init logging is wrongly suppressed. That is REFUTED: quietLogs:true at every call site is deliberate TUI noise suppression, and initPlatform.ts:71-72 records the convention explicitly - "Malformed project config is actionable degradation, not routine progress noise, so this deliberately bypasses quietLogs" - with showPersistentConfigWarning (:73-75) writing straight to stderr as the precedent for what SHOULD bypass.

The residue is one site whose own comment states an intent the mechanism defeats. initPlatform.ts:255-265 wires the lifecycle host onError with the comment "Same severity and wording as the extension/desktop hosts: a shutdown handler failure is an error everywhere, not a warning in one host" - then routes it through logAt(), which returns early under quietPlatformLogs. Since grep shows zero quietLogs:false call sites across 46, that error is unreachable in every CLI command, so the stated cross-host parity does not hold. By the file own taxonomy a shutdown-handler failure is actionable degradation, not progress noise.

The model-list refresh failure at :298-309 is deliberately NOT included: a failed refresh is recoverable and reconciles on the next startup, which is closer to routine noise.

**Proposal**

Route the lifecycle onError through the same stderr bypass showPersistentConfigWarning uses, so it honours the parity its comment claims. Roughly +4 lines (a small named writer beside the existing one, or a direct writeTextStderr call). Leave every other logAt site alone - they are the routine progress noise quietLogs exists to suppress.

**What we give up**

CLI shutdown-handler failures become visible on stderr where today they are silent. That is the point; if a maintainer prefers silence here, the fix is to correct the comment instead, since comment and mechanism currently disagree either way.

**Verifier corrections — these override the evidence and proposal above**

Rewritten after maintainer review. The original sweeping framing (all platform-init logging wrongly suppressed, 32 call sites, Supabase auth log to /dev/null) is refuted - quietLogs is deliberate and documented at initPlatform.ts:71-72. Only the lifecycle-onError site survives, and it survives on the strength of its own comment rather than on a general silent-degradation argument. Net moves from 0 to +4: this is a fix that adds lines, not a deletion.

<details><summary>Verifier reasoning</summary>

The load-bearing claim is a census claim, and the census holds: every one of the 37 production init paths hard-codes `quietLogs: true`, and `quietLogs: false` exists nowhere outside four test files. That makes `logAt`'s body unreachable in production, which makes three error-level writers unreachable output: the lifecycle drain's `onError`, the model-refresh catch, and — through `cliPlatformLog` -> `deferredAuthLog` -> `createHostAuthCoordinator` — the whole SupabaseSession log. That is a verifiable configuration-dead branch carrying error reporting, and the repo's own twice-stated policy (initPlatform.ts:71-72 and cliPresentationHost.ts:89-92) says actionable failures bypass the quiet gate, so the code's self-explanation does not defend it; it argues against it. My initial suspicion of a misread (the shared `fixtures/cliContext.ts` defaults `quietLogs: false`) dissolved once I found the file-local helper at :187-198 defaulting to true. What does not survive intact is the finding's severity and its cost. The CLI's user-facing error channel is ungated and already loud; the info-level model-refresh lines are correctly quiet; auth failure has a designed `auth status` classification; and the null output channel that the finding treats as incidental is in fact protecting stdout from `console.info` fallback. The remedy is also not a delete: a bare unconditional `writeTextStderr` reproduces a pattern round 3 already recorded as a defect (raw stderr under Ink) and would dirty `texra doctor`, so the real change is a per-host carve-out plus two test edits. Real defect, narrower than advertised, roughly LoC-neutral.

</details>

### Trace-viewer export reports 'not bundled in this CLI install, rebuild the CLI' for any read failure — the two probes catch every error instead of only file-not-found

- **Slice**: b6 · **Kind**: amend · **Risk**: low · **Net**: 14 LoC (proposer claimed 6; verifier figure governs)
- **Files**: `packages/cli/src/runtime/history.ts`, `packages/cli/src/commands/history.ts`

**Evidence**

history.ts:293-302 `readCliHistoryStandaloneTemplate` ends with `return readFile(templatePath, 'utf8').catch(() => null);` — a bare catch-all. history.ts:322-337 `stageCliHistoryTraceViewerAssets` does the same with `await stat(assetsSrc).then((info) => info.isDirectory()).catch(() => false)` and returns `'missing'`.

Both carry a doc comment that scopes the null/'missing' answer to exactly one cause: ":288-291 \"Returns `null` (without throwing) when the CLI install doesn't have the bundled template — e.g. a dev checkout where `packages/trace-viewer` hasn't been built\"" and ":318-320 \"Returns `'missing'` … when the CLI install doesn't have the bundled assets — e.g. a dev checkout where `copy:resources` hasn't run\". Defeating that comment explicitly: the catch establishes no such thing. EACCES on the resources directory, EISDIR, EMFILE, or any transient I/O error produces the identical answer, and the caller then prints a categorical, wrong remedy — commands/history.ts:190-197 writes \"The bundled trace-viewer standalone template was not found in this CLI install. Rebuild the CLI (`npm run texra-local:build`) …\" and returns CliExitCode.Usage; :169-176 writes the parallel \"the bundled trace-viewer assets were not found in this CLI install\". A user with a permissions problem is sent to rebuild, and the real cause never reaches them.

The repo already owns the correct predicate and applies it in neighbouring CLI runtime files: cliContext.ts:4/339 uses `isFileNotFoundError`/`isNotADirectoryError` around `stat`, and initConfig.ts:105-112 uses it with a comment naming this exact hazard — \"Anything else (EACCES, a transient I/O error, ...) must not be treated as 'file absent'\". history.ts imports no error predicate at all.

Dedupe: grepped `readCliHistoryStandaloneTemplate`, `stageCliHistoryTraceViewerAssets`, `traceViewerShared`, `isFileNotFoundError` against rounds1234-index.md and the four survey docs. Round 4B shipped the same defect CLASS at a different site ("Approval preview readFileWithFallback swallows all read errors without the FNF predicate") — a distinct symbol in a distinct file; these two sites were not covered and are still open.

**Proposal**

Narrow both catches with `isFileNotFoundError` (import from `@common/errors`, as cliContext.ts already does in this package): return `null` / `'missing'` only for ENOENT, and rethrow anything else so `texra history export`'s error boundary reports the real cause. Leave the ENOENT wording and exit code exactly as they are — the dev-checkout case is the common one and its message is correct. No new test: the existing not-found path is unchanged, and per the testing budget a rethrow of an unmodelled error does not earn a regression test.

**What we give up**

`texra history export --format html` can now fail with an I/O error message plus a non-zero crash exit code instead of the tidy Usage exit it gives today, on a machine where the resources directory is present but unreadable. That is the intended trade: an honest failure over a confident wrong remedy.

**Verifier corrections — these override the evidence and proposal above**

1. "Both carry a doc comment that scopes the null/'missing' answer to exactly one cause" overstates slightly: both comments read "when the CLI install doesn't have the bundled template — e.g. a dev checkout where…", so the dev checkout is an example of one condition, not the sole enumerated cause. The mismatch claim survives (the stated condition is still narrower than the catch), but "exactly one cause" is not what the comment says.
2. The proposal's predicate is too narrow. Both sites should gate on `isFileNotFoundError(error) || isNotADirectoryError(error)`, not ENOENT alone — the repo precedent the finding itself cites (cliContext.ts:339) uses both, and BaseFS.statIfExists does the same. ENOTDIR here (a file sitting where `resources/traceViewer` should be, a truncated install) is genuinely a "this install lacks the bundle" shape; ENOENT-only would turn it into a crash, which is a behavior regression the finding did not price.
3. A raw rethrow lands on the CLI crash boundary, which appends "This looks like a bug — please report it at <bugs.url>" (cliContext.ts:246-257, `formatCrashReportLine` returns undefined only for `CliUsageError`). For an EACCES on the user's resources directory that is a second wrong remedy. Follow cliContext.ts:338-347 instead: throw `new CliUsageError(\`history export: cannot read ${templatePath}: ${toErrorMessage(error)}\`)`, which keeps the clean exit-2 path, names the real cause, and suppresses the bug-report prompt. This also makes the "give up" paragraph unnecessary — the tidy Usage exit is retained, only the wording changes.
4. Unstated but load-bearing for cost: existing tests already cover both sites and both pass unchanged under the narrowed predicate. src/test-kernel/cli/History.vitest.ts:1400-1412 ("reports 'missing' … when the bundled trace-viewer assets are absent") and :1470-1480 ("returns null instead of throwing when the default template is absent") both point at an empty temp dir, so the probe sees ENOENT. The "no new test" conclusion is right, but for this reason rather than the one given.
5. The `stat` probe has a second non-error miss path the finding does not mention: `info.isDirectory() === false` already returns 'missing' when a plain file occupies the path. That branch is correct and must be preserved by the amend.
6. Claimed 6 net LoC is low. Two try/catch conversions with a two-predicate guard and a CliUsageError wrap, plus one import line and the two doc comments corrected to state the narrowed contract, lands near +14.

<details><summary>Verifier reasoning</summary>

Read both target files directly rather than trusting the evidence block. history.ts:293-302 and :322-337 are exactly as quoted, and their doc comments do promise a cause the catches do not establish, so the self-explaining-code kill fails on its own terms. The caller's wording and CliExitCode.Usage at commands/history.ts:169-176 and :190-197 confirm the wrong-remedy consequence is real and user-visible, which is what makes this a defect rather than a style preference.
