  The repo's own type-checker already agrees: `groupStartTime` at :35-37 returns `group.startTime` with declared return type `number` and compiles.

Second collapse: `compareGroups`/`compareRootGroups` both call `compareBySeqNo(a, b, () => undefined, …)`. With `seqNoOf` always undefined, compareBySeqNo (src/shared/streams/streamOrdering.ts:29-40) reduces to `fallbackTimeOf(a) - fallbackTimeOf(b)`, so both are literally `a.startTime - b.startTime`.

The defending comments must be defeated explicitly, and they are: ":29 Full-rebuild fallback: rows missing a timestamp sort last" and ":39 Full-rebuild fallback: root groups missing a start time sort last" describe a case the schemas and the TS types both forbid. Two more dead guards ride along: `m.timestamp ?? 0` (:309) and `t.group.startTime ?? 0` (:315).

Dedupe: `rowTimeForRebuild`, `compareRowsForRebuild`, `compareRootGroups`, `ForRebuild` — zero hits across the rounds-1-4 index and all three survey docs.

**Proposal**

Collapse :24-58 to three functions:
`function rowTime(row: TranscriptRow): number { return row.timestamp; }`
`function compareRows(a, b) { return compareBySeqNo(a, b, (row) => row.seqNo, rowTime); }`
`function compareGroups(a, b) { return a.startTime - b.startTime; }`
Then retarget the three call sites — `rows.toSorted(compareRowsForRebuild)` at :259 and :452, and `.sort(compareRootGroups)` at :300 — onto `compareRows` / `compareGroups`, and drop the two dead `??` arms at :309 and :315. Delete the two stale "sort last" comments rather than reword them; the honest replacement is one line on `compareRows` saying seqNo wins when both rows have a usable one, timestamp otherwise.

Keep the `seqNo` half of `compareBySeqNo` untouched for rows — `TranscriptRowBase.seqNo` really is optional (:55) and locally-appended CLI rows exercise it.

Risk is medium only because this is the transcript sort in a hot render path: the change is provably behaviour-preserving, so verify by reasoning plus the existing TaskGroupList/TranscriptIndex suites, not by adding an ordering test.

**What we give up**

Give up if any producer of `TranscriptRow` or `TaskGroup` outside the two I traced constructs a row with `timestamp`/`startTime` cast in (an `as TranscriptRow` on a partial literal, or a hand-built object in a host adapter). A single such site restores the distinction and the two families must stay.

**Verifier corrections — these override the evidence and proposal above**

1. The "type-checker already agrees" argument at the end of the evidence is not evidence. TypeScript accepts `x ?? y` on a non-optional `number` without complaint (`@typescript-eslint/no-unnecessary-condition` is what would flag it, and it is not on here). That `groupStartTime` compiles proves `startTime` is non-optional; it does NOT prove the compiler flagged the dead arms. The real proof is the type declarations plus the exhaustive producer trace — which holds on its own.

2. The finding traced only two `TranscriptRow` producers and no `TaskGroup` producer at all. The load-bearing one it missed is `src/shared/streams/taskGroupProjection.ts`, which has two group-creation sites (:86-95 and :107-119) — including the GROUP_END-for-an-unseen-group path that builds a group from a deliberately PARTIAL `GroupLogPayloadSchema`. Both set `startTime: entry.timestamp` unconditionally, so the claim survives, but this was the finding's own stated give-up condition and it was never checked.

3. Provenance is missing and it matters: the family was correct when written. f6f127ad8a (#10717, "order transcript by wire seqNo with shared comparator") added it against `LogMessageData.timestamp?: number`; 6b988d219b ("one shared row model so the CLI renders what the webview does") made the field required and left the dead arms and their comments behind. Say this in the PR — it converts "someone wrote a pointless guard" into "a migration left residue", which is both truer and reviewer-proof.

4. The retarget list is incomplete. Beyond the three call sites (:259, :300, :452), `compareRowsForRebuild` is named in two doc comments that must be reworded: the `rebuildTree` comment at :256-258 ("Sort rows by wire append sequence… Rows without a usable sequence (archived/compat) fall back to timestamp") and `rebuildRowArrays`'s doc at :444-446 ("the same `compareRowsForRebuild` fallback `rebuildTree` uses"). Both are zero-net-line edits, but missing them leaves dangling symbol references.

5. Collapsing `compareGroups` to `a.startTime - b.startTime` is the one part not purely mechanical. #10717's own commit body says it deliberately "reserve[d] seqNo ordering for the homogeneous message arrays until B-2 carries group sequence" — the `() => undefined` is a named placeholder for planned work, not an accident. It has sat unused for three months and `TaskGroupSchema` is a `z.strictObject` with no `seqNo`, so a group cannot gain one silently; but if you want the change to be 100% argument-free, keep `compareGroups` exactly as-is and delete only the four `ForRebuild`/`RootGroups` members. That variant is -18 instead of -22 and cannot be second-guessed.

6. Risk should be low, not medium. "Hot render path" is about blast radius if wrong, and the equivalence here is total: with both fields required at every producer and every schema, the two comparator families compute identical numbers for every reachable input. The existing TaskGroupListIndex.vitest.ts (719 lines) covers the ordering behavior; the finding is right that no new ordering test is warranted.

<details><summary>Verifier reasoning</summary>

Adversarially checked all seven kill conditions and the finding's own give-up condition, then went past both.

Dedupe: zero hits for `messageIndex`, `ForRebuild`, `compareRootGroups`, or `comparator` across the 318-line rounds-1-4 index and all four survey docs (the round4 pair lives in the scratchpad, not docs/proposals — the finding's grep path would have silently missed them; I checked the real location and it is still clean).

Ruling: `git log -L24,58` on the block returns exactly two commits, neither of which defends the missing-timestamp fallback. #10717's message defends the seqNo fallback only.

Self-explanation defeated by provenance, not just by assertion: the two "sort last" comments were accurate against `LogMessageData.timestamp?: number` and went stale in the row-model migration.

Reachability: `timestamp` is required on `TranscriptRowBase` (16 interfaces, 16 union members, verified by count), required on the wire (`z.number()`, no `.catch`), and set unconditionally at all three production producers. Zero `as TranscriptRow` casts exist outside tests. `startTime` is required on a `z.strictObject` and set unconditionally at both `taskGroupProjection` creation sites — including the partial-payload GROUP_END path that was the finding's stated escape hatch. `compareBySeqNo` provably degenerates to plain subtraction when `seqNoOf` is constantly undefined.

Cost: 35 lines in, ~13 out. The finding's -22 is arithmetically right for the aggressive variant; -18 for the variant that leaves `compareGroups` alone. I report -20 as the honest midpoint since the `compareGroups` collapse is a judgment call against a stated (if stale) future intent.

Nothing here touches the CLI NDJSON wire, persisted files, settings keys, the texra-action contract, or any ratchet.

</details>

### BackgroundTasksPanel still branches on a childStreamId and identity that #9705 made required, and its module doc claims process rows are not clickable while every row now renders as a link

- **Slice**: b11 · **Kind**: amend · **Risk**: low · **Net**: -16 LoC (proposer claimed -18; verifier figure governs)
- **Files**: `packages/extension/src/progressView/frontend/components/BackgroundTasksPanel.ts`, `src/shared/schemas/streamState.ts`

**Evidence**

`ActiveChildInfoSchema` (src/shared/schemas/streamState.ts:26-60) declares `childStreamId: z.string()` (:29) and `identity: RunIdentitySchema` (:31) — both required — and its header comment (:21-24) states the invariant outright: "Every child owns a stream tab (`childStreamId` always present) and carries its parsed `identity` verbatim; renderers key icons and clickability on `identity.kind`". It reaches the view via `subagents: z.array(ActiveChildInfoSchema).prefault([])` (:147) with no `.catch`, so a row missing either field fails the parse rather than reaching a renderer. `git show fb47d75bdc` confirms #9705 (2026-08-04) is what promoted both fields out of the old discriminated union.

BackgroundTasksPanel still carries the pre-#9705 shape:

- :442-448 — `const childStreamId = child.childStreamId;` then `childStreamId ? … : undefined` twice, for `description` and `phaseLabel`.
- :466-480 — `@click` and `@keydown` each bound as `childStreamId !== undefined ? handler : nothing`, ~10 lines of ternary for a branch that cannot be taken.
- :452-454 — `child.identity ? runIdentityDisplayName(child.identity) : child.agentName`; the `agentName` fallback is unreachable.
- :546-557 `getTaskIcon` — `case undefined:` with the comment "legacy emitters without an identity get the neutral agent icon", describing a row the schema rejects.
- :281, :459, :601-602 — `child.identity?.kind` optional chaining on a required field.

The drifted comment pair is the reader-visible half. The module doc (:6-9) says "Each subagent row is clickable to navigate to its stream tab … Processes don't have their own tab so they are not clickable", while the inline comment at :440-441 says the opposite ("Every roster row owns a stream tab, so every row is navigable") — and the markup at :461-465 applies `task-name--clickable`, `role="link"` and `tabindex="0"` unconditionally, with a "Go to {name}" tooltip at :483. So a process row today is a focusable, underlined, tooltipped link, which the module doc says it is not.

Dedupe: `renderTaskItem`, `getTaskIcon`, `childStreamId` — zero hits in the rounds-1-4 index and the three survey docs. BackgroundTasksPanel appears in round 2 only as _evidence_ for the `resumeOutcome` finding, which is policy-protected and which this proposal does not touch (it reads `status`, `lastQuestionPreview`, `lastActivityIso` and stays untouched here).

**Proposal**

Two coupled edits, both mechanical:

1. Drop the dead optionality. `const childStreamId = child.childStreamId` is a `string`: inline the two `description`/`phaseLabel` reads (:443-448), bind `@click=${() => this.navigateToStream(childStreamId)}` and the keydown handler directly (:466-480), replace the displayName ternary with `runIdentityDisplayName(child.identity)` (:452-454), delete `case undefined:` and its comment from `getTaskIcon` (:552-556 — the switch then covers `process`/`agent`/`multiAgentWorkflow` exhaustively), and drop the `?.` on `child.identity` at :281, :459, :601-602.
2. Fix the module doc (:6-9) to state what the code does — every roster row owns a tab and every row navigates, process rows included — rather than leaving the two comments contradicting each other. Do not "fix" it the other way by re-adding a process guard: #9705 deliberately gave processes a stream tab, and ProcessStreamContent (in this same slice) exists to render it.

This is `amend` rather than `delete` because the visible half is a stale claim about behaviour, not just dead branches; the LoC saving is the by-product.

**What we give up**

Give up on step 1 if any host builds an `ActiveChildInfo` by hand and casts it (bypassing the Zod parse) with either field omitted — check the roster emitters in src/agent/runtime before deleting the branches. Step 2 (the doc correction) stands regardless.

**Verifier corrections — these override the evidence and proposal above**

1. Optional-chaining sites are :281, :459, :546 and :602 — the finding lists ":281, :459, :601-602". :546 is the `switch (child.identity?.kind)` head itself, which must lose its `?.` in the same edit as `case undefined:` (deleting the case without dropping the `?.` leaves a non-exhaustive switch and a TS error); :601-602 is the two-line `subagentStatusStillInFlight` expression whose `?.` sits on :602.
2. "It reaches the view via `subagents: ... .prefault([])` (:147) with no `.catch`, so a row missing either field fails the parse rather than reaching a renderer" is right in effect but wrong about where: the webview does NOT parse. `packages/extension/src/progressView/frontend/slices/streamStateMerge.ts` merges `StreamMetadata` unparsed; the `StreamMetadataSchema.parse` is on the producing side at `src/shared/streams/streamMetadata.ts:33`. The guarantee is backend parse + TypeScript type, not a frontend boundary parse. This does not weaken the finding (both producers are typed and verified), but the PR should not claim the frontend re-validates.
3. Give-up condition is discharged, not open: the only two row producers are `src/agent/runtime/executionRegistry.ts:818-837` (`getActiveChildren`, sets `identity` and `childStreamId` unconditionally from the handle) and `src/controllers/session/SessionFactApplier.ts:790` (retained rows are `{ ...child, finishedAt }` spreads). `packages/trace-viewer/src/replayTrace.ts:224` emits `subagents: []`. No host hand-builds and casts an `ActiveChildInfo`.
4. No test changes needed: `src/test-kernel/progressView/BackgroundTasksPanel.vitest.ts:38-50` builds fixtures with both fields always set and pins nothing on the dead branches, so this is a zero-test-delta PR (matches the "behavior-preserving refactor adds none" bar).
5. The claim "process rows have no tab" is stale for a second, checkable reason worth citing in the PR: `src/tools/bash.ts:515-545` registers the execution with `streamId: childStreamId` and `identity: { kind: 'process', tool: 'bash' }`, and `packages/extension/src/progressView/frontend/components/ProcessStreamContent.ts` is the tab body. The panel's own :279-284 filter (finished process rows dropped because their tabs are ephemeral) is the correct nuance to preserve in the rewritten doc — say live process rows navigate, finished ones are not listed.
6. -18 is slightly optimistic after prettier re-wrap at 80 columns (the collapsed `phaseLabel` call and the `@keydown` arrow both re-wrap onto multiple lines). Honest net is about -16.

<details><summary>Verifier reasoning</summary>

Both halves check out against HEAD. The schema half is unambiguous: `ActiveChildInfoSchema` declares `childStreamId: z.string()` and `identity: RunIdentitySchema` as required with a header comment stating the invariant, and #9705 is the commit that made them so — so every `childStreamId !== undefined` ternary, the `child.identity ? ... : child.agentName` fallback, and `case undefined:` in `getTaskIcon` are branches TypeScript already proves unreachable. I traced both producers (`executionRegistry.getActiveChildren`, `SessionFactApplier` retained-row spreads) plus the trace-viewer replay path and none can emit a row missing either field, which discharges the finding's own give-up condition. The comment half is the sharper defect: the module doc at :8-9 asserts process rows are not clickable while :461-465 applies `task-name--clickable`, `role="link"` and `tabindex="0"` to every row with a "Go to {name}" tooltip, and the inline comment 430 lines below says the opposite — a reader-visible contradiction where the doc, not the code, is wrong, since bash.ts does give a background process its own stream and ProcessStreamContent renders it. Dedupe is clean across the index and all three survey docs, no dated ruling protects the optionality (the only relevant ruling mandates its removal), no ratchet or wire contract is touched, and no test pins the dead branches. Cost is a real, modest negative with zero test delta.

### The welcome webview mints a crypto-random CSP script nonce for a page that contains no script

- **Slice**: b11 · **Kind**: delete · **Risk**: low · **Net**: -3 LoC (proposer claimed -4; verifier figure governs)
- **Files**: `packages/extension/src/frontend/ui/welcomeView.ts`

**Evidence**

`renderWelcomeHtml` (welcomeView.ts:27-135) emits a complete document: a `<style>` block (:45-105) and a body of headings, a list, and anchors (:107-133). There is no `<script>` element, no `src=`, and no inline event handler anywhere in the 100-line template — the interactive affordances are all `command:` and `https:` hrefs (:121-127).

Yet :33-34 computes `const nonce = nanoid();` (pulling the `nanoid` import at :1 in for this one use) and :43 spends it on `script-src 'nonce-${nonce}';`. Nothing in the document can ever match that source expression, so the directive is equivalent to inheriting `default-src 'none'`.

The comment at :33 ("CSP nonces must be unpredictable — nanoid is crypto-random") defends the _choice of generator_, not the existence of a nonce, so it does not shield the finding — it is answered by deleting the nonce it justifies.

Dedupe: `welcomeView` returns zero hits in the rounds-1-4 index and all three survey docs; the single `nonce` hit in round 3 is an unrelated test-migration note in the ProgressBackendStreamLifecycle finding.

**Proposal**

Delete :33-34 and the `nanoid` import at :1, and drop `script-src 'nonce-…';` from the CSP at :43, leaving `default-src 'none'; style-src 'unsafe-inline';`. The `style-src 'unsafe-inline'` must stay — the `<style>` block at :45 depends on it.

Leave `enableScripts: true` at :20 alone unless someone verifies against the VS Code webview API that `enableCommandUris` (:21) works without it; the `command:` links at :121-127 are the page's only real function and a wrong guess there breaks Open Folder and Try the Sample Project silently. Removing the nonce is strictly independent of that question: with or without `enableScripts`, a page with no script tag is unaffected.

**What we give up**

Give up if a future edit is already planned that adds interactivity to this page — then the nonce is a scaffold with a named consumer rather than dead surface. Also give up if the CSP string is asserted verbatim by a webview-security test that treats the nonce directive as the pattern other views must copy.

**Verifier corrections — these override the evidence and proposal above**

1. NET LoC IS -3, NOT -4. Deleted lines: :1 (nanoid import), :33 (comment), :34 (const). Line :43 is edited in place, not removed, and no blank line collapses (line :2 `import * as vscode` becomes the new first line with no surrounding gap change).

2. "Nothing in the document can ever match that source expression, so the directive is equivalent to inheriting `default-src 'none'`" is right in effect but slightly imprecise about the document. The DOM VS Code actually parses is not this exact string: the webview host prepends its own elements (the `_defaultStyles` block the page's `var(--vscode-*)` lookups depend on, and the API bootstrap when `enableScripts` is true) into `<head>` ahead of the CSP `<meta>`, so they are not governed by the policy in either configuration. Better framing: the change is a small hardening (nonce allowlist to no-script-at-all), not a provable no-op — which cuts in favor of the change, not against it.

3. The template is 99 lines (:36-134), not "100-line". Cosmetic.

4. The dedupe section undersells its own evidence: the history check is the stronger argument. The nonce was never scaffolding left by a removed script — it shipped in the webview's first commit (f6df5fda7d, #3081) against a body that already had zero script elements, and every version since has been script-free. That closes the "Give up" branch about planned interactivity as far as anything in the repo or its history shows.

5. Minor: the finding says the `style-src 'unsafe-inline'` is needed for "the `<style>` block at :45". True, and it is also needed for VS Code's injected `_defaultStyles` element if that one is subject to the policy — either way, keeping it is correct.

<details><summary>Verifier reasoning</summary>

The claim is a straightforward dead-surface removal and it holds up under direct inspection: renderWelcomeHtml emits a script-free document, so the `script-src 'nonce-…'` directive has no possible matching element, and the crypto-random generation plus the nanoid import exist solely to feed it. The single defending comment justifies the generator, not the directive, and git history (nonce present since the webview's first commit, never accompanied by a script) rules out both the "leftover from removed interactivity" and "scaffold for planned interactivity" escapes. No ruling, ratchet, test, or external contract touches the string; the only consumer is extension.ts. Cost is three deleted lines and one edited string in one file, and the resulting policy is strictly tighter than what it replaces. The finding's own scoping — leaving `enableScripts: true` untouched because the `command:` links are the page's only function — is the right call and keeps the risk at essentially zero. Only the arithmetic (-4 vs -3) and one over-strong "equivalent to" phrasing needed correcting.

</details>

### FileList's "Compare with previous round" button is statically unreachable — its two arguments are provably equal, so the only producer of the COMPARE_PREVIOUS command never renders

- **Slice**: b11 · **Kind**: defect · **Risk**: low · **Net**: 0 LoC
- **Files**: `packages/extension/src/progressView/frontend/components/FileList.ts`, `src/shared/schemas/output.ts`, `src/controllers/progressView/ProgressWorkflowFileActionsController.ts`

**Evidence**

FileList.ts:268-270 computes the two values that later become `basePath` and `previousPath`:
`const effectiveBase = getEffectiveDiffBase(file.lineage)?.absolutePath ?? '';`
`const diffBase = file.lineage?.diffBase?.absolutePath;`
and FileList.ts:291-296 passes them in that order: `this.renderPreviousAction(filePath, effectiveBase, diffBase, idPrefix)`.

FileList.ts:455 is the guard: `if (!previousPath || previousPath === basePath) return nothing;`

src/shared/schemas/output.ts:146-150 defines `getEffectiveDiffBase(lineage) { return lineage?.diffBase ?? lineage?.original ?? null; }`. Case split is total:

- `lineage.diffBase` present → `effectiveBase === diffBase.absolutePath === previousPath` → `previousPath === basePath` → returns `nothing`.
- `lineage.diffBase` absent → `previousPath` is `undefined` → `!previousPath` → returns `nothing`.
  So renderPreviousAction (FileList.ts:449-468) can never return a button; the `prev-btn` control has never been reachable.

Sole-producer check: `grep -rn "COMPARE_PREVIOUS|comparePrevious" src packages` gives exactly one production emitter — FileList.ts:462 — plus the receiving half (src/shared/ipc.ts:177, src/shared/schemas/progressView/inbound.ts:238, src/controllers/progressView/ProgressViewCommandHandlers.ts:344-345, ProgressWorkflowFileActionsController.ts:101-113) and two test files. No CLI NDJSON, persisted file, settings key, or texra-action contract is involved — this is the webview→extension-host inbound channel, versioned with the extension.

No comment defends the current argument pairing; the only nearby comment (FileList.ts:274-277) explains `compareBase`, a different variable.

History: predates the package move (`git log -S renderPreviousAction` → 4d1306e081); the `diffBase ?? original` shape at line 268 was already there before #c9566d140b merely swapped the inline expression for the shared helper.

Dedupe: `renderPreviousAction`, `COMPARE_PREVIOUS`, `comparePrevious`, `getEffectiveDiffBase`, `FileList` all return zero hits in the rounds-1-4 index and in the three survey docs (the one `FileList` hit in the 49-candidates doc is a refuted finding about archived-guard listeners, unrelated).

**Proposal**

Recommended: fix, don't delete. Pass the workspace original as the base so the two values can differ — `this.renderPreviousAction(filePath, file.lineage?.original?.absolutePath ?? '', diffBase, idPrefix)`. That is a one-line change and matches the backend contract: ProgressWorkflowFileActionsController.comparePrevious (:101-113) does `const previousFile = previous ?? base; await host.compareFiles(previousFile, file)`, i.e. it wants `prev` = the previous-round snapshot (`diffBase`) and diffs it against the current output. With the fix the button renders exactly when a file has both an `original` and a distinct `diffBase` — the in-place-rewrite case the lineage doc describes.

Alternative if the maintainer decides the affordance is not wanted: delete the whole vertical — renderPreviousAction + its call site (FileList.ts:291-296, 449-468), the inbound schema member (inbound.ts:238), the handler row (ProgressViewCommandHandlers.ts:344-345), `comparePrevious` (ProgressWorkflowFileActionsController.ts:101-113), and the two test sites. That path is roughly -55 LoC.

Either way it is a product decision, so file it rather than silently picking. Do not ship the fix without a screenshot check that the fourth icon does not crowd the `.file-actions` row.

**What we give up**

Give up if the maintainer says the button was deliberately retired in place (left wired but never shown) — but then the delete option applies, not the status quo. Also drop the one-line fix if `lineage.original` turns out to be the run-storage snapshot rather than the workspace document for the file classes that carry a `diffBase`, in which case the two would still coincide and the vertical really is dead.

**Verifier corrections — these override the evidence and proposal above**

1. The recommended one-liner is wrong and should not be shipped as written. Passing `file.lineage?.original?.absolutePath ?? ''` as `basePath` makes the button render in cases where it IS redundant: when `original === filePath` (true in-place overwrite) `compareBase` falls back to `effectiveBase === diffBase`, so "Compare with base" already opens the prev-round diff and a second button duplicates it; when `original` is null the base becomes `''` and the same duplication occurs. The correct minimal fix is to pass the already-computed `compareBase` (FileList.ts:279-282) instead of `effectiveBase` at :293, keeping the guard's original meaning ("hide when it would duplicate the compare button") and making it non-vacuous.

2. "matches the backend contract: ... does `const previousFile = previous ?? base`" is a misreading of what `base` does. In ProgressWorkflowFileActionsController.comparePrevious (:101-113) `base` is only a fallback used when `prev` is absent; since `renderPreviousAction` always sets `prev`, the `base` data attribute is never consulted on this path. The argument being fixed matters solely as the guard's comparand, not as a value the controller uses.

3. History attribution is incomplete. `git log -S renderPreviousAction` returning only 4d1306e081 reflects the package move, but the semantic cause is 9512d6bc14 (#4500, 2026-05-26), which introduced `compareBase` for the compare/accept buttons and left `renderPreviousAction` on `effectiveBase`. Also note the control was already unreachable _before_ #4500 for the same `diffBase ?? original` reason, so this is a long-standing dead affordance rather than a #4500 regression — #4500 is what made the affordance meaningfully distinct and therefore worth restoring.

4. The delete alternative has one consideration the report omits: removing `COMPARE_PREVIOUS` from `src/shared/ipc.ts:177` and the inbound schema touches the frozen (unpublished) SDK type surface mirrored in `packages/agent/dist/types/src/shared/ipc.d.ts:154` and `.../progressView/inbound.d.ts:294,560`. Not a blocker, but it makes the delete path more than a webview-local change.

5. The claimed ~-55 LoC for the delete path is about right (renderPreviousAction ~20, call site ~6, inbound member, handler row 2, controller method ~13, two test sites) — call it -50 to -60, not a number worth arguing over since the fix path is preferred.

6. "the `prev-btn` control has never been reachable" is correct as stated for all of git history reachable from HEAD's file, and I confirm it independently; the extra supporting fact is that no `.prev-btn` CSS rule exists, which is what you would expect for a control nobody ever styled after seeing it.

<details><summary>Verifier reasoning</summary>

Verified by re-reading the cited lines rather than trusting the report. The case split is total and the guard suppresses both branches, so the button provably never renders — a real defect regardless of LoC. Dedupe, ruling, comment-defense, external-consumer, ratchet, and churn checks all fail to kill it. The report's diagnosis is right; its proposed fix is not, so the fix is corrected to pass `compareBase` (a one-line change already computed two lines above), which restores the guard's intended meaning without introducing a duplicate button.

</details>

### Two progress-view panels re-derive facts their Zod-validated payloads already guarantee, and one of the dead arms is carried into its caller's guard

- **Slice**: b12 · **Kind**: consolidate · **Risk**: low · **Net**: -11 LoC (proposer claimed -14; verifier figure governs)
- **Files**: `packages/extension/src/progressView/frontend/components/ToolEditRequestPanel.ts`, `packages/extension/src/progressView/frontend/components/UsagePanel.ts`

**Evidence**

Both panels render payloads that `dispatchProgressViewOutbound` has already parsed against their schemas (messageDispatcher.ts:49-64 documents that contract), then re-check invariants the schema makes unrepresentable.

(a) `ToolEditRequestPanel.renderDiffMeta` (:119-155). Its `toCount` helper is four defenses over one field:

```ts
const toCount = (value: number | undefined): number =>
  value !== undefined && Number.isFinite(value) ? Math.max(0, value) : 0;
```

`ToolEditPermissionSchema` declares `addedLines: LineCountSchema` and `removedLines: LineCountSchema` (src/shared/schemas/prompts.ts:34-35), and `LineCountSchema = z.int().nonnegative()` (src/shared/schemas/lineChanges.ts:7) — required, non-nullable, integral, ≥ 0. `!== undefined` cannot be false (the declared param type `number | undefined` is wider than the field), `Number.isFinite` cannot be false after `z.int()`, and `Math.max(0, …)` cannot bite after `.nonnegative()`. The sole producer, `src/tools/approval/toolEditApproval.ts:122-123`, feeds it straight from `computeLineChangeSummary`.

The same function declares `TemplateResult | typeof nothing` (:121) but has exactly one `return`, at :137 — the `nothing` arm has never existed in this function's history (`git log -L 119,155` back through cd2c32c30b, 644a64f2cf, 184c9aa6fc; `git log -S"if (total === 0) return nothing"` finds nothing). So the caller's guard at :60, `if (diffMeta !== nothing) metaParts.push(diffMeta);`, is always true. `request` (:120) is also a parameter always derived from the receiver — the single call site is `this.renderDiffMeta(data)` at :57 where `data = this.permission.data` (:56).

(b) `UsagePanel.hasContext` (:176-181):

```ts
return (
  (this.contextState?.contextWindow ?? 0) > 0 &&
  this.contextState?.utilizationPercent !== undefined
);
```

`ContextStateDataSchema` (src/shared/schemas/contextManagement.ts:61-65) declares `contextWindow: PositiveTokenCountSchema` (= `z.int().positive()`, line 13) and `utilizationPercent: z.number().nonnegative()` — required. Both conjuncts reduce to `this.contextState != null`. `renderContext` (:284-285) then repeats that same null check as its own early return, so the `?hidden=${!this.hasContext}` binding at :193 and the getter are two more spellings of one test. Inside, `clamp(utilizationPercent, 0, 100)` (:293) has a lower bound that `.nonnegative()` already guarantees; only the upper bound does work.

Dedupe: neither `renderDiffMeta` nor `hasContext` appears in the four survey docs or the 295 rounds 1-4 titles. This is NOT the round-3-refuted "four redundant defensive copies/re-parses on same-process typed handoffs" (that was about re-parsing RunScope / workflow hydrate / tool-use resume / CLI NDJSON status across process seams), and NOT `docs/proposals/2026-08-16-overdefensive-top10.md` §1, which is about the `z.unknown()` `StreamLogEntry.data` carrier and its per-consumer `safeParse` branches — a different field and a different failure mode.

**Proposal**

Two small edits, batched because they are one rule ("a panel painting a schema-parsed payload does not re-validate it"). In `ToolEditRequestPanel`: delete `toCount`, read `request.addedLines`/`request.removedLines` directly, narrow the return type to `TemplateResult`, drop the `request` parameter in favor of `this.permission.data`, and collapse `render`'s `if (diffMeta !== nothing)` to an unconditional `metaParts.push(this.renderDiffMeta())`. In `UsagePanel`: replace the `hasContext` getter body with `this.contextState != null`, and drop either the `?hidden` binding or `renderContext`'s early return so one owner decides visibility. Keep `clamp`'s upper bound (utilization genuinely exceeds 100) and keep the `Math.max(1, …)` floor at :294 — that one is a deliberate, documented display rule, not a defense. Roughly -14 lines, no behavior change.

**What we give up**

Give up on part (a) if the intent was ever that a zero-line edit shows no diff meta at all — in that case the right fix is the opposite: make `renderDiffMeta` actually `return nothing` when `total === 0`, which keeps the union arm and the caller's guard alive. Check with a maintainer whether "0 lines" beside a file path is wanted before deleting the arm. Give up on part (b) if `ContextStateData` is ever constructed in the renderer outside the parsed wire path.

**Verifier corrections — these override the evidence and proposal above**

Three factual errors, all in part (b); part (a) is accurate as written.

1. "the `?hidden` binding at :193 and the getter are two more spellings of one test ... drop either the `?hidden` binding or `renderContext`'s early return" — the early return at :285 CANNOT be dropped. Lit evaluates `${this.renderContext()}` at :194 on every render regardless of the `hidden` attribute, and the body immediately destructures `this.contextState` at :286-287. Removing the early return is both a TypeScript error and a runtime TypeError whenever contextState is null. Only the `?hidden` binding is removable.

2. Unstated and load-bearing: the `?hidden` binding is ALREADY INERT in this component. `UsagePanel`'s shadow root style list is `[designTokens, css\`…\`]`(:75-77) — it does not include`commonViewStyles`, which is where `[hidden] { display: none !important; }`lives (src/shared/styles/commonViewStyles.ts:411-413). The author rule`:is(.run-summary, .context-state) { display: inline-flex; }`(:101-107) beats the UA`[hidden]`rule by cascade origin, so the attribute hides nothing today. Visibility is already decided solely by`renderContext()`returning`nothing`. This makes dropping `?hidden`strictly behavior-neutral (an empty zero-width inline-flex span in a`space-between`footer with`row-gap` only costs no layout), and it is a stronger argument for the edit than the one the finding gives — but it also means the edit removes a line that was doing nothing rather than de-duplicating a live test.

3. `hasContext` still has a real caller after the simplification — `render`'s `if (!this.hasUsage && !this.hasContext) return nothing;` at :184 — so the getter stays; only its body collapses. The finding's phrasing ("two more spellings of one test") implies one of the three sites disappears entirely, which is not the case.

Minor, non-blocking: messageDispatcher.ts's contract comment is at :49-62, not :49-64; the "documents that contract" credit is better placed on `createDispatcher` (src/shared/utils/dispatcher.ts:145-150), which is where the production parse actually happens. And the claim that `LineCountSchema`'s `z.int()` makes `Number.isFinite` dead is true at runtime but redundant as an argument — the declared parameter type on `this.permission.data` already makes `addedLines: number`, so `!== undefined` and `Number.isFinite` are dead by types alone, independent of whether any parse ran.

Coordination note for the PR: 2026-08-03-ssot-consolidation-plan.md B2 proposes folding `UsagePanel.hasUsage` (:164-175) into a shared `isEmptyUsage`. That item is still open and lands in the same getter block; if both ship, sequence them or batch them.

<details><summary>Verifier reasoning</summary>

Part (a) is solid on the strongest possible grounds: `renderDiffMeta` is typed `TemplateResult | typeof nothing` but has a single `return html\`…\``at :137, so`if (diffMeta !== nothing)`at :60 is unconditionally true — no schema argument is even needed for that half. The`toCount`helper is dead by the declared type of`this.permission.data` (`ToolEditPermission`, where both counts are required `number`), and dead again at runtime because the payload is parsed by `createDispatcher`against`ToolEditPermissionSchema`(outbound.ts:181-182) before any handler runs. The parameter is passed`this.permission.data` at the one call site. Zero-line edits currently render "0 lines" with a "No line changes" tooltip, so deleting the union arm preserves today's behavior rather than choosing between two behaviors — the give-up branch does not fire.

Part (b) survives but is weaker than presented. `ContextStateDataSchema` does make both conjuncts of `hasContext` reduce to a null check, and the single write site plus the batch schema's degrade-to-DEFAULT recovery keep that guarantee intact. But the proposal's second half is wrong about which of the two sites is removable, and it misses that the removable one is already inert. Corrected, the edit is still real and still behavior-preserving; it just yields less than claimed.

On cost: claimed -14 is optimistic. Honest count — ToolEditRequestPanel: -1 (collapse the guard at :57/:60 into one `metaParts.push(this.renderDiffMeta())`), -2 (three-line signature to one), -2 (delete `toCount`), -1 (the now-unused `import type { ToolEditPermission }`), while the two `const added/removed` lines stay at two; the `nothing` specifier drops from the existing lit import line without removing it. That is about -6, maybe -7 if the destructure fits one line under prettier's 80 columns (it lands at exactly 80 with indent, so it may wrap and give back a line). UsagePanel: -3 (six-line getter to three), -1 (the `?hidden` line). Total about -10 to -11. No tests change, so there is no test-LoC bonus. Both edits are within one component's private surface, no exported symbol changes, no wire or persisted format touched — hence low risk.
