### Three fallbacks for one missing account label, and the least informative one wins: the settings account card headlines "N/A"

- **Slice**: b14 · **Kind**: amend · **Risk**: low · **Net**: 0 LoC (proposer claimed -2; verifier figure governs)
- **Files**: `packages/extension/src/settingsView/frontend/slices/profileSlice.ts`, `packages/extension/src/settingsView/frontend/tabs/AccountTab.ts`

**Evidence**

AccountTab.ts:64-66 has its own fallback: `hasStoredAccount && this.userEmail ? this.userEmail : 'TeXRA account'`, with the comment "Unavailable and expired sessions retain the stored account label." That `&& this.userEmail` test can never be false when `hasStoredAccount` is true, because profileSlice.ts:17 substitutes a placeholder one hop earlier: `userEmail.set(data.user?.email ?? 'N/A')`. Path to the bad render: `SettingsProfileController.buildProfileMessage` (src/controllers/settingsView/SettingsProfileController.ts:67-84) sets `sessionProblem='expired'` for an invalid stored session and returns `user: storedEmail ? { email: storedEmail } : null`; `getStoredAccountLabel` (src/auth/SupabaseClient.ts:282-292) returns null both when nothing is stored and when the read throws. So an expired session whose label is unreadable arrives as `user: null` → the slice makes it `'N/A'` → AccountTab's guard passes → the banner title renders the literal string "N/A" instead of "TeXRA account", above the "Session expired" tag.
The two comments in the area do NOT bless this: SupabaseClient.ts:287-288 says "Callers render \"N/A\" for null" — a description of the caller, written when the caller was a field row, not the card headline — and SupabaseSession.ts:168 explicitly delegates: "the caller decides whether to surface \"N/A\"". The caller has already decided, at AccountTab.ts:66; the slice's substitution is what prevents that decision from taking effect. There are exactly two `'N/A'` producers repo-wide (SettingsProfileController.ts:92 and profileSlice.ts:17) and one consumer (AccountTab.ts:66).
Dedupe: no `userEmail`/`N/A` entry in rounds1234-index.md, and `grep -rn "userEmail|'N/A'"` over the four survey docs in docs/proposals/ returns nothing. Round 4B's "four born-dead account-auth copy formatters" is src/shared/copy/accountAuth, a different surface.

**Proposal**

Delete the frontend placeholder: `userEmail.set(data.user?.email ?? '')` in profileSlice.ts:17, so AccountTab's own `'TeXRA account'` fallback becomes reachable and the `&& this.userEmail` guard becomes load-bearing instead of dead. Then decide the authenticated case at the one remaining producer (SettingsProfileController.ts:92): either keep `?? 'N/A'` there deliberately, or drop it too and let the same UI fallback cover both. Do not add a new copy constant — this is a subtraction.

**What we give up**

If a maintainer wants "N/A" to be the visible account-card headline for a stored-but-unreadable session (i.e. treats the literal as a deliberate signal to the user), or if a screenshot/walkthrough asset pins the string. Neither is evidenced in-repo; `scripts/capture-walkthrough-media.mjs` does not reference it.

**Verifier corrections — these override the evidence and proposal above**

1. LoC is wrong. Both proposed edits are same-line changes (`?? 'N/A'` deleted from an existing expression); no line is added or removed. Honest net is 0, not −2. If the now-stale `SupabaseClient.ts:287-288` comment is rewritten rather than deleted, it stays 0.
2. "That `&& this.userEmail` test can never be false when `hasStoredAccount` is true" is true only after the first UPDATE_PROFILE has been handled. `settingsState.ts:160` initializes `userEmail` to `''` via `trackedSignal(() => '')`, so pre-message and post-reset the property is empty — but `authenticated` and `sessionProblem` reset in the same registry, so `hasStoredAccount` is false there too and the conclusion (dead guard in practice) holds.
3. "an expired session whose label is unreadable" understates the precondition and misses the likelier path. `SupabaseSession.getStoredAccountLabel` is `session?.account.label ?? null`, and `supabaseSessionTypes.ts:153` derives the label as `email?.trim() || user.id`, so a stored, parseable session always has a non-empty label. The reachable paths are (a) the store read throwing — which classifies as `'transient'`/`'unavailable'`, not `'expired'`, so the more likely bad banner is the outage one, and (b) a persisted label that trims to `''` (`supabaseSessionTypes.ts:13`), which is falsy at `SettingsProfileController.ts:81` and collapses to `user: null` the same way.
4. The fix must also correct `SupabaseClient.ts:287-288`, which becomes factually false once no caller renders "N/A" for null. That is a comment edit, not an added constant, so it does not violate the "subtraction only" framing — but the finding should name it as part of the change.
5. Scope note the finding omits: `packages/desktop/src/renderer` mounts the same `SettingsApp` (`SettingsApp.ts:352` is the single `<account-tab>` binding), so the defect and the fix cover both hosts, not just the extension.

<details><summary>Verifier reasoning</summary>

Verified by reading every cited line at HEAD. The defect is real and reachable: `profileSlice.ts:17` substitutes `'N/A'` for a null user one hop before `AccountTab.ts:66` tests for an empty label, so the tab's own `'TeXRA account'` fallback is unreachable and the account card can headline the literal "N/A". Neither nearby comment blesses it — one justifies a warn log and predates the guard, the other explicitly delegates the decision to the caller. No dedupe hit in the round-1-4 index or the four survey docs, no dated ruling, no test or wire contract pins the string, and the only test on this render uses a real email. The claimed −2 LoC is wrong (the edits are same-line, net 0) and the failure mode is an outage banner more often than an expired one, but a defect is judged on reality, not profit, and this one is a masking fallback of the kind §15 and the "never compensate at render time" rule both target. Low risk: two token deletions plus a comment fix, one shared component across both hosts.

</details>

### `texra.compare` / `texra.acceptEdited` carry a dead first argument: one caller passes the base file twice, the other passes a throwing placeholder marked "unused"

- **Slice**: b15 · **Kind**: delete · **Risk**: low · **Net**: -70 LoC (proposer claimed -32; verifier figure governs)
- **Files**: `packages/extension/src/webview/managers/executionHandlers.ts`, `packages/extension/src/commands/extensionCommandHandlers.ts`, `packages/extension/src/commands/latex/compareCommands.ts`, `packages/extension/src/progressView/ProgressViewMessageHandler.ts`

**Evidence**

executionHandlers.ts:118-126 (my slice) passes `pathToLocation(message.baseFile)` as BOTH arg 1 and arg 2 of `texra.compare` / `texra.acceptEdited`. The other production caller, ProgressViewMessageHandler.ts:436-448, passes `pathToLocation('')` in slot 1 with the literal comment `// inputFile unused` — and that placeholder is not inert: `pathToLocation` (src/utils/files/fileLocation.ts:68-79) throws `Cannot resolve empty path without workspace` when `locatePath('')` resolves external. Downstream, arg 1 reaches exactly one expression: compareCommands.ts:38 `const fileToUseLocation = baseLocation ?? inputLocation;` inside `validateFileLocations` (:32-43), called from `handleCompare` (:95-103) and `handleAcceptEdited` (:219-228). Both callers always supply a non-null `baseLocation`, so the `?? inputLocation` arm is unreachable in production. Same function also declares a third parameter `editedLocation` (:35) that its body never reads — the error text is passed separately as `errorMessage`. Consumer count is closed: `rg 'texra.compare|texra.acceptEdited'` over src+packages returns only those two call sites plus the handler table (extensionCommandHandlers.ts:264-288) and the interface (:167-178); both ids are in `EXTENSION_INTERNAL_COMMAND_IDS` (:122-129, "intentionally absent from the shared catalog — they don't appear in the command palette or package.json contributions"), and `rg '"command": "texra.(compare|acceptEdited)"' packages/extension/package.json` returns nothing. Not a wire/persisted/settings surface. Dedupe: none of `acceptEdited`, `validateFileLocations`, `inputLocation` appears in rounds1234-index or in any docs/proposals survey (grepped all four).

**Proposal**

Drop the leading `inputLocation` parameter from `texra.compare` and `texra.acceptEdited` end to end: `CompareCommandArgsSchema`/`AcceptEditedCommandArgsSchema` (extensionCommandHandlers.ts:74-93) lose their first `FileLocationSchema.nullish()`, `ExtensionCommandActions.compare`/`.acceptEdited` (:167-178) and the two `definedHandler` bodies (:264-288) lose the arg, `handleCompare`/`handleAcceptEdited` (compareCommands.ts:95,219) take `(baseLocation, editedLocation, …)`. `validateFileLocations` then reduces to a two-line `if (!baseLocation) { showLoggedMessage(...); return null; }` guard at each caller (or keeps the helper minus both dead params). Update the two call sites: executionHandlers.ts:118-126 stops duplicating `pathToLocation(message.baseFile)`; ProgressViewMessageHandler.ts:436-448 drops both `pathToLocation('')` placeholders and their comments, removing the latent no-workspace throw.

**What we give up**

The unreachable `baseLocation ?? inputLocation` fallback — if a future caller ever wanted to compare against the primary input file rather than a base file, it would have to pass it as `baseLocation`. No production caller does today, and the ProgressView comment shows the slot was already understood as vestigial.

**Verifier corrections — these override the evidence and proposal above**

Three factual errors, none fatal:

1. OVERSTATED THROW. "that placeholder is not inert: `pathToLocation` throws" is only true with no workspace folder open. `WorkspaceFS.locatePath('')` (src/utils/files/workspaceFS.ts:50-71) short-circuits to `{kind:'external', absolutePath:''}` only when `getPath()` is undefined; with a workspace it falls through to `locatePathInRoot(root, '')` (src/utils/files/workspaceRoot.ts:41-59), where `path.posix.normalize('')` yields `'.'`, which does not start with `'..'`, so it returns `kind:'workspace'`, `absolutePath = root`, `relativePath = '.'`. So in the normal (workspace-open) ProgressView case the placeholder resolves to a bogus-but-non-throwing FileLocation pointing at the workspace root. The latent throw exists but is reachable only in a no-folder VS Code window.

2. "arg 1 reaches exactly one expression" is FALSE. Besides compareCommands.ts:38, arg 1 is read by the `.refine(([inputLocation, baseLocation]) => inputLocation != null || baseLocation != null, { error: 'inputLocation or baseLocation required' })` predicate on BOTH `CompareCommandArgsSchema` and `AcceptEditedCommandArgsSchema` (extensionCommandHandlers.ts:74-93). The proposal does list those schemas for edit, but the evidence census is wrong: there are three readers, not one. (Removing the slot also means deciding whether slot-1-less `baseLocation` stays `.nullish()` with the runtime guard in compareCommands, or becomes required — the finding does not say.)

3. TEST CONSUMER OMITTED. The consumer census excluded tests, and there is a live suite pinning this exact behavior: src/test-kernel/commands/ExtensionCommandRegistry.vitest.ts — `it('forwards compare and accept arguments without collapsing them')` (:307), `it('forwards accept arguments when copy metadata is omitted')` (:341), and a dedicated `it('preserves the input-location fallback when base is omitted')` (:362-390) that asserts `compare`/`acceptEdited` receive `(WORKSPACE_INPUT, undefined, EDITED_FILE)`. That last test must be deleted, not adapted, and the other two lose an argument.

Minor line-number drift: `handleCompare` is at compareCommands.ts:94 (not :95) and `handleAcceptEdited` at :218 (not :219).

<details><summary>Verifier reasoning</summary>

The claim is a straightforward speculative-generality deletion and every load-bearing fact checks out at HEAD. Arg 1 has no production value: one caller duplicates the base file into it, the other stuffs a placeholder it explicitly labels unused, and the sibling desktop path never had the parameter. The only code that reads it is a `?? inputLocation` fallback that can never fire (both callers always supply a non-null base) plus two tuple `.refine` predicates that exist solely to keep that fallback honest. The dead third parameter of `validateFileLocations` is a bonus confirmation the helper has drifted. Nothing frozen is touched: both command ids are declared internal, absent from the catalog and from package.json contributions, so there is no palette, keybinding, or wire consumer to break. The claimed -32 undercounts: production alone is roughly -45 (two schema refines ~14, interface + two definedHandler bodies ~14, compareCommands helper and its two call sites ~18, minus the three call-site lines in the two hosts), and deleting the fallback test plus trimming two others adds roughly another -30. Risk is low — behavior-preserving, single-package, compile-checked by the tuple schemas and the `satisfies` constraint on the handler map. The only judgment call the implementer must make explicitly is whether `baseLocation` becomes schema-required (changing a malformed-args error from a runtime showLoggedMessage to a parse rejection) or stays `.nullish()` with the guard preserved; the safe move is the latter.

</details>

### Two per-component prefers-reduced-motion blocks that lose to the `!important` reduced-motion reset designTokens already ships

- **Slice**: b15 · **Kind**: delete · **Risk**: low · **Net**: -12 LoC
- **Files**: `packages/extension/src/webview/frontend/components/InstructionPanel.styles.ts`, `packages/extension/src/webview/frontend/styles.ts`, `src/shared/styles/litStyles.ts`

**Evidence**

litStyles.ts:193-205 — `designTokens` ends with `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { *, *::before, *::after { animation-duration: 0.01ms !important; animation-iteration-count: 1 !important; transition-duration: 0.01ms !important; scroll-behavior: auto !important; } }`, documented as applying "inside every shadow root that adopts the token sheet". Both components in this slice adopt it: InstructionPanel.ts:106-111 (`[designTokens, commonViewStyles, selectStyles, instructionPanelStyles]`) and MainApp.ts:136-142. So InstructionPanel.styles.ts:520-526 (`.session-hint, .launcher-picker-pane, :host([desktop-host]) .instruction-box { transition: none; }`) and styles.ts:374-378 (`.desktop-file-context-chevron { transition: none; }`) are non-important declarations that can never beat `transition-duration: 0.01ms !important` — every selector targets an element inside the component's own shadow tree, which `*` matches. I checked the one rule that is NOT redundant and it must stay: styles.ts:379-381 `.launcher-loading-canvas wa-skeleton::part(indicator) { animation: none; }` pierces wa-skeleton's nested shadow root, where the host's `*` reset does not reach. Also confirms the local blocks are not compensating for a gap the reset leaves: InstructionPanel's two animations — `.session-hint { animation: session-hint-fade … }` (:109) and the infinite `.recording { animation: pulse-record 1.2s ease-in-out infinite }` (:528-533) — are covered by the reset's `animation-duration`/`animation-iteration-count`, and neither is named by the local `transition: none` block anyway. Dedupe: rounds1234-index has no reduced-motion or InstructionPanel.styles entry; grepped the four survey docs for `prefers-reduced-motion`, `session-hint`, `picker-pane` — no hits.

**Proposal**

Delete the `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` block at InstructionPanel.styles.ts:520-526 and the `.desktop-file-context-chevron` rule inside styles.ts:374-378, keeping the `wa-skeleton::part(indicator)` rule (which needs its own `@media` wrapper once the chevron rule leaves). While in the same file, the four `.team-picker-visible` / `.agent-picker-visible` pane rules (InstructionPanel.styles.ts:253-274) restate one pair of values — the hidden pane is always `opacity:0; pointer-events:none; position:absolute` and the visible one always `opacity:1; pointer-events:auto; position:static`, and the wrapper always carries exactly one of the two classes (InstructionPanel.ts:443-447) — so they collapse to two rules; that half is optional and carries a small geometry risk because `.agent-picker-pane` alone declares `inset: 0` (:246-251).

**What we give up**

Local, explicit intent-documentation in each component's sheet. The behaviour is identical: 0.01ms with one iteration versus `none` is imperceptible either way, which is exactly what the shared reset's own comment says it is for.

**Verifier corrections — these override the evidence and proposal above**

1. CASCADE REASONING IS WRONG (does not change the verdict). "Non-important declarations that can never beat `transition-duration: 0.01ms !important`" is false. `transition: none` is a shorthand: it sets `transition-property: none` along with duration/timing/delay. The reset only marks `transition-duration`, `animation-duration`, `animation-iteration-count` and `scroll-behavior` as `!important` — it never sets `transition-property`. So the local normal declaration DOES win for `transition-property`, and the computed result with the local rule is `transition-property: none` (no transition runs, no transitionrun/transitionend fires) versus `transition-property: opacity|transform, transition-duration: 0.01ms` without it. The correct argument is not "the locals are inert", it is "both outcomes are user-visibly identical (0.01ms is one imperceptible frame, exactly what the shared comment claims) and nothing observes transition events" — I confirmed the latter: `grep -rn "transitionend|transitionrun|animationend"` over packages/extension/src/webview/frontend and packages/desktop/src returns zero hits.
2. "Neither [animation] is named by the local `transition: none` block anyway" is wrong for `.session-hint`: it IS named at InstructionPanel.styles.ts:521. The substance still holds — `.session-hint` (:104-110) declares only `animation: session-hint-fade var(--transition-fast)` and no `transition`, so the local `transition: none` on it is inert today independent of the reset. The block is only load-bearing-looking for `.launcher-picker-pane` (:234-238, `transition: opacity var(--transition-fast)`) and `:host([desktop-host]) .instruction-box` (:325-334).
3. The proposal's "keeping the `wa-skeleton::part(indicator)` rule (which needs its own `@media` wrapper once the chevron rule leaves)" is wrong. The `@media` wrapper at styles.ts:374 and its closing brace at :382 stay; only the inner rule at :375-377 plus the blank at :378 are removed. No new wrapper is written, which is why the count is -12 and not -10.
4. OMISSION worth resolving before shipping: two structurally identical blocks that also lose to the same reset are NOT in the finding's scope — `packages/extension/src/progressView/frontend/components/ToolEditRequestPanel.styles.ts:72-76` (`.diff-dropdown-trigger wa-icon { transition: none; }`) and `packages/extension/src/progressView/frontend/components/ApproveSplitButton.ts:81-85` (`.approve-split-trigger wa-icon { transition: none; }`). Both components adopt `designTokens` (ApproveSplitButton.ts:50-53; ToolEditRequestPanel.ts:38-42) and both targets are shadow-tree elements the `*` reset matches. Both are pinned by `src/test-kernel/progressView/ToolEditRequestPanel.vitest.ts:193-194` ("keeps native caret state motion-safe"). Deleting only the two in scope leaves the convention half-applied and invites the reviewer question "why not those?"; deleting all four requires amending that test. Either extend the PR to all four and drop those two assertions with the same argument, or state in the PR description why the pinned pair is deliberately left alone.
5. The one rule the finding keeps is correctly kept and for the right reason: `.launcher-loading-canvas wa-skeleton::part(indicator) { animation: none; }` reaches into wa-skeleton's own shadow root, which does not adopt `designTokens`, so the `*` reset cannot reach it. `CompactionActivityRender.vitest.ts:82-92` pins the same ::part-piercing pattern for `wa-spinner::part(base)` and its comment ("designTokens also mention prefers-reduced-motion, so pin the component-owned rule") is direct repo evidence that the piercing case is the intended local-block use and the non-piercing case is not.
6. Both blocks were written AFTER the shared reset (reset: cecdb27977, 2026-06-10; InstructionPanel block: 9a617f9c92 #9216, 2026-07-26; styles.ts block: 434559d50c #9702, 2026-08-04). That is not a ruling, but the PR description should say so plainly rather than implying the reset postdated them.
7. The optional second half (collapsing the four `.team-picker-visible`/`.agent-picker-visible` rules at :257-274) is correctly flagged as risk-carrying and should stay out of this PR: `.agent-picker-pane` alone declares `inset: 0` (:246-251) while `.team-picker-pane` (:241-244) does not, so the two panes are not symmetric and a naive collapse changes the absolutely-positioned pane's geometry. Its LoC is not included in my -12.

<details><summary>Verifier reasoning</summary>

The core claim holds after independent verification: both components adopt the shared token sheet, both targeted element sets live in the adopting shadow root where the reset's `*` selector applies, no test or ratchet pins the two blocks, no comment defends them, and no duplicate exists in the index or the survey docs. The finding's CSS mechanism is stated incorrectly (the shorthand's `transition-property` is not overridden by the reset), but the correct mechanism reaches the same user-visible conclusion — one imperceptible frame versus none — and nothing in the codebase listens for transition events, so the deletion is behavior-preserving. It is a small but genuine, shim-free -12. The real weakness is scope: two identical, test-pinned instances in progressView are left standing, which makes this a partially-applied cleanup rather than a finished one; that is a correction, not a refutation.

</details>

- **Slice**: b15 · **Kind**: delete · **Risk**: low · **Net**: -9 LoC (proposer claimed -16; verifier figure governs)

constants.ts:20-24 defines `parseSessionType` as `SessionTypeSchema.optional().catch(undefined).parse(...)`. It has exactly two callers. (a) sessionSlice.ts:17-20 re-parses `message.sessionType`, whose outbound schema declares `sessionType: z.string().nullish()` (outbound.ts:138-141) even though `SessionTypeSchema` is the closed vocabulary right beside it — and both producers send a literal: MainViewProvider.ts:244-248 (`sessionType: 'toolUse'`) and packages/desktop/src/main/index.ts:944-947 (`sessionType: 'toolUse' as const`); `rg SET_SELECTED_AGENT` over src+packages returns no other producer. (b) mainViewActions.ts:211-212 `changeSessionType(value: string)` re-parses a value that arrives already typed: its only caller is MainApp.ts:422-425, which passes `detail.value` from `CustomEvent<SessionTypeChangeDetail>`, and `SessionTypeChangeDetailSchema.value` is `SessionTypeSchema` (src/shared/schemas/mainView/state.ts:430-432). The DOM-boundary narrowing already happened upstream at InstructionPanel.ts:195-202, which coerces `target?.value` to one of the two literals before dispatching. **Proposal**

Tighten `SetSelectedAgentMessageSchema.sessionType` (outbound.ts:140) from `z.string().nullish()` to `SessionTypeSchema.nullish()` — schemas are the SSOT, both producers already satisfy it, and an out-of-vocabulary value then fails at the dispatcher with a reported schema error instead of vanishing. Then sessionSlice.ts:17-20 reads `message.sessionType` directly, and `changeSessionType` narrows its parameter to `SessionType` (mainViewActions.ts:211) so the `?? SESSION_TYPES.WORKFLOW` fallback goes with it. `parseSessionType` (constants.ts:20-24) then has no callers and is deleted along with its `.catch(undefined)`; `SessionTypeSchema` also stops being imported by constants.ts. src/test-kernel/webview/MainViewActions.vitest.ts:247,264,292 already pass valid literals and keep compiling.

**What we give up**

Tolerance for a host that sends a misspelled session type: today it silently falls back to workflow, afterwards the message is rejected and reported. That is the intended direction under "silent degradation is a defect", but it is a behaviour change, not a pure deletion.

**Verifier corrections — these override the evidence and proposal above**

1. LINE NUMBER WRONG: the desktop producer is packages/desktop/src/main/index.ts:919-924 (`sessionType: 'toolUse' as const` at :923), not :944-947. Content of the claim is correct.

2. NET LoC OVERSTATED (-16 claimed). PRODUCER SWEEP INCOMPLETE: the evidence's `rg SET_SELECTED_AGENT over src+packages` misses two producers that use the raw string, not the constant — scripts/capture-walkthrough-media.mjs:103 (`sessionType: 'workflow'`) and :167-170 (`'toolUse'`), and scripts/smoke-webviews-electron.mjs:47-51 (`'workflow'`). Both post into the built webview bundle. Both send in-vocabulary literals, so the tightening is still safe, but the "no other producer" claim as written is false.

<details><summary>Verifier reasoning</summary>

Both targets are provably unreachable at HEAD and I verified each link in the chain myself rather than trusting the evidence block: the two call sites (rg over the full repo, node_modules excluded, returns 5 hits total — one definition, two imports, two calls), the Set-based producer, the Zod-validated inbound message plus the type-predicate narrowing, the total Record with no cast and no `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`, and the host-side handler that re-resolves, re-filters and re-dedupes. Nothing in the repo's dated rulings or the 295-title index touches either symbol, and the one nearby ruling adjudicated the twin construct as a legitimate small typing fix that has since shipped. The change touches no wire schema, no persisted file, no settings key, no ratchet, and no test. Under the repo's "silent degradation is a defect" rule this is not a masking-fallback removal but the opposite: two constructs that can never execute, one of which lies about the function's contract by declaring a boolean nobody reads. The only real defect in the finding is arithmetic: -3, not -8, because four of the five edits are in-place and the `@utils/core` import line survives on `tryParseUrl`. A sign-preserving overstatement on a zero-churn, zero-test, three-file deletion does not meet the bar for a kill under criterion 7 — the finding itself flags this as a batch of 1-3 line items and explicitly refuses to expand into a drop-path sweep, which is the right scope discipline. Risk is low: behaviour is bit-identical on every reachable input, and both removals would be caught by `npm run typecheck` if my narrowing analysis were wrong.

The preprocessor it now wraps is `normalizeAgentConfigInput` (:80-92), whose entire job is to stamp `agentCategory: AgentCategory.Workflow` onto an input that omits it, so the discriminated union can select a variant — it does no field renaming at all, and its own docblock (:76-79) says so. ### Onboarding funnel treats any credential-probe failure as "no credential" and blanks the whole launcher, silently

- **Slice**: b15 · **Kind**: amend · **Risk**: low · **Net**: 10 LoC (proposer claimed 4; verifier figure governs)
- **Files**: `packages/extension/src/webview/MainViewProvider.ts`, `src/controllers/onboarding/onboardingFunnel.ts`, `packages/desktop/src/main/index.ts`

**Evidence**

MainViewProvider.ts:209-211: `const hasCredential = await hasAnyUsableSetupCredential().catch(() => false);` — bare catch, no log, no comment justifying it (so there is no comment to defeat). The value feeds `planOnboardingFunnelTransition` (:212-216). Traced the consequence: `deriveOnboardingFunnelState` (onboardingFunnel.ts:31-40) returns `'needs-credential'` for `{hasCredential:false, firstRunDone:false, declined:false}`, and MainApp.ts:358-384 renders ONLY `<onboarding-welcome-card>` for that state — the agent/model pickers, Files and LaTeXDiffs are all replaced. So a transient failure inside `hasUsableSetupCredential` (src/model/setupCredentialAccess.ts:24-31 → `isCodexSubscriptionActive` reading the OAuth token, then `hasAnyUsableProviderApiKey(secrets)` reading VS Code SecretStorage — a locked/absent keyring rejects) turns into "you have no credentials, here is the first-run welcome card" for an existing user, with nothing in the log. Cross-host counter-evidence that the mask is not policy: the desktop host wires the same probe with no catch at packages/desktop/src/main/index.ts:940 (`hasCredential: () => hasUsableSetupCredential(platform().secrets)`). Dedupe: `hasAnyUsableSetupCredential` appears in rounds1234-index nowhere; `rg` over docs/proposals returns only 2026-08-07-prod-structural-leads-triage.md:377 (a different, refused idea: inline the 1-line delegate) and 2026-08-26-simplification-survey-round3.md:2592 (about routing it off @model/providerCapabilities). The nearest relative is docs/proposals/2026-07-12-fallback-audit.md:740-758 (P1.2), which names three OTHER false-on-error sites (packages/cli/src/onboarding/runOnboarding.tsx:129-159, packages/extension/src/extension.ts:320-349, packages/desktop/src/main/index.ts:797-836) all feeding `backfillFirstRunDone`; this fourth site is not listed there and has a different consequence (live funnel state, not a permanent marker).

**Proposal**

Keep the false — the funnel must still render something — but make it loud, per the CLAUDE.md "silent degradation is a defect" rule and P1.2's "remove false-on-error" disposition. Replace the bare `.catch(() => false)` with a caught branch that logs the cause at warn through the provider's channel (`showLoggedErrorMessage`/`createLog`) before falling back, e.g. `let hasCredential = false; try { hasCredential = await hasAnyUsableSetupCredential(); } catch (error) { log.warn(\`Credential probe failed; treating as no credential: ${toErrorMessage(error)}\`); }`. Optionally follow P1.2 and return a three-valued probe so `unknown` holds the previous funnel state instead of demoting to State 0 — but the one-line loud fallback is the bounded fix and needs no shared-service work.

**What we give up**

Nothing behavioural: the fallback value is unchanged, only its silence. Cost is ~4 lines and one extra log import in a file that already logs elsewhere.

**Verifier corrections — these override the evidence and proposal above**

1. FALSE CROSS-HOST COUNTER-EVIDENCE. "the desktop host wires the same probe with no catch" is wrong. `packages/desktop/src/main/index.ts:917` (not :940 — the cited line 940 is inside `kickoffSetup`) passes `hasCredential: () => hasUsableSetupCredential(platform().secrets)` as a _callback_, and the consumer applies the identical mask: `packages/desktop/src/main/desktopOnboardingIpc.ts:79-83` — `const hasCredential = await Promise.resolve(options.hasCredential()).catch(() => false,);` — then feeds `planOnboardingFunnelTransition` at :84-88 exactly as the extension does. So the mask is symmetric, not an extension-only slip, and the desktop is a second instance of the same defect rather than evidence against it. A fix that touches only MainViewProvider creates cross-host divergence; the honest scope is both sites.

2. WRONG LINE. Desktop wiring is `index.ts:917`, not `:940`.

3. STALE AUDIT PINS, AND A THIRD LIVE SITE. P1.2's extension pin `packages/extension/src/extension.ts:320-349` has drifted; the live code is `extension.ts:387-409`, where `hasAnyUsableSetupCredential().catch(() => false)` sits at :394 _inside_ a try whose catch logs `Onboarding firstRunDone backfill failed: …` at warn (:405-409). The inner `.catch` pre-empts that logger, so the one place that already intends to log a credential-probe failure never sees one. Worth naming in the same fix. Also `onboardingFunnel.ts:136-159` in P1.2 no longer exists — `backfillFirstRunDone` now lives at `src/shared/state/onboardingState.ts:65`.

4. INCONSISTENT SIBLING WORTH NOTING. `packages/extension/src/extension.ts:180` (`refreshApiKeyStatus`) calls the same probe with **no** catch at all, so the identical keyring failure becomes an unhandled rejection there while it becomes a blanked launcher here. That is the real cross-host/cross-site inconsistency, and it undercuts any "the mask is deliberate policy" defense better than the (incorrect) desktop claim did.

5. LOC UNDERSTATED. `MainViewProvider.ts` currently imports no logger and no `toErrorMessage` (verified: its import block, lines 1-52, has neither), so the proposed loud fallback costs an added import plus the try/catch, not 4 lines. Desktop already has `platform()` in scope so its copy is cheaper.

6. SEVERITY FRAMING. The demoted state is not purely cosmetic but it is also not data loss: a keyring failure means the user genuinely cannot resolve a key for that session, so State 0 is a defensible _output_; the defect is strictly the silence plus the misleading "add an API key" card for a user who already has one. "low" risk is right.

<details><summary>Verifier reasoning</summary>

Verified every cited line at HEAD rather than trusting the write-up. The central claim holds exactly: `MainViewProvider.ts:209-211` swallows any credential-probe rejection into `false` with no log and no justifying comment, that value drives `deriveOnboardingFunnelState` to `'needs-credential'`, and `MainApp.ts:358-384` renders only the welcome card for that state — so a transient SecretStorage failure blanks an existing user's launcher with nothing in the log. I confirmed the throw is reachable (`resolveApiKeyUncached` awaits `secrets.get` unguarded; `isCodexSignedIn` is likewise unguarded), which rules out the "defensive wrapper around code that cannot throw" (M6) kill. The review checklist §15 classifies this as M2 silent swallow and calls an uncommented `.catch(() => …)` a blocker, and the 2026-07-12 fallback audit's P1.2 disposition ("Remove false-on-error") supports rather than settles it — its three pins are the `backfillFirstRunDone` sites, and this one is not among them, nor is it in rounds1234-index.md or any of the three survey docs. Dedupe, ruling, self-explaining-code, external-consumer and settled-surface kills all fail. The one real error is the corroborating cross-host argument: the desktop applies the identical `.catch(() => false)` at `desktopOnboardingIpc.ts:79-83`, so there is no counter-evidence and the fix must cover both hosts (plus the pre-empted logger at `extension.ts:394`). That is a correction to the evidence, not to the defect. Judged as a defect finding, it survives; net LoC is positive, which per the rules does not refute it.

</details>

### Four residues in ModelInvocationNode: two constructor writes always overwritten, two never-passed parameters, and a guard on a return value that cannot be undefined

- **Slice**: b16 · **Kind**: delete · **Risk**: low · **Net**: -9 LoC (proposer claimed -14; verifier figure governs)
- **Files**: `src/agent/core/flows/ModelInvocationNode.ts`, `src/test-kernel/agent/runtime/RetryState.vitest.ts`

**Evidence**

(1) The constructor at :188-193 sets `this.maxRetries = getNodeMaxRetries()` and `this.wait = RETRY_BACKOFF_MS/1000`; `_exec` unconditionally recomputes and reassigns both (:370-390) before the only reader, `execWithRetries` (:428,:443). Both production constructions (ResponseCycleFlow.ts:596, ToolUseRoundFlow.ts:48) go through `_exec`, so the constructor's `getValidatedConfig` read is discarded every time; the only consumer of the constructor-time values is RetryState.vitest.ts:441-445, which asserts them without running the node. (2) `rebindClient(context, signal?)` at :203-216 has one caller, :507, which passes no signal — the parameter is always `undefined`, so `modelCell.rebind(undefined, undefined)`. (3) `recordResolvedAttempt(result, attemptSource, details = {})` at :300-314 has one caller, :340, which never passes `details`. (4) :583-585 `if (!interaction) throw new Error('HostInteractions.requestRetry is required')` — `session.interactions` is a `SessionHostInteractions` (SessionHandle.ts:141,174) whose `requestRetry` (HostInteractions.ts:587-596) returns `Promise<RetryResult>` unconditionally; the optional `requestRetry?` lives on the attachment interface (:369-372) and is already defaulted inside `enqueue`. So the guard tests a value that is never falsy — error handling for a failure the call cannot produce, left over from when the manager method was optional. Dedupe: the rounds1234 index has no ModelInvocationNode/retry-node title; round-1 refuted item 'Fold three single-implementation seams in the flow kernel' covers the post-compaction hook, stampCompatibilityKey and `shouldAutoRetry` — none of the four items here — and none of the policy-protected six touches this file.

**Proposal**

Delete the two constructor assignments (keeping the field declarations, which `_exec` initializes) and adapt RetryState.vitest.ts:441-445 to read them after an `_exec` rather than after `new`; drop the unused `signal` parameter from `rebindClient` and the `details` parameter from `recordResolvedAttempt`; delete the `!interaction` guard and inline `const result = await session.interactions.requestRetry(...)`. If the manual-retry rebind should actually be abortable, wire `this.services.runScope.signal` into it instead of deleting the parameter — but decide, rather than keeping a parameter no caller fills.

**What we give up**

Nothing observable. A subclass could no longer read `maxRetries`/`wait` before its first `_exec`; only the one test does that today, and the value it reads is the same one `_exec` computes.

**Verifier corrections — these override the evidence and proposal above**

1. NET LoC OVERSTATED. Recount: item 2 = -3 (the four-line signature at :203-206 collapses to one line); item 3 = -2 (param line + `...details,`); item 4 = -4 (the three-line `if` plus folding `const interaction = ` / `const result = await interaction;` into one `const result = await session.interactions.requestRetry(`); item 1 = -2 production. That is -11 production, not -14, and item 1 then ADDS test lines. Honest total: -9 if item 1 is dropped, about -6 if all four ship.

2. ITEM 1 IS THE WEAK ONE AND ITS COST IS UNCOUNTED. `tsconfig.json:167` sets `"strict": true`, so `strictPropertyInitialization` is on: with the constructor assignments gone, `maxRetries: number` and `wait: number` (:177, :179) do not compile and must become `maxRetries!: number` / `wait!: number`. The proposal's "keeping the field declarations, which `_exec` initializes" is therefore not a no-op — it trades two initializers for two definite-assignment assertions. And "adapt RetryState.vitest.ts:441-445 to read them after an `_exec`" is not a small edit: that test constructs `new ExposedRetryNode()` with NO services (:150-157, :435), while `_exec` reads `this.services.runScope.signal` (:393) and then calls `execWithRetries` → `this.exec(prep)`, i.e. the real invoke path. The test needs services plus an `exec` short-circuit, roughly +5 lines; `getNodeMaxRetries` (:72) is module-private, so testing it directly needs a new export.

3. THE FIELD COMMENTS ARE NOT QUOTED, AND THEY ARE THE CODE-EXPLAINS-ITSELF DEFENSE FOR ITEM 1. :176-179 read "One initial attempt plus automatic retries. Re-read on every `_exec`." and "Seconds between automatic retries. Re-read on every `_exec`." The dual write is documented, not accidental. That does not make the constructor value load-bearing, but criterion 3 requires the finding to defeat the comment explicitly, and it never mentions it.

4. "THE ONLY CONSUMER OF THE CONSTRUCTOR-TIME VALUES IS RetryState.vitest.ts:441-445" — incomplete. Two other subclasses write these fields in their own constructors and then drive `execWithRetries` directly, bypassing `_exec`: `ScriptedRetryNode` (src/test-kernel/agent/PocketFlowNode.vitest.ts:78-104, `this.maxRetries = maxRetries; this.wait = 0;` at :98-99, `execWithRetries` at :103) and `RepresentativeFailingProviderNode` (src/test-kernel/cli/ApprovalAdapter.vitest.ts:445-468, :458-459, :467). Neither breaks under the change since each sets its own values, but they show the fields are a live pre-`_exec` write surface, which is exactly what makes a `!` assertion a real lie: a future direct `execWithRetries` caller that forgets to set `maxRetries` gets `runAttempts(NaN)` instead of today's settings default. Recommendation: ship items 2, 3, 4; drop item 1 or accept it knowing it is LoC-neutral.

5. `modelCell.rebind(undefined, undefined)` MISDESCRIBES THE CALL. `rebind(selection: ModelCredentialSelection = 'configured', signal?: AbortSignal)` (src/agent/runtime/ModelCell.ts:108-111) defaults the first argument, so today's call already means `rebind('configured')`, not a selection-less rebind. The edit should drop the explicit `undefined` too and become `await modelCell.rebind()`.

6. THE `signal` PARAMETER HAS AN OBVIOUS PROVENANCE THE WRITE-UP OMITS. The sibling credential path does thread a real signal: `prepareRetryForCredentialSelection` (:231-269) calls `modelCell.rebind(selection, signal)` at :238/:255/:259 and `signal.throwIfAborted()` at :266. `rebindClient`'s parameter was almost certainly copied from there. Nothing supplies one today, so the deletion stands, but "residue" undersells the symmetry a reviewer will ask about.

7. ADJACENCY WORTH FLAGGING, NOT A KILL. round3 candidate at lines 706-768 ("One policy gate for all seven request kinds") explicitly names `src/agent/core/flows/ModelInvocationNode.ts:564` — the same `handleManualRetryPrompt` body item 4 edits — and was rated risk:high. Deleting the dead guard does not conflict semantically, but if that candidate ever ships the two touch the same 20 lines.

<details><summary>Verifier reasoning</summary>

Items 2, 3 and 4 are verified dead code with single callers and no defending comment, no ratchet, no wire or settings surface, and no emitted-declaration change. Item 4 in particular is a provably unreachable error path: the run scope's `session` is typed `SessionHandle` (RunScope.ts:23), its `interactions` is `SessionHostInteractions` (SessionHandle.ts:140), and that class's `requestRetry` always returns the Promise built by `enqueue`, which itself always returns a Promise — the optional `requestRetry?` the guard was written for lives one layer down on the attachment interface and is already absorbed by `dispatch`. Item 1 is real but marginal: it saves two production lines, forces two `!` assertions under `strict: true`, and costs more test lines than it saves. The dedupe and dated-ruling checks come back clean, and every cited line number is exact. A "delete" finding that is three-quarters clean, zero-behavior-change, and net negative on LoC survives.

</details>

### Reflection debug saves overwrite each other: messages and response share one filename, and so does every round

- **Slice**: b16 · **Kind**: defect · **Risk**: low · **Net**: -8 LoC
- **Files**: `src/agent/debug/debugMessageSaver.ts`, `src/agent/core/flows/CommonCycleTypes.ts`, `src/agent/implementations/flows/reflection/ResponseCycleFlow.ts`

**Evidence**

debugMessageSaver.ts:62-69 builds the filename as `fileBase = outputFile ? path.basename(outputFile, ext) : baseName`, then `${fileBase}${modelPart}${cont}.json` — `objectType` ('messages' | 'response') never enters the name; it only colours the log line at :81. The reflection flow passes an `outputFile` from one helper for BOTH saves: ResponseCycleFlow.ts:92-100 `responseDebugFileOptions` returns `{continuationCount, baseName:'response', outputFile: shared.outputLocation.relativePath}`, used at :140-145 to save the _messages_ array and again at :609-610 (`getDebugFileOptions`) to save the _response_. That outputLocation is `workflowOutputPath({ext:'xml', round})` (runReflectionFlow.ts:175-180) = `r{N}/output.xml` (workflowOutput.ts:22,25,51), whose basename-without-extension is the constant `'output'`. So both saves in every round of every reflection run write exactly `output_<model>_cont{N}.json`: the response clobbers the messages, and round 1 clobbers round 0. Two consequences prove the intent was the opposite: (a) `baseName:'response'` at :98 is dead — the `outputFile` branch always wins; (b) the tool-use twin of this code has no `outputFile` and distinguishes the two objects by baseName instead — `'tooluse'` for messages (ToolUseRoundPrepNode.ts:85-88) vs `'tooluse_response'` for the response (ToolUseRoundFlow.ts:67-70), plus `continuationCount: run.totalRounds` so its rounds do not collide. This is the reflection copy of a two-copy pattern that drifted. Dedupe: `outputFile`/`maybeSaveDebugObject`/`saveModelIO` appear in the round-1/2/3 survey docs only in the unrelated `PRINT_INPUT_PROMPT` template-variable deletion (round2 doc:590,634,595); no rounds1234-index title touches debug file naming; `CycleDebugFileOptions` and `debugMessageSaver` are absent from the shipped/refuted/keep lists.

**Proposal**

Delete the `outputFile` option from `DebugSaveOptions` (debugMessageSaver.ts:21) and `CycleDebugFileOptions` (CommonCycleTypes.ts:87-91) along with the `fileBase` ternary at :62-64, leaving `baseName` as the only naming input — the shape the tool-use path already uses correctly. Then have `responseDebugFileOptions` take the object kind (or have the two call sites build their own literal, as ToolUseRoundPrepNode/ToolUseRoundFlow do) and return a round-qualified name, e.g. `baseName: `r${roundIndex}_messages`` / `r${roundIndex}_response``, so the reflection flow gets one file per round per object instead of one file per continuation index for the whole run.

**What we give up**

Debug filenames change (they stop being named after the output document). Nothing reads these files programmatically — they exist only for `texra.debug.saveModelIO` inspection — and the current name carries no information anyway, since the basename is the literal constant 'output' for every workflow run.

**Verifier corrections — these override the evidence and proposal above**

1. PATH WRONG. ToolUseRoundPrepNode is at src/agent/implementations/flows/tooluse/toolUseRound/ToolUseRoundPrepNode.ts (extra `toolUseRound/` segment); the cited lines 85-88 are correct.

2. "`objectType` never enters the name" is imprecise. It is the `baseName` default at debugMessageSaver.ts:60 (`baseName = objectType`), so it _is_ the name for any caller that passes neither `outputFile` nor `baseName` — which is what the module test exercises (writes `response.json`). It is inert only for the reflection path, which supplies both. The precise statement is "the reflection path never lets objectType reach the name."

3. THE FINDING OMITS THE IN-CODE COMMENT IT MUST DEFEAT (kill criterion 3). ResponseCycleFlow.ts:87-90 says the two saves "must land on the same base name and round." Any PR must quote it, explain that it justifies a shared identity rather than a shared _file_, and delete or rewrite it — leaving it in place next to a name that now differs by object kind would re-create the drift.

4. THE COMMENT'S "and round" IS ALREADY FALSE TODAY, which strengthens the finding: nothing in the filename encodes the round. `continuationCount` is not the round index — it is per-round state reset to 0 every round (PrepareContextNode.ts:36-37 + AgentState.ts:13 `.prefault(0)`), which is precisely why round N clobbers round N-1.

5. LoC ACCOUNTING NOT SHOWN. The claimed -8 is only reachable if `responseDebugFileOptions` and its 4-line doc comment are deleted outright and the two call sites inline their own literal (the ToolUse shape). Once `outputFile` goes, `shared` is the helper's only remaining unused parameter, so inlining is the right move: -15 (helper + comment) +6 (two 3-line inline literals) -3 (debugMessageSaver `fileBase` ternary collapses into the template) -1 (CommonCycleTypes.ts:90) -1 (DebugSaveOptions.outputFile) ≈ -14 gross, call it -8 after prettier re-wrapping and the round-index plumbing. Keeping the helper instead yields roughly -5.

6. "one file per continuation index for the whole run" (the Give-up section) understates it slightly: it is one file per _distinct continuation index_ per run, and since continuationCount resets per round, in the common no-continuation case that is literally one file for the entire run, holding only the last round's response.

<details><summary>Verifier reasoning</summary>

This is a genuine defect, verified from source rather than from the finding's quotes. `texra.debug.saveModelIO` documents itself as persisting both what is sent to and what is received from the model, and in the reflection flow it persists neither reliably: the response overwrites the request messages within a cycle, and each round overwrites the previous one, so a multi-round reflection run leaves exactly one `output_<model>.json` containing the last response. The tool-use flow, which shares `saveCycleDebug` and `maybeSaveDebugObject`, gets this right by distinguishing the two objects via `baseName` and keying on a monotonically increasing counter — so this is one copy of a two-copy pattern that drifted, exactly as claimed. The `outputFile` option is what causes it: it is optional, has one production caller, and the value it derives from is the fixed literal `'output'` for every workflow run, so it contributes zero information while suppressing the `baseName` the caller actually set. Deleting it is both the fix and a small net deletion. The one substantive gap in the finding is that it never confronts the ResponseCycleFlow.ts:87-90 comment asserting the two saves "must land on the same base name and round"; I checked that comment against the module docstring and against what the name actually encodes (nothing about the round) and it does not survive as a justification — it explains why the helper is shared, not why the response should destroy the request. Risk is low: no ratchet, no wire contract, no persisted user data, no settings-key change, and the sole test on the module does not exercise the option.

</details>

### OutputNode's base-file existence probe also suppresses between-round latexdiff, which does not use base files

- **Slice**: b16 · **Kind**: defect · **Risk**: medium · **Net**: -8 LoC (proposer claimed -10; verifier figure governs)
- **Files**: `src/agent/implementations/flows/reflection/nodes/OutputNode.ts`, `src/agent/implementations/flows/reflection/output/LatexDiffManager.ts`

**Evidence**

OutputNode.ts:313-330 `handleLatexdiff` probes `AbsoluteFS.exists` over the diff base files and, when none exists, logs 'No base files found for latexdiff' at debug and returns `[]` — never calling `diffManager.handleLatexdiffOfOutput`. But that callee does two independent things (LatexDiffManager.ts:173-243): the `isRewrite` branch (:173-199) diffs each output against `entry.base`, and the `generateBetweenRoundDiffs` branch (:205-238) diffs each output against `entry.prev` — the previous round's output. `entry.prev` is built in lineageMapping.ts:112-120 from `state.rounds.get(currRound-1).outputs`, with no reference to baseFiles at all. In runReflectionFlow.ts:142-144 `baseFiles` is `config.outputFiles.length > 0 ? config.outputFiles : config.inputFiles`; for a create-new workflow the declared output files do not exist in the workspace before the run, so `existingBase.some(Boolean)` is false and the between-round diffs a user explicitly enabled (`texra.latexdiff.generateBetweenRoundDiffs`, default false — latexConfig.ts:44) silently never run, on any round. The guard is also redundant for the branch it was written for: with no base files, `traceFileLineage` sets no `entry.base`, so `collectPairs(entry => entry.base)` is empty and the rewrite branch is already a no-op; LatexDiffManager.ts:269-273 even guards its own 'no mappings' log on `this.baseFiles.length > 0`, acknowledging the empty case. Nothing in either file comments on why the probe gates both branches. Dedupe: no latexdiff title in the rounds1234 index; the only latexdiff mentions in the three survey docs are the mathMarkup type-owner refutation (round2:3397-3409), the `runDiffBetweenRounds` rounds-argument row inside issue #8913 (round2:2232,2275 — an argument-passing cleanup in src/latex/latexdiff, not this gate), and unrelated dead-export/exec lists.

**Proposal**

Move the existence probe inside the `isRewrite` branch of `handleLatexdiffOfOutput` (or drop it and let that branch's own empty-pair path handle it), so the between-round branch is reached whenever the setting is on and a previous round produced outputs. While there, delete the outer `tryOperation(..., this.recoverWarn('Latexdiff'))` wrapper at OutputNode.ts:113-121: `handleLatexdiffOfOutput` already wraps its entire body in `tryOperation` with `recover: () => []` (LatexDiffManager.ts:257-262), so the outer layer is a second catch over the same operation that only ever sees the probe's own failures, and the two disagree on severity (warn vs error). That leaves `handleLatexdiff` as a direct call and lets the `AbsoluteFS` import leave OutputNode.

**What we give up**

Create-new workflows with the between-rounds setting enabled now pay a `checkToolInstalled('latexdiff')` probe and the round-dir mirroring in `handleLatexdiffOfOutput` before discovering there is nothing to diff on round 0 (`currRound > 0` still gates the loop). If the isRewrite branch keeps the probe, no new latexdiff warnings appear for missing bases.

**Verifier corrections — these override the evidence and proposal above**

1. WRONG: "The guard is also redundant for the branch it was written for: with no base files, traceFileLineage sets no entry.base, so collectPairs(entry => entry.base) is empty and the rewrite branch is already a no-op." That holds only when `baseFiles` is _empty_. The case the probe actually fires on is base files that are _declared but missing on disk_, and there `traceFileLineage` still populates `entry.base`: `findMatchingBaseFile(baseEntries, entry.source)` and `createFileMapping(baseFiles, currentLocations, 'contains')` (lineageMapping.ts:99-131) are pure path/name matching with no filesystem check, and for paper2slide the output is literally named `slides.tex`, matching the missing base. `isRewrite` defaults to `true` (AgentDataclass.ts:42) and no shipped agent YAML overrides it. So the "or drop it and let that branch's own empty-pair path handle it" half of the proposal is unsafe — it would send latexdiff at a nonexistent base file on every such run and produce exactly the failure noise the probe suppresses. Only the "move it into the isRewrite branch" variant is correct, and the most accurate transplant is a per-pair existence filter on `entry.base`, not a whole-list `some()`.

2. IMPRECISE: "for a create-new workflow the declared output files do not exist in the workspace before the run." In the extension the output list is populated by an open dialog (`selectOutputFiles` = `createMultiPicker`, fileSelectionCommands.ts:105-109), which can only pick existing files, and the delegation tool's field says "Must be a subset of input files. Never create new files or change format" (inputFields.ts:93-98). The real, verifiable trigger is agent-declared `defaultOutputFiles`, which `resolveOutputFiles` writes into `agentConfig.outputFiles` (userVars.ts:546-548) — paper2slide, paper2poster, ocr, transcribe_audio. Plus the zero-base-file case (`inputFiles` and `outputFiles` both empty), where `[].some(Boolean)` is also false. The finding should name those four agents; as written it reads as speculative when it is not.

3. MISSING CONTEXT (severity): a separate, host-specific path still honors the setting — the extension's manual latexdiff command reads `LATEXDIFF_BETWEEN_ROUNDS` and passes it to `runLatexdiffForExecution` over the stored per-round outputs (latexdiffCommands.ts:393-419), independent of base-file existence. A user can recover the missing between-round diffs after the run in VS Code, but not in the CLI or desktop, and not automatically anywhere. That mitigation belongs in the write-up.

4. MISSING DETAIL for the transplant: `LatexDiffManager.baseFiles` (constructed at runReflectionFlow.ts:150-157 from the raw `baseFiles`) is NOT the same list OutputNode probes. OutputNode probes `diffBaseFiles`, the snapshot-resolved list from `resolveBaseFilesForDiff`. Moving the probe verbatim into the manager would change which paths are tested. Filtering on the mapping's `entry.base` locations sidesteps this.

5. CORRECT and confirmed: the outer `tryOperation` at OutputNode.ts:113-121 is genuinely dead once the probe moves — `handleLatexdiffOfOutput` wraps its entire body in `tryOperation` with `recover: () => []` (LatexDiffManager.ts:257-262), and `tryOperation` (outputOperations.ts:42-49) catches everything the operation throws; the only other statement in the outer callback is an array `push`. The severity disagreement the finding notes is real (`level: 'error'` inside vs `recoverWarn`'s `'warn'` outside).

6. LoC: -10 is optimistic once the per-pair existence filter is written honestly. Deleting `handleLatexdiff` plus the `AbsoluteFS` import removes ~19 lines from OutputNode and ~5 more from collapsing the outer wrapper; the filter inside the isRewrite branch adds ~10-14. Honest net ≈ -8.

<details><summary>Verifier reasoning</summary>

The mechanism is verified end to end. `handleLatexdiff` (OutputNode.ts:321-327) short-circuits the entire `handleLatexdiffOfOutput` call on a base-file existence test, but that callee runs two independent branches, and the second one (LatexDiffManager.ts:205-238) diffs round N against round N-1 using `entry.prev`, which lineageMapping.ts builds solely from the previous round's outputs (:96-97, :112-120) with no reference to base files. So a user-enabled setting is silently disabled by a condition unrelated to it, logged only at `debug` — the repo's "silent degradation is a defect" rule (CLAUDE.md, review-checklist §15) names exactly this shape. The trigger is not hypothetical: four shipped agents declare `defaultOutputFiles` naming files that cannot exist before the run, and `resolveOutputFiles` promotes those into `config.outputFiles`, which becomes `baseFiles`. Dedupe, ruling, self-documentation, external-contract, and settled-surface checks all came back clean, and I re-read every cited line. The one genuine error is the finding's claim that the probe is redundant for the rewrite branch — it is not, because name-based lineage matching happily pairs a missing base with a same-named output and `isRewrite` defaults to true — which invalidates the "just delete it" option but not the defect or the "move it into the isRewrite branch" fix.

</details>

schemas.ts:4-6 says the `ExportNode` IR is 'consumed by every renderer (markdown, LaTeX, HTML)' and :48-52 repeats the framing; normalizeConversation.ts:410-411 says the nodes 'are consumed by every format renderer (markdown, LaTeX, HTML)'. **Verifier corrections — these override the evidence and proposal above**

1. THE THIRD SITE IS MISCITED — schemas.ts:48-52 does NOT repeat the framing. A GOOD MODEL COMMENT TO COPY: packages/cli/src/runtime/history.ts:254-255 already words this correctly — "the {@link ChatExportInput} the markdown export formatter consumes (the HTML export path uses `assembleTrace` instead — see `commands/history.ts`)". Reuse that phrasing rather than inventing new wording, and mind that this file's formatter also emits LaTeX, which the CLI comment omits because the CLI only offers md.

7. THE SECONDARY re-export CLAIM IS CORRECT BUT WEAKER THAN PITCHED. chatExportFormatter.ts:26 `export type { ChatExportInput } from '@agent/export/schemas';` does have exactly one consumer, chatExportFormatter.vitest.ts:8-12, which pulls it alongside formatChatAsMarkdown/formatChatAsLatex from the same specifier. But it is NOT in knip-baseline.json, so no ratchet row shrinks and there is no dead-code-gate pressure to remove it; and dropping it forces the test into two import statements from two specifiers, which is worse-reading, not better. Treat it as optional and drop it from the PR if the diff gets any wider than three comment edits.

<details><summary>Verifier reasoning</summary>

The load-bearing claim is verified twice over: the comments promise an HTML renderer over ExportNode, and no such renderer exists — only two FormatSpec values in the repo, zero ExportNode/FormatSpec code references outside src/agent/export, and both HTML export paths (extension controller and CLI) demonstrably go through assembleTrace + the trace-viewer standalone bundle instead. ChatExportController.ts:151-154 names the retired hand-written chat-bubble exporter explicitly, which is exactly the third renderer these comments still advertise, so the finding defeats the only self-explaining comment in the neighborhood rather than tripping over it. That is a genuine stale-doc defect: a reader adding a block type is told to add "one entry per renderer table" for a table that does not exist, and the loadChatExportInput.ts:7 wording would send them looking for an HTML formatter that consumes ChatExportInput. Judged as a defect, it survives regardless of profit. The misread at schemas.ts:48-52 is real and I would normally weigh criterion 6 heavily, but it lands on one of three enumerated sites while the two verbatim-quoted ones are exact, and the miss is compensated by a stale site the finding overlooked entirely — so the amend's scope is unchanged in size even though its file list changes. The claimed -3 LoC is not defensible: removing the substring ", HTML" from three comment lines deletes characters, not lines, and no paragraph rewraps into a shorter comment; the optional re-export removal buys one line back and the test-side import split spends it again. Honest netLoc is 0. Risk is low — comments only, no ratchet row, no wire or persisted surface, and merged precedent (#10700) for exactly this kind of correction in this exact file.

</details>

### ToolUseRunShared.lastResponse has been write-only since #9560 — persisted on every cycle, read by nobody

- **Slice**: b17 · **Kind**: delete · **Risk**: low · **Net**: -16 LoC (proposer claimed -8; verifier figure governs)
- **Files**: `src/agent/implementations/flows/tooluse/nodes/types.ts`, `src/agent/implementations/flows/tooluse/nodes/ToolUseCycleNode.ts`

**Evidence**

`ToolUseRunSharedSchema.lastResponse` (types.ts:64-65, doc: "Last assistant response without the full assembly buffers") has exactly one writer, `ToolUseCycleNode.post` at ToolUseCycleNode.ts:219, and zero readers. A whole-repo grep for `lastResponse` (excluding `assembly.lastResponse`, `cycleStartLastResponse`, node_modules and dist) returns only: the write at ToolUseCycleNode.ts:219; the WaitNode's local of the same name (ToolUseWaitNode.ts:19/39-51/93), which is derived independently by walking `shared.messages` with `modelHandler.extractAssistantText` and never reads `shared.lastResponse`; the reflection cycle's unrelated `ProcessPrepResult.lastResponse` (ResponseCycleFlow.ts:160,300); and the `onIdle` callback parameter names. There is no string-key access either — `grep "'lastResponse'"` / `"lastResponse"` / `[...]` indexing returns nothing.

The last production reader was deleted deliberately: `git show c4698ecd47` (#9560, 2026-08-01, "contain stale tool-use resume results") removes `shared.lastResponse ||` from runToolUseFlow's result assembly, after which `RunToolUseFlowResult.response` comes only from the `onCycleResponse` closure (runToolUseFlow.ts:224, 247-249, 692). #9658 then hardened that rule, and SessionResumeRetrieval.vitest.ts:812-829 now asserts the opposite of a read: a resumed cycle that produces no new text must report `response: undefined` even though the persisted record carries `lastResponse: 'A'`. The remaining mentions in test-kernel (ToolUseProgressEvents.vitest.ts:298/343/361, SessionResumeRetrieval fixtures at :276/:1178) only pin the write.

Safe on the persisted-data axis in both directions: the field is `.optional()` in `ToolUseRunSharedSchema`, and that schema (parsed once via `parseToolUseShared`, types.ts:130-134) is the single boundary for the flow record — an old record carrying the key still parses after removal, and an older build reading a new record without it also parses. Dedupe: no entry in rounds1234-index.md and no hit for `lastResponse` in the four survey docs.

**Proposal**

Delete the `lastResponse` field from `ToolUseRunSharedSchema` (types.ts:64-65) and the `shared.lastResponse = cycleResponse;` write at ToolUseCycleNode.ts:219, keeping the `onCycleResponse` call on the next line (that is the live path). Drop the three `expect(shared.lastResponse)` assertions in ToolUseProgressEvents.vitest.ts and the two fixture fields — per Testing discipline, tests pinning retired state go with it; the surrounding cases that assert `result.response` stay.

**What we give up**

A persisted breadcrumb that a future feature might have wanted ("what did the last cycle answer"). It is recoverable from `shared.messages` exactly the way `ToolUseWaitNode.prep` already recovers it, which is also the only correct source across a resume — the current write stores `undefined` on every skipped (i.e. resumed) cycle anyway.

**Verifier corrections — these override the evidence and proposal above**

1. Omits the strongest adjacent fact a reviewer will raise: `continuationGenerationId` (types.ts:47-48) is an explicitly retained write-only field in the same schema. The PR body must state why the precedent does not extend (that field is required, `lastResponse` is `.optional()`), and must NOT delete or "tidy" `continuationGenerationId` in the same pass.

2. Omits the governing dated ruling on this schema's persisted shape: types.ts:31-43, decision #10641 (referenced from docs/proposals/2026-08-14-delegation-flow-substrate-consolidation.md:439). It permits the removal but should be cited rather than left for a reviewer to find.

3. netLoc understated. Removing the field kills more of the test scaffolding than the three assertions and two fixtures listed: `runCyclePost`'s `sharedLastResponse?: string` option (ToolUseProgressEvents.vitest.ts:118), the ternary that seeds it (:131-135, collapsing 4 lines to 1), and the `sharedLastResponse` rows in the `it.each` type and table (~:311-313, :317, :322) all die with it, plus three `{ onCycleResponse, shared }` destructures shrink. Real net is about -16, not -8.

4. Minor incompleteness: reflection's unrelated `lastResponse` also appears at ResponseCycleFlow.ts:220 and :356 (the latter is `assembly.lastResponse`), not only :160/:300.

5. The downgrade-safety argument can be stated harder than "it parses": no build since #9560 (2026-08-01) reads the field at all, and a pre-#9560 build reading a record that lacks it falls through to `undefined` — precisely the behavior #9560 shipped. There is no downgrade hazard, not merely a tolerable one.

6. Grammar of the claim: the field is not "persisted on every cycle" so much as _overwritten_ on every cycle, including being cleared to `undefined` on every skipped (resumed) cycle — which the finding does note under "Give up" and is correct.

<details><summary>Verifier reasoning</summary>

Verified at HEAD: exactly one writer (ToolUseCycleNode.ts:219), zero readers anywhere in src/ or packages/ (no string-key or index access either), and the last production reader was removed deliberately by #9560 as a stale-result bug fix, with SessionResumeRetrieval.vitest.ts:808-830 now pinning the opposite behavior. The field is `.optional()` on both sides of the single persisted parse boundary (`parseToolUseShared`), so neither an old record on a new build nor a new record on an old build breaks. The one guard that could have killed it — the retained write-only `continuationGenerationId` two lines above — is distinguishable because that field is required. Dedupe, ruling, wire-contract and ratchet checks all come back empty. Survives; net win is modestly larger than claimed once the dead test scaffolding goes with it.

</details>

### Three orphaned parameters in the reflection output pipeline, one of them a leftover from #11184's own cleanup

- **Slice**: b17 · **Kind**: delete · **Risk**: low · **Net**: -10 LoC (proposer claimed -12; verifier figure governs)
- **Files**: `src/agent/implementations/flows/reflection/output/roundSummary.ts`, `src/agent/implementations/flows/reflection/output/snapshotResolution.ts`, `src/agent/implementations/flows/reflection/output/outputFileExtraction.ts`, `src/agent/implementations/flows/reflection/nodes/OutputNode.ts`, `src/agent/implementations/flows/reflection/output/diffComputation.ts`

(b) `resolveBaseFilesForDiff(baseFiles, executionId)` (snapshotResolution.ts:18-22) types the second parameter `ExecutionId | undefined` and early-returns unchanged when it is undefined (:22). (c) `prepareRunWorkspaceIfNeeded(state, deps)` (outputFileExtraction.ts:32-40) never references `deps`; the body only awaits and nulls `state.runPreparation`. Its one caller is :142.

Dedupe: rounds1234-index.md has no entry for any of the three; the round-1 survey doc mentions `prepareRunWorkspaceIfNeeded` only in passing inside the shipped `processMultipleOutputs` fold (docs/proposals/2026-08-25-simplification-survey-49-candidates.md:955), and never touches its signature.
