```
tikzEnvironments.reduce((content, env, i) => content.replace(`__TIKZ_PLACEHOLDER_${i}__`, env), processedContent)
```

`String.prototype.replace` applies `$`-substitution to a string replaceValue regardless of whether searchValue is a string or a RegExp, so any `$`-sigil pair inside the stashed environment is interpreted: `$&` -> the matched substring (the placeholder itself), `$$` -> `$`, `` $` `` -> text before the match, `$'` -> text after the match. TikZ bodies routinely contain `$…$` math next to `&` column separators (`\matrix{$a$&$b$};`).
Reproduced: `'pre __TIKZ_PLACEHOLDER_0__ post'.replace('__TIKZ_PLACEHOLDER_0__', '\\begin{tikzpicture}\\matrix{$a$&$b$};\\end{tikzpicture}')` yields `\matrix{$a__TIKZ_PLACEHOLDER_0__$b$}` — the placeholder text is left in the user's .tex, and since restoration is the last step of the block callback, no later pass removes it. The callback form `() => env` produces the correct output.
This runs on the default path: applyLatexQuotesFormatting is one of the three unconditional cleanup passes in applyReplacements (src/replacement/engine.ts:316-320, `cleanupPasses !== false`), and applyAllPolicy's final pass leaves them on.
Second, smaller drift in the same function: the doc comment at :14 says quoted text "between 3 and 15 characters long", but the regex at :62 is `{3,16}`.
Dedupe: no rounds1-4 entry names advanced.ts or the tikz placeholder; the survey doc does not cite this file.

**Proposal**

Change the reduce body to `content.replace(`__TIKZ_PLACEHOLDER_${i}__`, () => env)` (function replaceValue disables `$`-substitution). Same one-character-class fix pattern applies nowhere else in the file — :48 and :61 already use function replacers. Correct the `3 and 15` comment to 16 while touching the function.

**What we give up**

Nothing. The `$`-substitution was never intended; the callback form is the standard escape and costs nothing.

**Verifier corrections — these override the evidence and proposal above**

1. NET LoC IS NOT 0. Line 77 is 79 characters; inserting `() => ` makes it 85, past prettier's 80-column print width, so the reduce callback reformats onto two lines. Honest net is +1, not 0. (Irrelevant to a defect verdict, but the stated number is wrong.)
2. "TikZ bodies routinely contain `$…$` math next to `&` column separators" overstates the trigger. Only four sigil pairs are dangerous with a string searchValue — `$$`, `$&`, `` $` ``, `$'` — and they require _immediate_ adjacency. The idiomatic `\matrix{ $a$ & $b$ \\ };` (spaces around `&`) is safe; only the unspaced `$a$&$b$` form corrupts. `$1`/`$<name>` are left literal because a string searchValue has no captures. The defect is real but the trigger is narrower than "routinely".
3. The finding omits the fast-path gate at advanced.ts:23-26: the function returns early unless the text contains BOTH `\begin{document}` and a literal `"`. So corruption fires only on documents that carry a raw double quote somewhere — not on every `.tex` write. That gate does not save the case (a raw `"` anywhere in a document containing a tikzpicture is enough, and the tikz body itself need not contain the quote), but "runs on the default path" should read "runs on the default path whenever the text has a `\begin{document}` block and any `\"`".
4. "Same one-character-class fix pattern applies nowhere else in the file" is true for advanced.ts, but the same class of hazard exists structurally one file over at engine.ts:306, `result = result.replaceAll(old, newText)` for non-regex rule tables (string search + string replaceValue → `$`-substitution on the rule's replacement text). I audited the rule tables: no value today contains `$$`, `$&`, `` $` `` or `$'` (rules.ts:725 `'.$': '$.'` is a false positive — `$.` is not a sigil), so there is no live bug there, but a future rule whose replacement ends in `$` followed by `$`/`&`/`` ` ``/`'` would hit it silently.
5. Risk is low, not medium: the change is semantics-preserving for every input that contains no sigil pair, no test pins the current output, and the only behavior difference is that stashed tikz bodies come back verbatim.

<details><summary>Verifier reasoning</summary>

I reproduced the corruption in node rather than reasoning about the spec, re-read all cited lines (advanced.ts:14, :44-79, engine.ts:63-75, :306-312), and traced the call path to a real user-visible sink (`WriteTool.ts:42` via `applyFor('tex-write')` → `applyAllPolicy` → final `applyReplacements` with cleanup passes on). The output keeps a `__TIKZ_PLACEHOLDER_0__` token inside the user's `.tex` and drops part of the tikz body — silent data corruption of authored content, which is exactly the "silent degradation is a defect" class in CLAUDE.md. Dedupe, ruling, self-explaining-code, external-consumer, and settled-surface checks all came back clean. The fix (`() => env`) is the standard escape, matches the callback form already used at :50 and :63, and breaks no test.

</details>

### openTexraWorkspaceConfigStore falls back to the internal config store silently for the exact case it computes — a read-only project — contradicting its own contract

- **Slice**: b27 · **Kind**: amend · **Risk**: low · **Net**: 4 LoC (proposer claimed 3; verifier figure governs)
- **Files**: `src/platform/defaults/nodeStores.ts`

**Evidence**

The function's contract (src/platform/defaults/nodeStores.ts:57-69) is explicit: "`warn` reports why the project store could not be used: falling back to the internal store is a degradation, so every host says so out loud rather than swallowing the cause", and it names three degraded cases including "read-only projects without an existing config".
The body only warns from the `catch` (:85-89), which fires when `JsonStore.open` throws (malformed JSON, unreadable file). The read-only case is decided by the `if` at :79-83: when `projectStore.keys().length === 0` and `canCreateOrWrite(projectConfigPath)` is false, control falls THROUGH the try block to :91 and opens the internal store with no warn call on any path. `canCreateOrWrite` (:41-55) exists solely to detect that case, and it deliberately returns false rather than throwing ("Answers false for e.g. a read-only checkout without ever creating the directory").
User-visible effect: on a read-only or non-writable checkout the user changes a project setting, it is written to `<storage>/config.json` instead of `<workspace>/.texra/config.json`, and no host says why — the same silent-degradation shape CLAUDE.md's "Silent degradation is a defect" rule and review-checklist §15 name. All three hosts pass a real warn sink: packages/extension/src/frontend/vscode/texraConfig.ts:107, packages/desktop/src/main/platform/index.ts:78, packages/cli/src/runtime/initPlatform.ts:250.
Dedupe: round 3 item 180 retired the in-place workspace-storage transition and round 4B fixed four stale transition comments; neither touches this function. No rounds1-4 title mentions nodeStores or the project config store. This is an amend (make the fallback loud), not a deletion.

**Proposal**

Move the fallback into an explicit branch: when the project store opens but is empty and not writable, call `warn(`Project .texra/config.json is not writable (${projectConfigPath}); using the internal workspace config store.`)` before falling through. Three added lines, no behavior change beyond the message.

**What we give up**

One extra startup warning line for genuinely read-only checkouts (CI containers mounting the repo read-only). That is the point of the contract, and it fires once per host start.

**Verifier corrections — these override the evidence and proposal above**

1. Extension line reference is stale. The finding cites `packages/extension/src/frontend/vscode/texraConfig.ts:107` as the extension's warn sink. That line no longer exists — e9ceffbd62 (#11452) retired the workspace-storage transition and shrank the file to ~32 lines. Current: the call is at texraConfig.ts:22 and the sink `(message) => log.warn(message)` at :25.

2. Desktop and CLI cites are the call lines, not the sinks. `packages/desktop/src/main/platform/index.ts:78` is the `openTexraConfigStores(` call; the sink `(message) => console.warn(\`[desktop] ${message}\`)` is at :81. `packages/cli/src/runtime/initPlatform.ts:250` is the call; the sink argument `showPersistentConfigWarning` is at :253, defined at :73-75 (`writeTextStderr(\`[warn] [cli.config] ${message}\`)`). The substantive claim — all three hosts pass a real warn sink — is correct.

3. The "contradicts its own contract" framing is stronger than the doc-comment strictly supports. Paragraph two lists three fallback cases, and the first of them — "Sessions without a workspace" — also reaches :91 without a warn, and obviously should not warn (there is no project to degrade from). So the comment's list is a list of fallback causes, not a per-case warn obligation. The load-bearing ground is narrower but still holds: paragraph one's "every host says so out loud rather than swallowing the cause" plus CLAUDE.md's silent-degradation rule, applied to the one case `canCreateOrWrite` was written to detect. Fix the wording when filing; do not lean on "the contract names three cases".

4. The gap is inherited, not a regression from the consolidation. The pre-consolidation extension copy (`openWorkspaceConfigStore`, deleted in aaf6eefa2b) had the same warn-only-in-catch structure, and the desktop copy matched it. Worth stating so the item is not mis-filed as a #11452 or aaf6eefa2b regression.

5. Adjacent case the finding does not claim and should not silently absorb: when the project config exists (`keys().length > 0`) but the directory is unwritable, the project store is returned and the failure surfaces later at `flush()`. That is a different path with a different owner; keep it out of scope.

6. Claimed net 3 LoC is one line light; prettier puts the template literal on its own line, giving +4.

<details><summary>Verifier reasoning</summary>

I read the full target file rather than trusting the excerpt, and the structural claim holds exactly: the sole `warn` call sits inside the `catch` (:85-89), while the empty-and-unwritable decision is made by the `if` at :79-84, which has no `else` and falls through to the internal-store open at :91-93. `canCreateOrWrite` (:41-55) exists only to compute that condition and deliberately returns `false` instead of throwing, so it can never route into the catch. Git archaeology (aaf6eefa2b, the C4 consolidation) shows both GUI hosts carried the same warn-only-in-catch shape before the fold, so the gap is real and long-standing rather than a misread of a transitional state. The dated material I could find — C4's "+1 missing degradation path", the commit's "The degradation stays loud", and the CLI call-site comment naming "or its directory cannot be written" as a fallback cause — all argue for the fix rather than against it. No index title, survey entry, ratchet, wire contract, or settings key is crossed. Judged as a defect, it survives at +4 LoC; the corrections are line-number drift in the host cites and an over-strong reading of the doc comment's three-case list.

</details>

### SortableController destroys the Sortable it just created on the first host update — Lit runs hostUpdated() before the element's updated()

- **Slice**: b28 · **Kind**: defect · **Risk**: low · **Net**: -30 LoC (proposer claimed -22; verifier figure governs)
- **Files**: `src/shared/litControllers/SortableController.ts`, `packages/extension/src/webview/frontend/components/FileSelectGroup.ts`

**Evidence**

`SortableController.hostUpdated()` calls `initialize()` (src/shared/litControllers/SortableController.ts:64-66), which creates the Sortable. Its only consumer, `FileSelectGroup`, overrides `updated()` and calls `reinitialize()` whenever `changedProps.has('config')` (packages/extension/src/webview/frontend/components/FileSelectGroup.ts:82-85). `reinitialize()` only destroys — the comment at SortableController.ts:78 says "Will be initialized on next hostUpdated call".

Lit's order is fixed: `@lit/reactive-element` runs `this.__controllers?.forEach((c) => c.hostUpdated?.())` at reactive-element.js:941 and `this.updated(changedProperties)` at :946. So controllers run FIRST. `config` is a property binding from the parent (`.config=${config}` at packages/extension/src/webview/frontend/MainApp.ts:509), so it is present in `changedProperties` on the very first update. Sequence on first render: hostUpdated → new Sortable → updated → reinitialize → destroy → `this.sortable = null`. The list is not draggable until some unrelated re-render triggers another host update.

The trigger is also pointless: `FILE_SELECT_CONFIGS` is a module-level constant array (packages/extension/src/webview/frontend/store.ts:142), so element identities are stable and `config` changes exactly once, at first bind. And nothing in `FileSelectConfig` can affect the Sortable — the only Sortable option is `animation` (SortableController.ts:88), the element and items come from live getters (`getElement`/`getItems`, :53-54), and `SortableControllerConfig` (:5-8) is never passed by the one call site (FileSelectGroup.ts:69-79 supplies four arguments, not five), so `animation` is always the 150 default.

This defeats the comment at SortableController.ts:72-75 ("Force reinitialization of Sortable (e.g., when config changes). Call this from the host's updated() when relevant properties change"): there is no Sortable-relevant property to change, and calling it from `updated()` is exactly the ordering that breaks it.

Dedupe: no SortableController / lit-controller entry in the rounds 1-4 index; grepped the four survey docs for SortableController, reinitialize, and FileSelectGroup — no hits.

**Proposal**

Delete `reinitialize()` and `FileSelectGroup`'s `updated()` override, leaving `hostUpdated()`'s idempotent `initialize()` as the single owner of the Sortable's lifecycle. Delete `SortableControllerConfig`, the `config` constructor parameter, and the `Required<SortableControllerConfig>` field, inlining `animation: 150` at the `new Sortable(...)` site. If a future host ever swaps the list element, the right fix is a `this.sortable.el !== element` check inside `initialize()`, not a caller-driven destroy.

**What we give up**

Nothing: a host that genuinely needs to rebind can get an identity check inside `initialize()`. We give up a configurable `animation` value no caller ever set.

**Verifier corrections — these override the evidence and proposal above**

1. THE STATED SYMPTOM IS WRONG, AND THE REAL ONE IS WORSE. "The list is not draggable until some unrelated re-render" does not follow, because drag-reorder is inert regardless. `getElement()` is `@query('.multiple-files-list')` (FileSelectGroup.ts:62-63), i.e. the wrapper at render() line 442, but `renderFileList()` (:270-363) wraps every row in a single `<div role="list">` (:276). sortablejs defaults `draggable` to `'>*'` (node_modules/sortablejs/modular/sortable.core.esm.js:1070), so the Sortable instance has exactly one draggable child and can never produce a reorder. That `role="list"` wrapper landed in e5e32fefae (UI design-review checkpoint), after the controller was wired. So the honest impact statement is: the ordering bug is real and the create/destroy churn is real, but no user has lost a drag to it — the Sortable path as a whole is currently dead, and the keyboard move buttons (:117-134, whose own comment calls itself the "counterpart to Sortable drag reordering") are the only working reorder. This does not kill the finding, but it changes the disposition: the choice is between fixing the target element and deleting the Sortable integration, and the proposal as written silently locks in the broken-drag status quo.

2. "config changes exactly once, at first bind" is too weak. `repeat` is keyed by `config.type` (MainApp.ts:505-506) over `visibleFileConfigs`, which is `FILE_SELECT_CONFIGS.filter(...)` when the session type is tool-use (MainApp.ts:391-393). Toggling session type destroys the input/context `<file-select-group>` elements and recreates them later, so a fresh element with a fresh controller repeats the create-then-destroy on its own first update. The bug fires once per element instantiation, not once per webview load — and the recreated element renders an already-populated list, which is the only path where the window is user-visible.

3. "SortableControllerConfig (:5-8)" — the interface spans :5-8 but the deletable block is :5-9 including the trailing blank; minor, but it feeds the LoC count.

4. The finding omits that `FileSelectGroup.updated()` never calls `super.updated()`. Harmless (LitElement's is a no-op) and it disappears with the override, but it should be stated since the override is being deleted rather than corrected.

5. Claimed -22 is understated. Actual deletions: SortableController.ts interface block (:5-9, 5), jsdoc example (:40-44, 5), field (:49, 1), ctor param (:56, 1), config assignment (:58-60, 3), reinitialize + jsdoc + leading blank (:71-79, 9) = 24; FileSelectGroup.ts:82-87 (override + blank) = 6. Total ~-30, with `animation: this.config.animation` -> `animation: 150` at :88 net zero.

<details><summary>Verifier reasoning</summary>

The mechanism is verifiable from source, not from memory of Lit's docs, and I checked the installed 2.1.2 build: hostUpdated at reactive-element.js:941 precedes updated at :946, and performUpdate populates changedProperties from the replayed instance properties before either. A property binding from the parent therefore guarantees `changedProps.has('config')` on the first update, which makes the destroy fire on the one instance the controller just built. That is a real lifecycle inversion, not a style complaint, and the jsdoc that prescribes the pattern is the thing being defeated rather than an unaddressed guard. Dedupe and dated-ruling checks both come back clean: the Jan-2026 PRD that introduced this pattern did so for OutputFilesSection, a component that no longer exists and that had a genuine stale-element problem FileSelectGroup does not share. Nothing here touches a frozen wire, a ratchet, or a persisted surface. The one thing the finding gets wrong is the consequence: I checked sortablejs's default `draggable: '>*'` and the template's `role="list"` wrapper, and the Sortable is attached to a container with a single child, so drag reorder is already impossible for an unrelated reason. That is a correction and arguably a second defect, not a refutation of the first — the finding's cited lines are all read correctly. Since this is judged as a defect, the understated LoC does not count against it.

</details>

### Four of the seven MainViewExecuteFiles wire fields cannot reach the agent — two are overridden by the sole consumer, one has no producer, one is stripped by the parse

- **Slice**: b28 · **Kind**: delete · **Risk**: low · **Net**: -16 LoC (proposer claimed -14; verifier figure governs)
- **Files**: `src/shared/schemas/mainView/executeMessage.ts`, `src/shared/mainView/executionFormState.ts`, `src/shared/schemas/mainView/inbound.ts`, `src/controllers/mainView/MainViewExecutionController.ts`, `packages/extension/src/webview/frontend/mainViewActions.ts`

**Evidence**

`MainViewExecuteFilesSchema` (src/shared/schemas/mainView/executeMessage.ts:9-17) declares seven file fields. Every execute path — extension `handleExecute` (packages/extension/src/webview/managers/executionHandlers.ts:37), desktop `handleExecute` (packages/desktop/src/main/desktopAgentExecution.ts:1241), and `buildDesktopSetupExecuteMessage` (src/controllers/onboarding/setupLaunch.ts:124) — funnels into `buildMainViewExecutionRequest` (src/controllers/mainView/MainViewExecutionController.ts:65). That function spreads `...files` at :107 and then hardcodes `outputFiles: []` at :112 and `editedFile: null` at :119, both AFTER the spread. So:

- `outputFiles` (executeMessage.ts:13) — value discarded at MainViewExecutionController.ts:112. It is also `.pick`ed into the POLISH_INSTRUCTION_TEXT schema (src/shared/schemas/mainView/inbound.ts:156), but the sole producer sends only inputFiles/contextFiles/mediaFiles (packages/extension/src/webview/frontend/mainViewActions.ts:360-367) and the sole reader iterates exactly `['inputFiles','contextFiles','mediaFiles']` (packages/extension/src/webview/managers/InstructionManager.ts:72). Dead on both messages.
- `editedFile` (executeMessage.ts:14) — actively produced by `buildMainViewExecuteMessage` from `state.singleFiles.editedFile` (src/shared/mainView/executionFormState.ts:43), then discarded at MainViewExecutionController.ts:119.
- `editedFiles` (executeMessage.ts:15) — `rg` over the whole repo finds no producer that puts it in an execute message; the only writers of that key are AgentConfig-level (src/agent/core/definition/AgentConfig.ts:32) and the tool-use dispatch node.
- `baseFile` (executeMessage.ts:16) — produced at executionFormState.ts:44, spread into the config, then silently stripped: `validateExecutionRequest` parses via `AgentConfigSchema.safeParse` (src/agent/core/state/executionRequests.ts:27), and `AgentConfigSharedFieldsSchema` (AgentConfig.ts:16) is a non-strict `z.object` with no `baseFile` member. The reflection flow's `baseFiles` (src/agent/implementations/flows/reflection/runReflectionFlow.ts:142) is derived from inputFiles, not from config.

The doc comment on `buildMainViewExecuteMessage` (src/shared/mainView/executionFormState.ts:30) — "Output files aren't user-selectable at execute time, so that list is always empty" — describes a field the function no longer emits at all.

Dedupe: the rounds 1-4 index has no MainViewExecute/execute-wire entry. `notifyWhenEmpty` (round 1 refuted) is a different field on different commands. Grepped the four survey docs in docs/proposals/ for MainViewExecuteFilesSchema, editedFiles, and buildMainViewExecuteMessage — no hits.

**Proposal**

Delete `outputFiles`, `editedFile`, `editedFiles`, and `baseFile` from `MainViewExecuteFilesSchema`; drop `editedFile`/`baseFile` from `buildMainViewExecuteMessage` (and `singleFiles` from `MainViewExecutionFormState` if nothing else needs it); drop the `outputFiles: true` member from the POLISH `.pick`; delete the now-redundant `outputFiles: []` and `editedFile: null` overrides in `buildMainViewExecutionRequest` (AgentConfig already prefaults `outputFiles` to `[]` and `editedFile` to `null`); rewrite the stale comment at executionFormState.ts:30. This is the webview IPC wire, not the frozen CLI NDJSON wire — both sides ship in the same build.

**What we give up**

A future main-view feature that lets the user pick output files or pass an edited file to a workflow agent would have to re-add the field. Nothing today reads it, and re-adding one optional field is cheap.

**Verifier corrections — these override the evidence and proposal above**

1. Desktop entry point is `packages/desktop/src/main/desktopAgentExecution.ts:1248` (`async handleExecute`), not :1241.

2. Neither host calls `buildMainViewExecutionRequest` directly. Both go through `prepareMainViewExecutionLaunch` (src/controllers/mainView/backend/MainViewExecutionLaunchController.ts:47) -> `prepareMainViewExecutionRequest` -> `buildMainViewExecutionRequest` (:65). The destination is right; the path skips a hop. Also, `buildDesktopSetupExecuteMessage` (setupLaunch.ts:124-133) never sets `files` at all, so citing it as an execute path that "funnels" these fields is padding — it is irrelevant to this finding.

3. Misread at runReflectionFlow.ts:142. The actual code is `config.outputFiles.length > 0 ? config.outputFiles : config.inputFiles`. `baseFiles` IS read from config, and from `config.outputFiles` first; it falls through to `inputFiles` only because the controller forces `outputFiles: []`. The verdict is unchanged (the wire field still never reaches config), but the consequence matters: deleting the controller's explicit `outputFiles: []` moves a live behavioral dependency of the reflection flow onto `NullableFileFieldsSchema`'s `.prefault([])`. Recommend KEEPING `outputFiles: []` and its two-line comment ("Workflow output paths are implicit in the input list...") — that comment is the only recorded rationale for the invariant, and the finding proposes deleting both it and the executionFormState JSDoc, erasing the rationale from the repo entirely.

4. `outputFiles` is not dead at the AgentConfig level. `MainViewStateRestoreController.ts:61` reads `agentConfig.outputFiles` and runReflectionFlow.ts:142 reads `config.outputFiles`. Only the two main-view _wire_ fields are dead. "Dead on both messages" is correct as written but should be explicitly scoped to the wire so a reader does not extend it to AgentConfig.

5. The JSDoc at executionFormState.ts:30 is not stale in the misleading sense the finding implies. "Output files aren't user-selectable at execute time, so that list is always empty" documents an intentional omission, which is legitimate. It becomes redundant only after the schema field goes; delete it rather than "rewrite" it.

6. Undercounted, in the finding's favour: `mediaFiles` is ALSO reassigned after the spread (controller :120-125, the pasted-image mapping). Once `outputFiles`/`editedFile`/`editedFiles`/`baseFile` are gone, `...files` at :107 carries only `inputFiles` and `contextFiles` — the spread could become an explicit two-key destructure, a tidy the finding did not count.

7. Test churn not counted: src/test-kernel/shared/MainViewExecuteMessage.vitest.ts must change at :22 (`singleFiles` in the helper), :43 (the `singleFiles` override), and :66-67 (the `baseFile`/`editedFile` assertions in `toMatchObject`). That is ~4 more deleted lines, which offsets keeping the controller's `outputFiles: []`.

8. Claimed -14 is slightly low. Honest count: executeMessage.ts -4; executionFormState.ts -2 builder, -1 interface field, -1 `SingleFiles` type import, -1 JSDoc; inbound.ts -1; controller -1 (`editedFile: null` only, keeping `outputFiles: []`); mainViewActions.ts -1; test -4. Net -16.

<details><summary>Verifier reasoning</summary>

Every load-bearing claim re-verified at HEAD. (a) `rg "message\.files"` returns exactly one production reader, MainViewExecutionController.ts:75; `grep -n` confirms `...files` at :107 with `outputFiles: []` at :112 and `editedFile: null` at :119 both AFTER it, so those two wire values are provably discarded. (b) `AgentConfigSharedFieldsSchema` (AgentConfig.ts:16) extends `NullableFileFieldsSchema` (fileFields.ts:20-23), which has `inputFiles/contextFiles/mediaFiles/outputFiles` + `editedFile` and no `baseFile`; it is a non-strict `z.object`, so `AgentConfigSchema.safeParse` at executionRequests.ts:27 strips `baseFile` silently — the claim holds. (c) `editedFiles` has no execute-message producer anywhere in the repo; the only writers are AgentConfig.ts:32, ToolUseDispatchNode, and `userVars.ts:296`. (d) POLISH: the sole producer (mainViewActions.ts:360-367) sends three arrays, the sole reader (InstructionManager.ts:72) iterates exactly three; only five files reference `POLISH_INSTRUCTION_TEXT` and none is in desktop, so the `outputFiles: true` pick member is unreachable. (e) Single-producer check passes for both hosts: `packages/desktop/src/renderer/main.ts:56` imports `@webview/frontend`, so `buildMainViewExecuteMessage` is the only builder in the repo and both sides ship in one build. Kill-check sweep: not a duplicate (rounds1234-index has no execute-wire entry; the four survey docs return zero hits on `MainViewExecuteFilesSchema`, `editedFiles`, `buildMainViewExecuteMessage`, and round-4-tests explicitly distinguishes the round-1 `MainViewExecuteMessage` item as a test-suite finding). No dated ruling defends the fields — the most recent commit on this exact object (`7ab05e138e`, 2026-08-18) deleted three sibling fields for the same reason without recording a keep. Not a settled surface: this is the webview IPC wire, not the frozen CLI NDJSON contract, not a settings key, not a ratchet, and not the texra-action result contract; the persisted `MainViewPersistedStateSchema` (state.ts:169) keeps its own `baseFile`/`outputFiles` and is untouched. Code-explains-itself: the two comments in play (controller :110-111, executionFormState.ts:30) explain why `outputFiles` is forced empty — they do not defend the wire fields, and the finding's proposal survives if the controller comment is retained. Where I did dock it: the runReflectionFlow.ts:142 read is a genuine misread (it reads `config.outputFiles` first, not just `inputFiles`), and the proposal to delete both explanatory comments would erase the only recorded rationale for the always-empty invariant. Neither defeats the deletion, so I keep the controller's `outputFiles: []` and adjust the count accordingly.

(b) `createProbeMarkdownIt` (src/shared/markdown/createMarkdownProcessor.ts:266-280) takes `{breaks, linkify, html}`. Its two call sites are the normalize probe, which passes the literals `{breaks: false, linkify: true, html: false}` (:733-735), and the render probe, which passes `config.renderer.options.{breaks,linkify,html}` (:802-808). Every renderer is built by `createMarkdownRenderer`, which hardcodes `breaks: false, linkify: true, html: false` (src/shared/markdown/createMarkdownRenderer.ts:36-41); the only two renderers in the repo are the KaTeX HTML one (katexHtmlProcessor.ts:37) and the CLI ANSI one (packages/cli/src/chat/tui/render/ansiMarkdown.ts:503), and neither `configure` hook mutates `md.options` (grepped ansiMarkdown.ts for `.set(`/`options.` — no hits). So both call sites resolve to the identical triple, and the two probes are the same object built two ways.

Dedupe: no markdown/texmath entry in the rounds 1-4 index; grepped the four survey docs for createTexmathPlugin, TexmathPluginOptions, createProbeMarkdownIt, and addDisplayMathParagraphInterruptions — no hits.

**Proposal**

Hoist the delimiter list to a module constant in texmathPlugin.ts, drop `TexmathPluginOptions.delimiters` and the `delimiters` parameter of `addDisplayMathParagraphInterruptions`, and concatenate the three `texmath.rules.*.block` arrays unconditionally. In createMarkdownProcessor.ts, drop `createProbeMarkdownIt`'s options parameter (or the function itself) and build both probes from the same fixed `{breaks: false, linkify: true, html: false}`, matching `createMarkdownRenderer`'s own constants — with a comment naming createMarkdownRenderer as the reason the probe must mirror those three values.

**What we give up**

If a host ever wants a different math-delimiter set or a renderer with `breaks: true`, the parameter comes back — but then it comes back with a second call site that actually exercises it, and the probe's coupling to `createMarkdownRenderer` becomes a real constraint to encode rather than a phantom one.

There is a third: src/shared/highlighting/lightweightMd.ts:18 calls `createMarkdownRenderer({ highlight: highlightCode })` for the settings view. ### RecordingButtonController.hostConnected is an empty method whose comment claims a structural requirement Lit's ReactiveController does not impose

- **Slice**: b28 · **Kind**: delete · **Risk**: low · **Net**: -4 LoC
- **Files**: `src/shared/litControllers/RecordingButtonController.ts`

**Evidence**

src/shared/litControllers/RecordingButtonController.ts:59-61 reads:

// Satisfies ReactiveController's structural requirement; state is driven via
// setRecording(), not host lifecycle callbacks.
hostConnected(): void {}

Lit's `ReactiveController` declares all four callbacks optional — `hostConnected?()`, `hostDisconnected?()`, `hostUpdate?()`, `hostUpdated?()` (node_modules/.pnpm/@lit+reactive-element@2.1.2/node_modules/@lit/reactive-element/reactive-controller.d.ts:47-73) — so `implements ReactiveController` is satisfied by an empty class. The two sibling controllers in the same directory prove it: `CopyButtonController` implements only `hostDisconnected` and `SortableController` implements only `hostUpdated`/`hostDisconnected`; neither declares an empty `hostConnected`. The host calls this no-op on every connect.

Dedupe: the rounds 1-4 index has no lit-controller entry; grepped the four survey docs for RecordingButtonController and hostConnected — no hits.

**Proposal**

Delete the method and its comment. `implements ReactiveController` keeps compiling.

**What we give up**

Nothing.

**Verifier corrections — these override the evidence and proposal above**

One citation is off: the finding cites reactive-controller.d.ts:47-73 for the four optional callbacks; the interface actually spans lines 48-76 (`hostConnected?()` at 54, `hostDisconnected?()` at 61, `hostUpdate?()` at 69, `hostUpdated?()` at 75). Substance unchanged.

One under-stated fact worth recording in the PR: the comment is not original authorship. It was reworded, not introduced, by commit 8b71e6149d (#9990, "code-simplifier sweeps across 132 production source files"), which replaced "Required by the Lit ReactiveController interface" with the current phrasing. A simplifier pass already had this line in hand and propagated the false claim instead of deleting the method — worth one sentence in the PR body so the deletion does not read as reversing a deliberate decision.

Everything else in the evidence is accurate: all four ReactiveController callbacks are optional, both sibling controllers implement partial subsets, the sole consumer never touches hostConnected, and Lit invokes it through optional chaining so removal is safe.

<details><summary>Verifier reasoning</summary>

The finding's central claim is verifiable and true: Lit's ReactiveController makes every lifecycle callback optional, so the comment's stated justification ("satisfies a structural requirement") is false, and the two sibling controllers in the same directory are in-repo counterexamples. The method is a no-op with no caller other than Lit's own optional-chained dispatch, so deleting it changes nothing at runtime or at type-check. No survey doc, index entry, or dated ruling covers it; no ratchet, wire contract, or persisted surface is involved. The only weakness is scale — it is a 4-line win — but "delete" findings are not refuted for being small, only for being wrong, duplicated, ruled on, or net-negative, and none of those apply. The single correction is a minor line-number miscitation.

### The markdown processor caches rendered output under a 32-bit FNV-1a hash of the source, so a collision silently renders another message's content

- **Slice**: b28 · **Kind**: defect · **Risk**: low · **Net**: 5 LoC (proposer claimed 4; verifier figure governs)
- **Files**: `src/shared/markdown/createMarkdownProcessor.ts`

**Evidence**

`hashContent` (src/shared/markdown/createMarkdownProcessor.ts:752-760) is FNV-1a truncated to 32 bits (`hash = (hash * 16777619) >>> 0`) rendered as base-36. `createMarkdownProcessor` uses that string as the LRU key and never stores or re-checks the source: `const key = hashContent(content); const cached = cache.get(key); if (cached !== undefined) { hitCount += 1; return cached; }` (:776-781), and `cache.set(key, result)` at :842. The cache holds up to `MAX_CACHE_ENTRIES = 2000` entries (:15, :766-770).

Two different message bodies that collide in 32 bits therefore render as each other — a chat message silently displaying a different message's HTML/ANSI, with no warning and nothing in the transcript to explain it. With a full 2000-entry cache the birthday probability is ~4.7e-4 per processor instance, and the CLI keeps one processor per `width:color` pair (packages/cli/src/chat/tui/render/ansiMarkdown.ts:495-521) over long-lived TUI sessions, so this is a real long-tail wrong-but-quiet failure, exactly the class CLAUDE.md calls a defect.

The comment at :752 — "FNV-1a hash → base-36 string. Cheap, no crypto needs here" — defends only against crypto strength. It does not address using the digest as an identity key, which is the actual failure mode; collision resistance here is a correctness requirement, not a security one.

Dedupe: no markdown-cache entry in the rounds 1-4 index; grepped the four survey docs for hashContent, createMarkdownProcessor, and LRUCache — the only hit is a 2026-08-15 proposal reference to `MATH_SPAN_PATTERNS`, an unrelated line.

**Proposal**

Widen the digest so collisions stop being reachable: run two FNV-1a lanes with different offset bases in the same loop and concatenate their base-36 forms (a ~4-line change to `hashContent`, no call-site change). Alternatively key the LRU on `content` directly and delete `hashContent` (−9 LoC) — but note `lru-cache`'s `maxSize`/`sizeCalculation` counts only the value, so keying on the source roughly doubles the cache's real memory; the two-lane hash is the cheaper fix.

**What we give up**

Nothing behavioral. The key string grows from ~7 to ~13 characters per cached entry.

**Verifier corrections — these override the evidence and proposal above**

1. Scope understated — this is not CLI-only. `src/shared/markdown/katexHtmlProcessor.ts:48` builds a second processor over the same cache, so the extension webview has the identical exposure, and there a collision injects another message's _HTML_ into the DOM. The finding cites only ansiMarkdown.ts; the fix is shared, so this strengthens rather than changes it.

2. The probability figure is misframed, and understates the exposure. ~4.7e-4 is P(some pair collides among 2000 _simultaneously cached_ distinct bodies). But the cache churns: every streaming prefix is a distinct key and a miss, so a long TUI session pushes far more than 2000 distinct bodies through a 2000-entry window. The honest cumulative figure is ≈ (distinct bodies rendered) × 2000 / 2^32 — roughly 5e-3 at 1e4 distinct bodies and ~5e-2 at 1e5. The finding's number is the floor, not the ceiling.

3. The proposed fix as written is unsound. Concatenating two variable-length base-36 strings with no delimiter is ambiguous (`"ab" + "c"` collides with `"a" + "bc"`), which re-imports collisions across the lane boundary. Join with a separator or zero-pad each lane to 7 chars.

4. Two lanes differing only in offset basis are weaker than "two independent 32-bit hashes". Each FNV-1a step `h = ((h ^ c) * p) >>> 0` is a bijection on 32 bits (odd multiplier, XOR), so both lanes are the _same_ bijection F applied to different seeds: `a = F(a0)`, `b = F(b0)`. They are structurally correlated, not independent. Use a different prime on the second lane, or fold `str.length` into the key, so the lanes do not share a composition.

5. Minor: base-36 of a 32-bit value is _up to_ 7 chars but variable (1-7), so "grows from ~7 to ~13" should read "up to 7 → up to 14 (+1 separator)".

6. Tangential but worth noting while in the file: the doc comment at ansiMarkdown.ts:528-531 ("Uses a per-host LRU cache so streaming deltas don't re-render the entire message body each frame") is inaccurate for a growing delta — every new prefix is a fresh key and a miss. The cache only pays off for unchanged content re-rendered across frames.

<details><summary>Verifier reasoning</summary>

Survives as a real defect. The citation is accurate line-for-line at HEAD: a 32-bit FNV-1a digest is the sole LRU identity key, the source string is never stored and never re-compared on a hit, and the cache holds up to 2000 entries. There is no dedupe hit in the rounds 1-4 index or in the four survey docs, no dated ruling on the key derivation, and the one defending comment ("no crypto needs here") speaks to attacker resistance, not to accidental collision as an identity requirement — the finding defeats it head-on. No external consumer is involved: both processors feed rendering only. The failure mode is low-severity but genuinely silent, which is the class CLAUDE.md explicitly calls a defect, and defect findings are not refutable on profitability. Four factual gaps remain: the webview processor shares the defect (scope understated), the quoted birthday probability is the floor rather than the cumulative session exposure, the proposed lane concatenation is delimiter-ambiguous, and the same-prime two-lane construction yields correlated rather than independent lanes.

</details>

### buildAuthStatusMessage is a generic `{command, status}` object literal whose doc claims to centralize a wire shape it never references

- **Slice**: b29 · **Kind**: delete · **Risk**: low · **Net**: -44 LoC (proposer claimed -35; verifier figure governs)
- **Files**: `src/shared/settingsView/handlers/authStatusMessage.ts`, `packages/extension/src/settingsView/SettingsViewMessageHandler.ts`, `packages/desktop/src/main/desktopCredentialSettingsController.ts`, `src/test-kernel/settings/settingsNotificationHandlers.vitest.ts`

It will happily produce `{command: SET_TAB, status: 42}`. All four production call sites already import both `SETTINGS_VIEW_COMMANDS` and the status getter, and both hosts pass the same two pairs:

- `packages/extension/src/settingsView/SettingsViewMessageHandler.ts:78, 187-190, 197-200`
- `packages/desktop/src/main/desktopCredentialSettingsController.ts:38, 453-456, 462-465`

Delete the `buildAuthStatusMessage` case from settingsNotificationHandlers.vitest.ts; the surviving cases in that file cover the agent-selection builders. Drop the module's knip-baseline row in the same PR if one exists.

**What we give up**

One fewer named seam between the two hosts' auth-status posts. Both hosts keep posting the same literal, and typing the literal against the outbound arm is strictly stronger than what the generic gave.

**Verifier corrections — these override the evidence and proposal above**

Three factual errors, none fatal:

1. WRONG on where the shape is checked, for half the call sites. The finding says "the arms are checked (if at all) at the `postMessage` boundary, exactly as they would be with an inline literal." On the extension side that is false in the finding's own disfavor: `packages/extension/src/settingsView/handlers/subscriptionHandlers.ts:31-32,41` declares `type SubscriptionAuthStatusMessage = UpdateChatGptAuthStatusMessage | UpdateGrokAuthStatusMessage` and types the constructor param `buildStatusMessage: () => Promise<SubscriptionAuthStatusMessage>`. So the two extension arms ARE compile-checked against the real outbound union today, at the constructor — not at `webview.postMessage`, which takes `any` in the VS Code API. The "it will happily produce `{command: SET_TAB, status: 42}`" hypothetical reaches no extension call site. The claim is true only for desktop: `packages/desktop/src/main/desktopCredentialSettingsController.ts:45-47` types `renderer.postToRenderer(message: unknown): void`, so those two arms are genuinely unchecked.

2. Therefore "typing the literal against the outbound arm is strictly stronger than what the generic gave" is half right. It is stronger only for the two desktop sites, and only if the inlined literals actually carry `satisfies UpdateChatGptAuthStatusMessage` / `satisfies UpdateGrokAuthStatusMessage`, which costs a new type import in desktopCredentialSettingsController.ts. The extension gets the same check with or without the helper. If the PR inlines bare literals into `postToRenderer(unknown)` and skips the `satisfies`, the change is a small type-safety LOSS on desktop, not a gain — that annotation is mandatory, not optional.

3. The AGENTS.md citation is fabricated. `grep -n "relocates complexity"` over AGENTS.md returns nothing; the nearest real text is AGENTS.md:645 ("grep the caller count before approving any new shared helper (single-caller extractions are banned)"), plus CLAUDE.md's "a wrapper that only creates state, runs a flow, and interprets results gets inlined," which is about flow wrappers. Worse, the quoted rule cuts the other way: this helper has four production callers across two hosts, so it is not a banned single-caller extraction. The honest argument is narrower and still sufficient — the wrapper saves zero lines per call site (extension 5 lines -> 4; desktop 4 -> 4) while costing a module, an import in three files, and a test, so multi-caller status buys it nothing.

Minor: `src/shared/schemas/settingsViewMessages.ts:514-536` is off. `ChatGptAuthStatusSchema` is 510-515, `UpdateChatGptAuthStatusMessageSchema` 518-524, `GrokAuthStatusSchema` 527-532, `UpdateGrokAuthStatusMessageSchema` 534-539.

Also confirmed for the executor: after deleting the test case at settingsNotificationHandlers.vitest.ts:103-121, both `vi` (lines 34, 35, 63, 64) and `SETTINGS_VIEW_COMMANDS` remain used by the surviving agent-selection cases, so only the `buildAuthStatusMessage` import (line 6) is removed.

<details><summary>Verifier reasoning</summary>

The module is a two-statement pass-through: `return { command, status: await getStatus() }`, with S a free type parameter, so it centralizes no contract. Its own doc comment claims only that "the object shape is identical across providers," which the generic signature does not enforce anywhere. All four production call sites already import both `SETTINGS_VIEW_COMMANDS` and the `@auth/*` getter, so the helper shields the hosts from nothing; the boundary test it cites is about the shared tree not importing `@auth/*`, which the tree's other three files keep satisfying after deletion. No ruling, index entry, survey entry, ratchet row, or wire/settings/persisted consumer stands in the way, and the emitted message is unchanged. It survives as a genuine, if small, deletion — with the mandatory rider that the desktop inlines must carry `satisfies` annotations, since `postToRenderer` takes `unknown` and would otherwise silently lose checking.
