- **Files**: `src/transcript/StreamSnapshotStore.ts`

**Evidence**

src/transcript/StreamSnapshotStore.ts:604-612: `private kv(streamId) { /* Record creation on read-only access stays deliberate: hasDiskProvenance() keys off record presence. */ this.getOrCreateRecord(streamId); return new KVStore(streamDataDir(streamId)); }`. `hasDiskProvenance` (:638-641) is `const state = this.records.get(stream)?.diskState; return state !== undefined && state !== 'unknown';` — an absent record yields `state === undefined` → false, and a freshly created record yields `'unknown'` (the registry default at :481) → false. Both answers are identical, so the record creation cannot change what `hasDiskProvenance` reports; the comment's stated reason is wrong. What it does change is `records` membership, which three loops key off: `getExecutionIdMap` (:1517-1530) calls `warnIfUnseeded('getExecutionIdMap', stream)` for **every** resident record, so a probe-only stream produces a spurious "served a record with unestablished disk provenance" warning; `unseenSeedChains` (:1660-1669) and `evictStreamsExcept` (:1868-1872) also walk them. The worst caller is `detachPersistedChildren` (:1479-1503), which loops `for (const stream of await this.listPersistedStreams())` calling `readMeta(this.kv(stream))` — one phantom record per stream on disk, retained until the next `load()`/`evictAll()`. `hasPersistedWorkPlan` (:1463-1465), `read` (:1731-1736) and `readOutputFiles` (:1777-1784) mint them the same way. I checked every other `this.records.get(...)` site: `writeMergedSidecars` (:2140) compares object identity, `queueWrite` (:1591-1592) guards on `writeMutexes`/`streamVersion`, and `streamVersion` (:627-629) reads the registry's version map, which `ResidentStreamRegistry` (src/transcript/ResidentStreamRegistry.ts:25-31) keeps independent of record presence — none treats presence as meaningful. Dedupe: round 2 shipped "Delete KVStoreCache" (rounds1234-index.md), whose proposal text (docs/proposals/2026-08-26-simplification-survey-round2.md:1843) preserved this call verbatim as surface-neutral; nobody checked whether it was still load-bearing, and no proposal mentions `hasDiskProvenance` or `getExecutionIdMap`.

**Proposal**

Drop the `this.getOrCreateRecord(streamId);` line and the comment from `kv()`, leaving `return new KVStore(streamDataDir(streamId));`. This removes phantom records from `records` so `getExecutionIdMap` stops warning about streams that were only probed, and read-only sweeps over every persisted stream stop retaining a record each. Verify against the StreamSnapshotStore suite, whose partial-preload/eager-overlay scenarios exercise the unknown-provenance paths directly.

**What we give up**

If a test or caller distinguishes "record exists with diskState unknown" from "no record" — I found none in this file, but this is the store's whole residency invariant, so if the suite pins record presence after a bare `read()`/`hasPersistedWorkPlan()`, keep the call and instead fix only the comment to say what it actually buys.

**Verifier corrections — these override the evidence and proposal above**

1. netLoc is -3, not -4. The edit removes exactly three lines (two comment lines at :605-606 and the call at :607); the second comment at :608-610, about the handle being stateless, stays.

2. "retained until the next `load()`/`evictAll()`" is incomplete. `load()` only evicts records outside its keep-set (`evictStreamsExcept`, :1867-1872); an explicit `evict(stream)` / staged deletion also clears one. A probe-minted record for a stream that a later `load()` happens to include survives as a real (still-unknown-provenance) record.

3. The finding calls the comment merely wrong today; it was wrong when written. #10335 introduced it as "Record creation on read-only access stays deliberate (see clearMissingOutputs)" at the moment the KV handle stopped living on the record — i.e. it was a post-hoc justification for a line whose actual reason (caching `record.kv`) had just been deleted. #11441 removed the `clearMissingOutputs` pointer after that method was itself deleted, leaving the false half. `hasDiskProvenance` has never keyed off presence: pre-#9965 it was `record?.seeded`, which also returns falsy for both absent and unseeded.

4. One behavioral edge the finding does not mention and a PR body should: `queueWrite` (:1591-1593) also calls `kv()`, inside the write mutex, so today a sidecar write re-mints a record for a non-resident stream. After the change such a stream stays non-resident, so a subsequent `load()` no longer evicts it and no longer cancels its pending write chain. This is not a deletion-safety hole — `StagedDeletionCoordinator` calls `evict(stream)` directly and `evict` (:1119-1131) clears `writeMutexes`/`dirtyWrites` by key prefix, not via the record — and every `dirtyWrites` entry originates from a record-owning mutator, so the window is theoretical. Worth one line in the PR, not a blocker.

5. Minor: `getExecutionIdMap` never emitted a wrong _entry_ for a probed stream (a phantom record has `runExecutionId: undefined`, so `map.size` is unaffected) — the only observable damage is the spurious warning plus the retained record. The finding implies this but does not state it.

<details><summary>Verifier reasoning</summary>

The core claim is exactly right and I confirmed it three ways: by reading `hasDiskProvenance` and the registry default (absent record and fresh record both yield false, so the comment's stated reason cannot be true), by git archaeology (the line is a leftover from when the KV handle was cached on the record, and the justifying comment was invented after that reason was removed), and empirically (a bare `hasPersistedWorkPlan` probe on HEAD makes `getExecutionIdMap` log "unestablished disk provenance" for a stream nobody read; the patched build logs nothing, and 948 tests across the transcript, progress-view and CLI-history suites stay green). No survey doc, index row, or closed issue rules on this line — round 2 copied it forward as surface-neutral without checking it. It is a small but genuine defect: a comment asserting a fact that is false, a read-only sweep that leaves a resident record per stream on disk, and a warning that fires for streams the warning was explicitly documented not to cover.

</details>

### A work-plan sidecar from a newer schemaVersion is discarded in silence, contradicting the function's own "every recovery logs a warning"

- **Slice**: b35 · **Kind**: amend · **Risk**: low · **Net**: 5 LoC
- **Files**: `src/transcript/streamSnapshotRead.ts`

**Evidence**

src/transcript/streamSnapshotRead.ts:136-156. The doc comment on `readPersistedWorkPlan` says "A file written by a NEWER `schemaVersion` is IGNORED (returns empty) … Every recovery logs a warning; a structurally unreadable file degrades to an empty plan loudly." The forward-compat branch at :153-156 is the one recovery that logs nothing: `if (typeof version === 'number' && version > STREAM_SNAPSHOT_SCHEMA_VERSION) { return EMPTY_WORK_PLAN; }`. Every sibling recovery in the same function does warn — non-object at :148-150, corrupted `schemaVersion` at :157-162, per-field failures in `readField` at :171-174 — as does `tryRead` (:94-99) and `assembleSnapshot` (:265-268). The consequence is not cosmetic: `applyStreamData` assigns `record.workPlan = data.workPlan` (StreamSnapshotStore.ts:2005) and sets `diskState = provenance` (:2117), so the empty plan becomes the resident truth; the next `setTodos`/`setPlan` (:1234-1273) calls `writeWorkPlan` (:1536-1547), which stamps the CURRENT `STREAM_SNAPSHOT_SCHEMA_VERSION` and overwrites the newer file. A user who downgrades TeXRA sees their todos and plan vanish and then be permanently replaced, with nothing anywhere saying why. Dedupe: rounds1234-index.md's persisted-data entries cover Zod `.catch()` on inputHistory and the tier-authored/derived migration split; nothing covers this branch, and `grep -rn 'readPersistedWorkPlan' docs/proposals/` returns zero hits.

**Proposal**

Add a warning before the early return, matching the wording of its siblings: `log.warn('Ignoring a work plan written by a newer schema version; this build will replace it on the next write.', { data: { version, supported: STREAM_SNAPSHOT_SCHEMA_VERSION } });`. Do not change the ignore decision itself — refusing to coerce a future shape is the correct forward-compat gate and is what the comment defends; the defect is only that this one recovery is mute while the doc promises it is not.

**What we give up**

If a maintainer argues a downgrade is expected to be silent because the newer file is left byte-intact until a mutation — the overwrite via `writeWorkPlan` is the reason I do not accept that, but a ruling that the whole forward-compat gate should instead refuse to write (rather than warn) would supersede this and is a larger change.

**Verifier corrections — these override the evidence and proposal above**

1. THE USER-FACING SCENARIO IS HYPOTHETICAL TODAY, NOT LIVE. `STREAM_SNAPSHOT_SCHEMA_VERSION = 1 as const` (src/shared/schemas/streamSnapshot.ts:57) and has never been bumped, so no released TeXRA build has ever written `schemaVersion: 2`. "A user who downgrades TeXRA sees their todos and plan vanish" cannot happen at HEAD — the branch fires today only on a corrupt or hand-edited file whose `schemaVersion` is a number greater than 1 (which is precisely the case the finding's own sibling-warn argument covers, since :157's corrupted-version warn is unreachable for any value above 1). The defect stands on two independently sufficient grounds: the doc comment is false as written, and the one recovery that will matter most the day version 2 ships is the one with no diagnostic. State it that way rather than as a bug users are hitting now.

2. PROVENANCE OF THE FALSE SENTENCE. "Every recovery logs a warning" is not original wording — it was introduced by #10791 (abec6fb4fd, "fix: surface durable parse failures"), which compressed #10374's long per-field paragraph into a blanket claim and in doing so overstated it. Worth citing, because it shows the sentence was written as a summary of the loud-recovery work and simply overreached, not as a considered promise about this branch.

3. A CHEAPER SHAPE EXISTS AND SHOULD AT LEAST BE CONSIDERED. Since :157 already warns for every `version !== CURRENT`, the alternative is to let that warn fire first and make the forward-compat return the second check, adjusting :159's "using current" wording to cover both. That may be zero net lines. The finding's dedicated warn is fine and clearer; just do not present "add a warn" as the only option.

4. The proposed message should include the stream id or key if the logger call site has one, matching `tryRead`'s "Discarding unreadable ${key}.json" — otherwise a user with many streams gets an unlocatable warning. `readPersistedWorkPlan` currently takes only `raw`, so this may mean threading the key or accepting the less specific form.

<details><summary>Verifier reasoning</summary>

The claim is verifiable in one file and I verified it line by line. `readPersistedWorkPlan`'s doc says "Every recovery logs a warning"; the forward-compat early return at :154-156 logs nothing while all four sibling recoveries in the same function, plus `tryRead` and `assembleSnapshot`, do. That is a genuine contradiction between a function and its own contract, in a file whose most recent substantive change (#10374) existed solely to close silent-recovery gaps here and whose commit message spells out the same silent-read-then-overwrite trap the finding describes. The overwrite chain is real: `applyStreamData` installs the empty plan as resident truth and marks the record loaded, and any later `setTodos`/`setPlan`/overlay replay calls `writeWorkPlan`, which rewrites the whole file with the current schemaVersion. No dated ruling, no ratchet, no external contract, and no test asserting silence stands in the way. The finding overstates reachability — the version constant is pinned at 1, so the downgrade story is forward-looking rather than a bug in the field — but that is a correction to the framing, not a refutation, and a defect finding is judged on whether the defect is real, which it is. Risk is low: one added log line in a read path, no behavior change to the ignore decision, existing forward-compat test unaffected.

</details>

### Transcript write failures are swallowed by a bare `catch {}` — the only handler on the authoritative log write

- **Slice**: b35 · **Kind**: amend · **Risk**: low · **Net**: 12 LoC (proposer claimed 6; verifier figure governs)
- **Files**: `src/transcript/StreamLogStore.ts`

**Evidence**

`runWriteBatch` at src/transcript/StreamLogStore.ts:1716-1729 wraps each stream's durable write in `try { await this.writeStream(...) } catch { /* re-mark dirty */ }` — line 1722 is a bare `catch` with no binding and no log call. Nothing below it recovers the cause: `writeStream` (:1433-1458) does not catch, and `KVStore.write` (src/common/storage/KVStore.ts:64-74) explicitly throws (its header: "Failures are never swallowed … every other error throws to the caller"). The summary-cache half of `writeStream` IS logged (`maintainSummaryCache` :1509-1526 warns and latches `disableSummaryCacheMaintenance`), so only the authoritative `streamLogs/{id}.json` write is silent. The drifted-copy evidence is the sibling store: `StreamSnapshotStore.write` (src/transcript/StreamSnapshotStore.ts:1549-1561) is the same "persist, keep dirty, retry" shape and logs `Failed to persist ${key}.json for stream ${stream}; sidecar remains dirty.` The only user-visible trace of a persistent failure is `flush()`'s generic throw (:1260-1265) — `Transcript flush failed after 3 retries; N stream(s) remain dirty.` — which carries no cause; on the ordinary throttled-save path (`scheduleSave` → `saveThrottle` → `executeWrite`, :1212-1218) nothing is thrown at all, so a full disk or a permission error means the conversation transcript silently never persists and resume finds nothing. Dedupe: rounds1234-index.md has three sibling swallow findings (run-workspace prep at debug, OpenAI totalUsage at debug, approval-preview readFileWithFallback) but nothing on StreamLogStore; `grep -rniE 'runWriteBatch' docs/proposals/` returns zero hits.

**Proposal**

Bind the error and log it: `catch (error) { … log.warn(\`Failed to persist transcript for stream ${streamId}; retrying on the next save: ${toErrorMessage(error)}\`, { data: error }); if (this.streams.get(streamId)?.log !== undefined) this.markDirty(streamId); }`. `toErrorMessage`and`log`are already imported (:24, :45). Because a throttled save retries every SAVE_MAX_WAIT_MS indefinitely, gate the warning on a per-stream latch cleared by the next successful`writeStream`— the same once-per-key idiom already used by`unseededReadWarned`in the sibling store (StreamSnapshotStore.ts:520-527) and by`disableSummaryCacheMaintenance`(:1550-1554). Optionally carry the last cause into`flush()`'s retry-exhausted message so the thrown error names the disk problem.

**What we give up**

If a maintainer can point at a deliberate ruling that transcript write failures must stay silent on the throttled path (none is written in the file — the comment at :1723-1725 only explains the re-mark-dirty and continue-the-batch decisions, never the discarding of the error). Do not "fix" this by deleting the catch: the continue-the-batch behaviour is load-bearing.

**Verifier corrections — these override the evidence and proposal above**

1. "the conversation transcript silently never persists and resume finds nothing" overstates the shutdown path. A persistent failure is fully silent only in-session; at session close it does surface, just causelessly: `SessionState.ts:728` and `SessionHandle.flushArtifactsOnce` (:610-624) await `transcripts.flush()`, and the rejection is aggregated through `throwAggregated(failures, 'Multiple session artifact writers failed to flush')`. The accurate claim is "no cause is ever recorded anywhere, and nothing at all is reported during the session" — not "no signal exists".

2. The catch is not literally `catch {}` — it is a bare `catch` with a two-line non-empty body (re-mark dirty). The title's "`catch {}`" is shorthand; the defect is the discarded binding, not an empty block. Worth phrasing precisely in the PR since §15's blocker text keys on both the empty form and the missing best-effort justification.

3. `flush()`'s throw is at :1262-1265 (the `writeAttempts >= MAX_WRITE_RETRIES` branch), not :1260-1265; `scheduleSave` spans :1211-1218, not :1212-1218; `unseededReadWarned` is the single field line :527, not :520-527. Cosmetic offsets, all within one or two lines.

4. Untested claim worth checking before landing: `src/test-kernel/transcript/StreamLogStoreLoad.vitest.ts:1615` ("rejects flush when authoritative transcript writes fail") and :739 ("opens from authoritative logs when summary cache writeback fails") both drive this exact path. Neither should break on an added warn, but confirm neither asserts a clean log.

5. Scope discipline: implement the warn + latch only. The optional "carry the last cause into flush()'s retry-exhausted message" is a second change touching a thrown-error contract that tests at :1615 may match on — either do it deliberately with that test updated, or drop it.

<details><summary>Verifier reasoning</summary>

This is a genuine M2 silent-swallow on the authoritative persistence path, and every element of the evidence chain checks out against HEAD: the bare catch discards the only error object; neither `writeStream` nor `KVStore.write` catches anything below it, and `KVStore`'s own header advertises that it throws precisely so I/O failures cannot masquerade as absent data; the summary-cache half of the same method logs and latches, and the sibling `StreamSnapshotStore` logs the identical shape, so the file is internally inconsistent. The in-file comment defends the retry and the batch drain, never the discard, so criterion 3 does not apply. Nothing in the round-1-4 index or the four survey docs mentions `runWriteBatch`, and no dated ruling protects it — the standing CLAUDE.md and §15 rulings both condemn it. The strongest counterargument, that the failure is not truly invisible because `flush()` throws at session close, weakens the severity but not the defect: the thrown message carries a stream count and no cause, so a maintainer facing a disk-full report has nothing to chase, and on the ordinary throttled path nothing is reported at all. Defects survive at positive LoC by the stated rule.

</details>

### appendTail's retainChars parameter has no production caller left, and the header comment names three consumers of which one exists

- **Slice**: b36 · **Kind**: delete · **Risk**: low · **Net**: -30 LoC (proposer claimed -32; verifier figure governs)
- **Files**: `src/utils/text/appendTail.ts`, `src/test-kernel/utils/AppendTail.vitest.ts`

**Evidence**

src/utils/text/appendTail.ts:6-10 documents `retainChars` as serving 'the webview's 100k→80k policy', and :18/:21/:25 implement it (`retainChars: number = maxChars`, `clamp(retainChars, 0, safeMaxChars)`, `cut = combined.length - safeRetainChars`) — the `clamp` import at :12 exists only for it. Grepping `appendTail` across src, packages and scripts (excluding packages/agent/dist and test-kernel) gives exactly five production call sites: src/tools/bash.ts:117, :124, :135, :183 and src/agent/modelHandlers/utils/toolAttachmentUtils.ts:201. Every one passes three arguments. Grepping `retainChars` repo-wide gives only the module itself and src/test-kernel/utils/AppendTail.vitest.ts:20-47, whose four cases (:23, :28, :32, :44) are the sole consumers — one of them still commented 'Models the 100k→80k webview policy'. No webview file calls appendTail at all. The same staleness runs through the header: :1-4 names 'the bash background tail, the CLI TUI process-output buffer, and the shared stream-meta reducer'; only bash.ts remains, the two CLI/stream consumers are gone, and the real second consumer (toolAttachmentUtils' oversized-tool-result truncator) is not named. Secondary drift in the same file, worth folding into the same PR: appendHead's :47-50 comment states it enforces the cap 'even for a caller that hands in an oversized starting value', while appendTail's `if (!chunk) return current` at :22 sits _before_ the cap check and returns an oversized `current` unchanged — the two halves of one file disagree about the same invariant. Dedupe: no survey doc mentions appendTail, appendHead or retainChars; the nearest index entry is round 1's 'Drop the compactRows parameter from the scroll-bounds helpers', a different symbol in a different subsystem.

**Proposal**

Delete the `retainChars` parameter, the `clamp` import and the clamp line; `cut` becomes `combined.length - safeMaxChars`. Delete the four retainChars tests (AppendTail.vitest.ts:20-47) with the behaviour, per the testing-discipline rule that tests pinning retired behaviour go with it — keep the surrogate-pair and negative-cap cases, which pin the surviving contract. Rewrite the header comment to name its two actual consumers, and move appendTail's empty-chunk early return below the cap check so both functions honour the 'at most maxChars' invariant they both claim.

**What we give up**

The ability to reset below the cap. If a future consumer wants a hysteresis window it re-adds one parameter — cheaper than carrying a knob whose only exercise is its own test file and whose documented caller no longer exists.

**Verifier corrections — these override the evidence and proposal above**

1. The proposal contradicts itself on the test range. It says "delete AppendTail.vitest.ts:20-47" but also "keep the negative-cap case" — and the negative-cap case IS inside that range, at :31-33. That case passes a fourth argument (`appendTail('0123456789', 'abc', -1, 100)`) but is really pinning the `Math.max(0, maxChars)` floor. It must be rewritten as `appendTail('0123456789', 'abc', -1)` and kept, not deleted. The genuinely retainChars-dependent blocks are :20-24, :26-29, :35-38, and :40-46.

2. The "surrogate-pair" case the proposal says to keep is :48-60, which already exercises the surrogate guard with three arguments. :40-46 ("keeps a surrogate pair intact when trimming to retainChars") is a retainChars variant of it and is redundant once the parameter goes, so nothing is lost by deleting it.

3. "the `clamp` import at :12 exists only for it" is true _within this file_ only. `clamp` remains a live export of `@utils/core` with other consumers, so removing the import deletes one line here and nothing downstream. Worth stating so a reviewer does not expect a cascade.

4. Removing the parameter does not collapse the signature. `export function appendTail(current: string, chunk: string, maxChars: number): string {` is 86 characters, over prettier's 80-char printWidth, so the multi-line form survives and only the `retainChars` line is saved — not four lines.

5. The empty-chunk reordering should not be sold as fixing a live bug. Checked against all five call sites: the only one that can pass an empty `chunk` is bash.ts:135 (`pendingWhitespaceTail` may be ''), and its `current` (`tail`) is already within `tailChars` by construction, so the early return never actually leaks an oversized string today. It is a real internal inconsistency between the two halves of the file and a reasonable hardening, but it is latent, not observed — describe it that way or a reviewer will call the finding overstated.

6. Useful provenance the finding omits: `git log -S retainChars` attributes the loss of the last real caller to #9139/#9167 ("recover parts 2 and 3 of the dead process pipeline retirement"), with the parameter introduced by #6827/#6852 for the stream-meta reducer. Citing that in the PR body pre-empts the "was this deliberate?" review question.

<details><summary>Verifier reasoning</summary>

This is the clean case for a dead-parameter deletion: a five-argument-slot knob whose every production call site passes three, whose only surviving exercise is its own test file, and whose documented justification points at a subsystem git history shows was deleted two months ago. I re-read the module and all five call sites rather than trusting the evidence block, and each quoted line number is correct.

The dedupe is clean — zero hits across the 295-title index and all five survey docs — and the one doc that names appendTail concerns its relocation, not its signature. Nothing in the frozen surfaces is touched: not the agent SDK, not a ratchet baseline, not the browser-safe six, not a wire contract.

The defects are all in the write-up, not the claim. The test-range instruction is internally inconsistent (it deletes a case it promises to keep), the LoC arithmetic assumes a signature collapse that prettier will not perform, and the appendHead/appendTail invariant mismatch is presented with more urgency than the call sites justify. None of those touch whether the parameter is dead, which is what the finding stands or falls on.

Honest cost: roughly -9 in appendTail.ts (six comment lines, the clamp import and its blank, the parameter line, the clamp line, minus a line or two for the rewritten header) and roughly -21 in the test file once the negative-cap case is preserved instead of dropped. Call it -30. Low risk — a private helper, no behavioral change at any live call site, and typecheck catches any missed argument immediately.

</details>

### The XML parse tier cannot represent a single <document>, so every single-output agent round logs two errors and falls through to the regex fallback

- **Slice**: b36 · **Kind**: defect · **Risk**: medium · **Net**: -3 LoC (proposer claimed -4; verifier figure governs)
- **Files**: `src/utils/text/xmlExtraction.ts`, `src/agent/implementations/flows/reflection/output/XmlOutputManager.ts`

**Evidence**

src/utils/text/xmlExtraction.ts:129-164. `extractContentFromXMLbyTagMultiple` returns documents only when `Array.isArray(container[OUTPUT_DOCUMENT_TAG])` (:142). fast-xml-parser returns an _object_, not an array, for a single child unless `isArray` is configured — and XML_PARSER_OPTIONS (XmlOutputManager.ts:54-61) configures no `isArray`. I ran the exact parser config: `{documents:{document:{content:'hello',name:'a.tex'}}}` for one document vs an array for two. So for a one-document response the function falls past :142, logs `log.error('Document property is not an array in multiple document case…')` (:154-156), falls out of the `if` and logs a _second_ `log.error('No documents or document elements found in output file…')` (:160-162), then returns null. XmlOutputManager.ts:257-262 then logs the fallback at debug and :271 hands the work to `extractMultipleDocumentsByRegex`. This is the common path, not an edge: the output blocks in packages/extension/resources/agents/ocr.yaml:46-50 and :64-68, polish.yaml, write/paper2slide.yaml and write/paper2poster.yaml:66-70,:74-78 all instruct the model to emit exactly one `<document name="{{ OUTPUT_FILES[0] }}">`. So the whole XML tier — the reason `addCdataToTagsMultiple` + XMLParser exist — never runs for single-output agents, and each round emits two error-level lines whose text ('No documents or document elements found') is the opposite of what happened. Dedupe: `extractContentFromXMLbyTagMultiple` appears in none of the five survey docs; the only xmlExtraction hit (49-candidates.md:979) is about a file rename/split, and round 1's shipped item 27 folded `processMultipleOutputs` into `extractFilesFromXml`, a different function. No comment defends the array-only shape; the one comment there (:147-149) is about the 'unnamed' contract.

**Proposal**

Accept the single-document shape: `const documents = ensureArray(container[OUTPUT_DOCUMENT_TAG])` — `ensureArray` already lives in `@utils/core`, which this file already imports `isObject` from (:13) — and drop the now-unreachable 'not an array' log. Demote the remaining 'no documents found' log from `error` to `debug`, since XmlOutputManager.ts:257-262 already narrates the fallback at debug and owns the recovery. One behaviour delta to check when implementing: the parse tier trims the body (`entry.content?.toString().trim()`, :146) while the regex tier does not (`removeCDATA(match[2])`, xmlExtraction.ts:92), so single-doc outputs would start losing the leading newline after the open tag — confirm that against a round-trip before merging.

**What we give up**

If the trim delta turns out to matter, the fallback ordering is deliberate and should stay; then the finding narrows to the log severity and wording alone (still worth fixing: two error-level lines per round on the normal path). Either way the parse tier stops claiming a failure that is really an unhandled arity.

**Verifier corrections — these override the evidence and proposal above**

1. The trim delta the finding calls a merge blocker does not exist in the written bytes. XmlOutputManager.ts:451-454 already calls `this.cleanExtractedDocumentContent(doc.content.trim(), texFile)`, and cleanExtractedDocumentContent trimEnds and re-appends a single '\n' (:496-508). My probe shows the two tiers differ only by the leading/trailing newline that this trim removes. The "Give up" clause is therefore moot — there is no round-trip risk to confirm on that axis.

2. The proposed `ensureArray(container[OUTPUT_DOCUMENT_TAG])` is UNSAFE as written and would introduce a data-loss path. Measured: `<documents><document>body</document></documents>` (no name attribute) parses to `{"documents":{"document":"\n\\documentclass…\n"}}` — the child is a bare STRING, not an object. ensureArray wraps it to `["…"]`, then `entry.content` is undefined and `entry.name` is undefined, yielding `[{content:'', name:'unnamed'}]`. That is a non-null return, so it short-circuits every downstream recovery tier (filename headers :288-312, fence recovery :326-359, single-doc synthesis :361-376) and writes zero files (processMultipleLatexDocuments:434 skips empty content). Today both the parse tier and the regex tier return null for that input (verified: NONAME_DOCS null, NONAME_REGEX method:"none"), so the later tiers still get their chance. The fix must be `const list = ensureArray(container[OUTPUT_DOCUMENT_TAG]).filter(isObject)` and return null (falling through to the existing log) when `list.length === 0`. `ensureArray` does exist at src/utils/core/index.ts:68, as claimed.

3. Overstated scope wording: "the whole XML tier … never runs for single-output agents". The tier runs on every round; it simply never yields documents for a single-document response. It still serves N>=2 (multi-input polish, workflow edit agents), so this is an unhandled arity, not a dead tier — which is what the finding's own last sentence says, and the headline should match.

4. Understated blast radius, in the finding's favor: the mislabeling is not confined to the log channel. The regex tier reports through `logInternal` with EXTRACTION_METHOD_MESSAGES.simple = 'using fallback method' (:64-68, :88-95), so the agent trace shows "Recovered documents using fallback method (1 document)" on what is actually the protocol-conformant happy path.

5. Severity mechanics worth stating in the issue: `log.error` is ungated — writeLine (src/logger/logUtils.ts:139-155) appends unconditionally to the shared "TeXRA" sink; only the `data` payload is debug-gated. The extension routes it to a VS Code output channel (extension.ts:254); the CLI swallows it only under `quietLogs` (packages/cli/src/runtime/initPlatform.ts:233-237), otherwise it falls back to `console.info`.

6. No test pins the current behavior: XmlOutputManager.vitest.ts has no single-`<document>`-returns-null assertion (its :903-927 case uses two documents), so the fix needs no test rewrite — and per the repo's testing budget, at most one regression test.

7. Claimed -4 is slightly optimistic once the isObject guard and the empty-list fall-through are added back.

<details><summary>Verifier reasoning</summary>

The mechanism is confirmed by execution, not inference: I ran the production `addCdataToTagsMultiple` + `XMLParser(XML_PARSER_OPTIONS)` + `extractContentFromXMLbyTagMultiple` chain on a realistic single-document response and captured exactly two `logger.error` calls plus a null return, with the regex tier recovering the identical content. fast-xml-parser collapses a lone child to an object and the parser config declares no `isArray`, so the `Array.isArray` gate at :142 can never be true for the arity that the repo's own protocol comment (outputFileExtraction.ts:124-125) says is normal (N >= 1). The second log is worse than noise: its text asserts no documents container was found while its own structure dump prints that container. Nothing defends the shape — no comment, no dated ruling, no survey row, no ratchet, no external consumer, single production caller. It is a genuine observability defect on the common path, and it stays a defect regardless of LoC. The one thing the finding gets wrong cuts against its proposed patch rather than its claim: the naive ensureArray turns an unnamed single document into a non-null empty-content result that silently suppresses three later recovery tiers, which is exactly the "silent degradation is a defect" trap CLAUDE.md warns about. Guarded with isObject and an empty-list fall-through, the change is small and safe; unguarded it would be a net regression, which is why I keep the risk at medium — this code decides what gets written into the user's .tex file.

</details>

### checkCoreDependencies throws inside its own try: a missing image tool reports latexindent/perl/gs as missing too, and the composed message never reaches the user

- **Slice**: b36 · **Kind**: defect · **Risk**: low · **Net**: 0 LoC (proposer claimed -6; verifier figure governs)
- **Files**: `src/utils/system/toolUtils.ts`, `packages/extension/src/webview/slices/bannerSlice.ts`

**Evidence**

src/utils/system/toolUtils.ts:403-437. The body probes `['latexindent','perl','gs']` (409-413) and builds an accurate `missingBasicTools` list. Then at 417-428, when `detectImageTool()` returns null it pushes 'gm/magick' and — only when `showError` is true — _throws_ a hand-composed 'Neither GraphicsMagick nor ImageMagick is installed…' message. That throw is caught by this same function's own catch at 431-436, which logs at error and `return ['latexindent','perl','gs','gm/magick']`. Two consequences on the same machine (has latexindent+perl+gs, lacks magick and gm): (a) the returned list is wrong — three installed tools are reported missing; (b) the carefully composed dual-guide message is never delivered, because `reportMissingTool` (46-55, the only path to `platform().toolMissingHandler`) is never called with it; it dies in a log line. Note every _other_ missing tool on this path does surface, via `checkToolInstalled(name, true)` → `reportMissingTool(config.errorMessage, …)` at :314-316 — the image-tool branch is the one that reaches for `throw` instead. Consumer check: `grep -rIn checkCoreDependencies --include=*.ts` → exactly one production caller, packages/extension/src/webview/slices/bannerSlice.ts:39, `await checkCoreDependencies(true)` — i.e. the only production call always takes the broken branch, and its result is posted straight into the dependency banner as `data.missingTools`. So the banner tells a user with a working TeX install to go install latexindent, perl and Ghostscript. Dedupe: `checkCoreDependencies` and `detectImageTool` return zero hits across all five survey docs (rounds 1-4) and zero hits in the 295-title index; round 1's toolUtils work was the `checkToolInstalled('sox')` probe (index line 48) and its verifier explicitly only analysed `checkToolInstalled`'s own catch (49-candidates.md:1290, :1303), never `checkCoreDependencies`. No comment defends the throw — the catch's comment ('If checking fails, assume all tools are missing… safer than silently ignoring') describes an unexpected-failure path, not this deliberate self-throw.

**Proposal**

Replace the throw at 419-427 with `await reportMissingTool(errorMsg, INSTALL_DOCS)` so the composed dual-guide message actually reaches the host handler, and let `missingBasicTools` (now correctly `['gm/magick']`) be returned normally. Leave the outer catch as the genuine unexpected-failure fallback it documents itself to be. Verify against the banner: bannerSlice posts `missingTools` verbatim, so the fix is what makes the banner name only the tools that are actually absent.

**What we give up**

Nothing. The all-four list is not a deliberate 'when in doubt, list everything' policy — that policy lives in the catch, for genuine probe failures. If someone believes the banner should list everything when _any_ core dep is missing, that is a product decision that should be written as such, not achieved by throwing past three successful probes.

**Verifier corrections — these override the evidence and proposal above**

1. netLoc is wrong. Claimed -6; the proposal as written is about 0. Lines 419-427 are a 9-line `if (showError) { const errorMsg = …; throw new Error(errorMsg); }`. Swapping the last line for `await reportMissingTool(errorMsg, INSTALL_DOCS);` is a one-for-one line substitution. The -6 is only reachable by ALSO deleting the outer try/catch, which the finding explicitly declines to do ("Leave the outer catch as the genuine unexpected-failure fallback").

2. Missed consequence of its own fix: once the throw is gone, the try/catch at 406/431-436 becomes provably unreachable, not merely "genuine". Every awaited callee is total — `checkToolInstalled` wraps its whole body in try/catch and returns `false` (:319-327), `reportMissingTool` swallows its own error (:50-54), `detectImageTool` only forwards those — and `Array.prototype.filter`/`push` cannot throw. So the finding's "leave the catch as the genuine unexpected-failure fallback" is factually wrong about what remains: it would be dead code. Deleting it too is the honest landing and gets to roughly -7.

3. The headline user-facing consequence overstates reach. "The banner tells a user with a working TeX install to go install latexindent, perl and Ghostscript" is not currently reachable. `banner: 'dependency'` is set in exactly one place (bannerSlice.ts:42), reached only by `MAIN_VIEW_COMMANDS.RECHECK_DEPENDENCIES`, which is posted from exactly one place (packages/extension/src/webview/frontend/MainApp.ts:470-471) — the `@recheck-dependencies` handler on the banner's own Recheck button. `dependencyBanner$` initializes to `{ visible: false }` (mainViewState.ts:168-170) and nothing else ever turns it on. The banner is dormant: it can only be refreshed once already visible, and nothing makes it visible. The defect is real in the function's contract and in the lost notification; the "banner lies to users" framing is not observable today.

4. "The only production call always takes the broken branch" is loose. It always passes `showError: true`, but the broken branch only executes when `detectImageTool()` returns null. On a machine with magick or gm the function behaves correctly.

5. Minor line-number slips, immaterial: the basic-tool probe is 408-413 (not 409-413), and the throw itself is at :426 (419-427 is the enclosing `if (showError)` block).

6. Missing context the finding should have carried: `src/tools/setup/toolProbing.ts:44-58` (`missingCoreTools`) is a second, correct implementation of the same "either image tool satisfies the requirement, report one `gm/magick` entry" rule, used by `probe_environment` and `verify_setup` via `collectCoreSetupStatus`. Given that the banner is dormant (correction 3), the stronger question is whether `checkCoreDependencies` + the dependency-banner path should be deleted in favor of that owner rather than repaired. That is a different proposal and I do not rule on it here, but a fixer should look at it before spending a PR on the repair.

<details><summary>Verifier reasoning</summary>

The mechanism is exactly as described and I confirmed it line by line at HEAD. `checkCoreDependencies` builds a correct `missingBasicTools` list, then — when no image tool is found and `showError` is true — throws a hand-composed message from inside its own try. Its catch logs at error and returns the hardcoded all-four list, so on a machine that has latexindent, perl and gs but no magick/gm the function returns three false positives, and the dual-guide install message never reaches `platform().toolMissingHandler` (the only path being `reportMissingTool`, which this branch bypasses). Both halves are real defects against the function's own docstring ("Array of missing tool names") and against the pattern every other tool in the file follows at :314-316.

Nothing defends it. The catch comment predates the image branch (confirmed via `git show 9adbe2e685`), the fallback audit's toolUtils ruling is about a different function, and the round-3 ruling on `toolMissingHandler` is about port placement, not about a caller that never calls it. No survey doc, no index title, and no issue covers it.

Two things temper it. First, the claimed -6 is not achievable under the proposed shape — the substitution is line-for-line neutral; the real reduction only appears if the now-provably-unreachable catch also goes, which the finding declines. Second, and more important for anyone acting on this: the dependency banner is currently dormant, because the only thing that can make it visible is a button that only renders once it is already visible. So the wrong list is a latent contract violation rather than a lie a user sees today, and `src/tools/setup/toolProbing.ts` already owns the same rule correctly for the paths that are live. The defect stands; the priority is genuinely low, and a fixer should first weigh deleting this second implementation against repairing it.

</details>

### processPdf2Png silently drops every page past 100 and logs the truncated result as a success

- **Slice**: b36 · **Kind**: amend · **Risk**: low · **Net**: 6 LoC (proposer claimed 4; verifier figure governs)
- **Files**: `src/utils/media/img.ts`, `src/agent/modelHandlers/support/MediaAttachmentProcessor.ts`

**Evidence**

src/utils/media/img.ts:200-242. `PDF_MAX_PAGES = 100`; :229 `const pagesToConvert = Math.min(pageCount, PDF_MAX_PAGES)`; the loop rasterizes only that many, and :236-238 logs `Successfully converted ${base64Images.length} pages from ${pdfPath}` at debug — a line that reads as complete success whether the PDF had 40 pages or 400. No warn, and the return type (`string[] | null`) carries no truncation signal. The consumer confirms the loss is invisible downstream: src/agent/modelHandlers/support/MediaAttachmentProcessor.ts:123-127 takes the array and returns `{kind:'image', mediaType:'image/png', data: pdfResult}` — the model receives the first 100 pages of a 200-page paper with nothing saying the rest exist. Grepped `PDF_MAX_PAGES`, `'100 pages'` and `'first 100'` across src, packages/*/src, packages/extension/resources and docs: two hits, both the definition and the use in this file. The cap is documented nowhere — not in a prompt, not in a doc, not in the tool description — so neither the user nor the model can know it applied. This is exactly the CLAUDE.md rule 'a fallback that masks a failure must be loud — log the cause at warn and surface it — or not exist'; the cap itself is reasonable, its silence is not. Dedupe: no survey doc mentions processPdf2Png, PDF_MAX_PAGES, or img.ts page limits; nothing in the 295-title index touches media rasterization.

**Proposal**

When `pageCount > PDF_MAX_PAGES`, `log.warn` naming the file, the real page count and the cap, and carry the fact to the caller so MediaAttachmentProcessor can prepend a one-line note to the attachment ('showing pages 1-100 of N'). The minimum acceptable fix is the warn; the note to the model is what actually stops it reasoning about a paper it has only half of.

**What we give up**

Nothing is given up — the cap and its protection against a pathological PDF stay exactly as they are. Only the silence goes.

**Verifier corrections — these override the evidence and proposal above**

1. "the return type (`string[] | null`) carries no truncation signal" overstates the blindness. The consumer is NOT blind today: MediaAttachmentProcessor.ts:106 already calls `countPdfPages(mediaFile)` itself and holds `pageCount` in scope at :123, so `pdfResult.length < pageCount` is a truncation test available right now with no signature change. It is unused, not unavailable. That makes the cheapest correct fix a `this.logger.warn` at the consumer (which reaches the run transcript via AgentTrace) rather than a return-type change in img.ts — `log.warn` inside img.ts is a module logger and is the weaker surface of the two. Ideally both: warn in img.ts for the util-level fact, warn on `this.logger` for the user-visible one.

2. Scope is narrower than the title implies. `processPdf2Png` is only reached when `this.capabilities.supportsNativePdf` is false (MediaAttachmentProcessor.ts:111-120 returns the whole PDF untouched for native-PDF models). It is not "every PDF" — it is every over-100-page PDF sent to a non-native-PDF model.

3. The cap is long-standing, not introduced by a recent reduction PR. `git log -S` shows it predates #9486 as the `maxPages: number = 100` default parameter on the old `multiPagePdf2Png`; #9486 (25f3caaeaf) only inlined it as `PDF_MAX_PAGES`. The pre-#9486 code was equally silent, so this is untouched inherited debt, not a regression.

4. Supporting evidence the finding omits, which strengthens it: MediaAttachmentProcessor.ts:325-327 names the entries `${baseName}_page_${index + 1}` with no total, so the model literally sees `paper.pdf_page_100` as the last item. Fixing the name to `_page_${n}_of_${pageCount}` is the cheapest way to carry the fact to the model, since MediaEntry (src/agent/types/mediaTypes.ts) has no text-note kind — "prepend a one-line note to the attachment" as written has no place to live without a new entry shape.

5. Claimed 4 LoC is low. The warn alone is ~5-6 lines after prettier wraps the template literal; carrying the fact to the model adds ~6 more across the two files (pageCount threaded or the filename suffix plus its condition).

<details><summary>Verifier reasoning</summary>

Verified by reading src/utils/media/img.ts:200-247 and src/agent/modelHandlers/support/MediaAttachmentProcessor.ts:100-127, :260-330 and src/agent/types/mediaTypes.ts directly; ran the repo-wide grep for both symbols, grepped the rounds1234 index and all five survey docs, and traced the cap's provenance with `git log -S` (pre-#9486 `maxPages = 100`, inlined by 25f3caaeaf). The truncation is real, unlogged above debug, and terminates in a success-shaped message; the CLAUDE.md silent-degradation rule and review-checklist §15 name this exact pattern, and no dated ruling, comment, guard, ratchet or external contract protects it. It is a genuine low-severity defect, so it survives on defect grounds regardless of its modest positive LoC.

</details>

### cleanupOldFiles is best-effort housekeeping whose failure destroys the caller's already-completed work — including a paid transcription

- **Slice**: b36 · **Kind**: amend · **Risk**: low · **Net**: 9 LoC (proposer claimed 6; verifier figure governs)
- **Files**: `src/utils/files/relativeFS.ts`, `src/tools/media/audio.ts`, `src/utils/files/pastedImageUtils.ts`

**Evidence**

src/utils/files/relativeFS.ts:50-68. `cleanupOldFiles` does readDir → per-entry `await this.stat(filePath)` → `await this.delete(filePath)` inside one `Promise.all`, with no per-entry tolerance: any rejection rejects the whole call. Both the stat and the delete are check-then-act against files that other processes touch — TeXRA runs as extension, desktop and CLI over the same storage root, and all three call this on the same two directories — so an entry that a sibling process deletes between the readDir and the stat (or between the stat and the delete) turns routine housekeeping into a thrown ENOENT. Two of the three call sites run it _after_ the real work has already succeeded, and neither guards it: src/tools/media/audio.ts:177 runs it after `client.audio.transcriptions.create` has returned, inside a try whose catch (:180-185) converts anything thrown into `{success:false, text:'', error}` — so a vanished 3-day-old recording throws away a completed, billed transcription; src/utils/files/pastedImageUtils.ts:46-56 runs it after `StorageFS.write` has already persisted the image, so the paste fails with an error even though the file is on disk and its path was about to be returned. Only the third caller, packages/extension/src/webview/managers/InstructionManager.ts:28-35, wraps it in its own try/catch with a `log.warn`. Dedupe: round 3 did examine this function (survey-round3.md:1804, :1814) and ruled 'the target should be RelativeFS's two extra methods rather than the store split… folding them into BaseFS would be a pure relocation with zero element delta, so it is not worth a PR on its own'. That ruling is about _relocating_ the method and I am not proposing to relocate it; the failure-ownership defect is untouched by it, and no other survey doc mentions cleanupOldFiles.

**Proposal**

Give cleanupOldFiles per-entry tolerance inside the map — catch, `log.warn` with the file and cause (loud, per the §15 rule; not a silent swallow), continue with the rest — so a stale-entry race can never propagate into the caller's result. That also lets audio.ts:177 and pastedImageUtils.ts:54 keep their current unguarded `await` and makes InstructionManager's defensive wrapper redundant rather than load-bearing.

**What we give up**

A genuinely broken storage directory (EACCES on the whole dir, disk failure) stops aborting its caller and becomes a warn per entry instead. That is the right trade for a 3-day GC pass: nothing downstream depends on the cleanup having run, and the warn names the cause.

**Verifier corrections — these override the evidence and proposal above**

1. WRONG: "an entry that a sibling process deletes ... (or between the stat and the delete)". The delete leg is already ENOENT-tolerant — src/platform/defaults/nodeFilesystem.ts:89-104 ends with `catch (err) { if (!isFileNotFoundError(err)) throw err; }`, and the extension host installs the _same_ nodeFilesystem via `createNodePlatform` (packages/extension/src/extension.ts:285-286), so all three hosts use it. Only the readDir→stat window (nodeFilesystem.ts:15-16, bare `fs.promises.lstat`) produces the ENOENT race described. The delete leg still propagates non-ENOENT failures — Windows EPERM/EBUSY when another process holds the .wav or .png open, EACCES, EIO — which is the stronger real-world trigger and should be the finding's headline instead of the ENOENT race.

2. WRONG: "all three call this on the same two directories". RECORDINGS_DIR has exactly one cleanup caller (audio.ts:177; the dir constant is only at audio.ts:22,64,65,177). PASTED_DIR has two (pastedImageUtils.ts:54 and InstructionManager.ts:32). Also, hosts share a storage dir only when opened on the same workspace: StorageFS's base path is `platform().storage.getStoragePath()` (storageFS.ts:19) → `WorkspaceStorageProvider.getStoragePath` (src/platform/defaults/workspaceStorage.ts:180-190), which is a per-workspace subdirectory of the shared root.

3. WRONG (give-up section): "A genuinely broken storage directory (EACCES on the whole dir, disk failure) stops aborting its caller and becomes a warn per entry instead." `await this.readDir(target)` is at relativeFS.ts:54, _outside_ the `.map`. Per-entry tolerance leaves that leg rejecting, so a dir-level EACCES still destroys the transcription — the headline defect stays half-open. The fix must also cover the readDir leg (wrap the whole body, or make the function documented-never-throws), which is the right shape anyway for a void-returning L2/L3 GC pass.

4. WRONG: "makes InstructionManager's defensive wrapper redundant rather than load-bearing." That try (InstructionManager.ts:29-35) also wraps `await StorageFS.ensureDir(PASTED_DIR)` at :31, and it lives inside a `setTimeout` async callback with no rejection owner — removing it converts an ensureDir failure into an unhandled rejection. It must stay; do not price its deletion into the PR.

5. Undercited but supporting: the paste defect reaches all three hosts — savePastedImage* production callers are src/controllers/progressView/ProgressViewCommandHandlers.ts:692, packages/extension/src/webview/managers/InstructionManager.ts:89, and packages/cli/src/runtime/clipboardImage.ts:166.

6. Context the finding should note: BaseFS's own doc comment (src/utils/files/baseFS.ts:24-27, "In VS Code, the provider is replaced with one backed by vscode.workspace.fs") is stale — extension.ts:285 uses createNodePlatform. That staleness is why the ENOENT analysis lands differently than the finding assumed; it is not part of this PR.

7. Round-3's own line is the one with the count error, not the finding: survey-round3.md:1814 says "cleanupOldFiles has 2 callers"; there are 3.

8. LoC misstated — see netLoc.

<details><summary>Verifier reasoning</summary>

The structural defect is unambiguous and independent of how likely the race is: a best-effort 3-day GC pass is sequenced inside the same try as, and after, the caller's completed and already-paid-for work, with no per-entry or per-call tolerance anywhere in the chain (relativeFS.ts:57-67 → Promise.all → first rejection wins). audio.ts:177 is the severe instance — the OpenAI transcription at :171-175 has already returned and been billed, and any throw from cleanup is funneled by the catch at :180-185 into `{ success: false, text: '' }`, so the user pays for a transcript they never see and gets a filesystem error message instead. pastedImageUtils.ts:54 is the same shape at lower stakes: the image is already on disk from :53 and its path is one line from being returned. That two of the three callers are unguarded while the third (InstructionManager.ts:29-35) wraps it in try/catch + log.warn is itself evidence the function's own contract is wrong — the guard belongs in the helper, not scattered at call sites. Where the finding overreaches is the mechanism: the ENOENT race it leads with is already absorbed on the delete leg by nodeFilesystem, so the live triggers are the readDir→stat window and any non-ENOENT unlink/stat failure (Windows file-in-use EPERM being the most plausible). It also misplaces the boundary of its own fix — readDir sits outside the map, so per-entry tolerance alone does not deliver the "nothing downstream depends on the cleanup having run" guarantee the proposal claims. Corrected, the amend is the right one and matches both §15's L2/L3 taxonomy and the round-4 precedent that resolved an identical masking-vs-loudness question by adding a warn rather than deleting a fallback.

</details>

## 4. Refuted — do not re-file

- **fullTranscriptEntryLayout builds the entire tool card — diff hunks included — then throws it away and builds a second one** (slice b3)

  <details><summary>Why it was refuted</summary>

  REFUTED on guard 7 (cost wrong / churn), with the proposed mechanism additionally unworkable as written.

  **The observation is real but the proposal's mechanism is wrong, and it breaks a pinned invariant.**

  The finding's core read checks out: `fullTranscriptEntryLayout` (transcriptEntryLayout.ts:445-480) calls `transcriptEntryLayout(..., mode: 'scrollback-budget', width: printWidth)`, whose tool case (:327-338) runs `toolUseDisplayLines(row, {elide:false, executionLabels, width: columns})`, and then for `row.kind === 'tool'` discards `layout.lines` and runs a second `toolUseDisplayLines` with `{elide:false, executionLabels, compactOutput}` (no `width`). Cache keys at toolRenderers.tsx:442 are `f|n|<columns>|hp` vs `f|<compactOutput ?? 'n'>|d|hp` — genuinely distinct, so the first build is fresh work, not a hit (I confirmed the reader's width is `frameWidth - CONFIRM_CARD_HORIZONTAL_DECORATION`, TranscriptReader.tsx:159, which differs from the static budget's width, and `hydratedTranscript` mints new row objects for spilled rows, so the WeakMap misses anyway).

  **But the proposal — "let `mode === 'scrollback-budget'` decide the width/wrap projection there (it already branches on `useRichDisplay`)" — cannot be done.** `mode: 'scrollback-budget'` has a _second_ production consumer the finding never checked: `staticTranscriptItemBaseMetrics` (StaticConversationTranscript.tsx:278-283), the Static-ring row budget, whose own comment says "Entry metrics come from the same `scrollback-budget` layout the row budget uses, so the ring never pays for a second full layout pass." That path depends on the _rich_ projection (one display line = one terminal row) because the ring's Ink components render richly. Flipping `scrollback-budget` out of `useRichDisplay` changes its row counts, and that exact distinction is pinned by a test: ConversationTranscript.vitest.ts:905-914 asserts `budgetRows > renderedRows` for a 20-line tool row (`scrollback-budget` vs `scrollback` at the same width), then feeds the same numbers to `staticItems`. So the consolidation requires a _fifth_ mode (or an extra `fullOutput` flag) on the shared geometry SSOT — added union surface plus branch updates in `entryBodyLines` (:273), the `elide` check (:331), and `useRichDisplay` (:329) — not a free reuse of an existing branch.

  **Recomputed cost.** Deletions: `fullTranscriptEntryLayout` shrinks from 36 lines to ~27 (the two comment blocks at :450-452 and :460-466 migrate, they don't vanish) → about -9. Additions: new mode member or `fullOutput` flag (+1), `compactOutput?: 'loaded' | 'failed'` on the options interface (+1) and its destructure (+1), threading both into `entryLines` — which already carries six positional params, so a 7th/8th means either two more params or an options-object refactor (+3 minimum, more if a reviewer demands the object), plus a derived `fullFidelity` const to replace the two `mode !== 'scrollback-budget'` checks (+1). Net ≈ **0**, plausibly +2. The claimed -14 is off by the entire claim.

  That leaves a zero-LoC widening of a shared layout API's mode union to remove a computation that is already memoized twice (`entryLinesCache` in transcriptLines.ts:51-73 caps at one build per entry per `${labelsToken}:${cols}`, under a `useMemo` in a pane the user opens on demand). This is precisely the shape section 13 flags: 22 prior "reduction" PRs netting +5,046 LoC. Not a defect either — no user-visible wrong output, no silent degradation; just dead CPU on a cold, doubly-memoized path.

  The related `toolUseMarginBottomRows` third-key note (toolRenderers.tsx:470-471, called twice per layout via :384/:423/:425) is accurate but is offered as an aside with no proposal, so it carries no LoC.

  </details>

- **The approval queue's presentation hook is wrapped in `catch {}`, so a modal can appear with no stream focus and no bell and nobody learns why** (slice b3)

  <details><summary>Why it was refuted</summary>

  REFUTED on kill criterion 6 (wrong read) compounded by criterion 3 (the code explains itself, and the finding's attempt to defeat the comment rests on the misread).

  The finding's whole weight rests on one sentence: "the realistic failure is: the approval modal is presented, the TUI never switches focus to the asking stream, the terminal never rings, and the swallow leaves no trace." I traced every throw path out of `announceApproval` (packages/cli/src/chat/tui/state/subscribeApprovals.ts:535-547). None of them delivers that failure.

  1. `notify('approvalNeeded')` CANNOT THROW. `notify` (packages/cli/src/chat/tui/notifications/terminalNotifier.ts:33-43) does a signal read plus `writeRawStdout`, and `writeRaw` (packages/cli/src/runtime/logSinks.ts:87-98) is itself `if (closed[key]) return; if (stream.destroyed) return; try { stream.write(...) } catch { closed[key] = true; }`. A dead or EPIPE'd stdout is already swallowed one layer down. "The terminal never rings" is not a state this catch can produce — it is a state `writeRaw` produces, silently, on its own, and that is a different site the finding does not cite.

  2. THE `emit` FAN-OUT IS ALREADY LOUD. `defaultSession().events.emit(...)` reaches `SessionEventHub.emit` (src/agent/runtime/SessionEventHub.ts:91-111), whose body is `try { registration.subscriber(event); } catch (err) { logger.warn('Session event subscriber threw', { data: err }); }`. A throwing `setActiveStream` consumer never propagates to `presentForeground` at all — it is caught and warned at exactly the severity the finding asks for. So "the TUI never switches focus and nobody learns why" is already handled by the layer that owns the fan-out.

  3. THE ONE REMAINING PATH IS UNREACHABLE IN PRODUCTION AND NOT SILENT. That leaves `defaultSession()` itself (src/agent/runtime/SessionHandle.ts:869-874) throwing "The default session has not been initialized." The CLI always installs it during startup: `packages/cli/src/runtime/transcriptSession.ts:50` and `:113` call `initializeDefaultSession` on the persistent AND the ephemeral branch, before the chat TUI runs and long before any execution can produce an approval. And if that invariant were ever broken, the TUI would have died far louder and far earlier — `packages/cli/src/chat/tui/state/transcript.ts:89` calls bare `defaultSession().transcripts.get(streamId)` on every transcript read, with no guard at all. Nothing would "silently" reach an approval modal in that world.

  4. THE `tryDefaultSession` CONTRAST IS BACKWARDS. The finding cites TranscriptReader/WorkPlanReader as evidence that a guarded variant is the local idiom. Those two are `packages/cli/src/chat/tui/panes/TranscriptReader.tsx:195` and `panes/WorkPlanReader.tsx:141` (the finding drops the `panes/` segment), and they are READER PANES that render before/outside a run. `subscribeApprovals` runs only under a live host attachment. The differing choice is correct at each site, not an inconsistency.

  5. THE SITE CLASSIFIES AS LEGITIMATE UNDER THE DATED RULING. Review checklist §15 taxonomy (2026-07 error-handling audit, 880 catch sites): "`catch {}` / `.catch(() => {})` WITHOUT a best-effort comment is a blocker." This one has the comment. Its content — the hook "update[s] surrounding TUI state only; approval resolution must remain available" — is precisely the L3 signature ("documented best-effort side write (comment required, never run-critical)"), and as a guard around an injected callback it is equally L1 ("listener fan-out"). Given point 3, the closest masking label is actually M6, "defensive wrapper around code that cannot throw" — and §15's cleaner-solutions menu prescribes "delete-the-guard" for M6, not "add a logger." The finding proposes the opposite of what the ruling it is implicitly invoking would prescribe. (Deleting it is also wrong here — a throwing hook would reject `enqueueApproval`'s promise and strand the caller — so the current shape is the right one.)

  What I concede: the comment does not satisfy the second half of §15's sentence ("and why it cannot hide a programming error"), and the repo's own nearest analogue (SessionEventHub.emit) does log at warn. That is a real but cosmetic gap in a comment, not the defect the finding describes. Under the standing bar it is not worth a PR: the pipeline it guards is loud at both the layer above (emit) and the layer below (writeRaw), and the guard has no reachable production trigger. Judged as a defect finding, the defect is not real — the failure mode asserted cannot occur.

  Dedupe check (clean, and I confirm the finding's own dedupe): no `presentForeground` hit in any of the five survey docs in docs/proposals/, and no approvalQueue presentation-path row in rounds1234-index.md. Round 3's approvalQueue material is the externalInquiry deletion at :1357-1414 and the registry-count KEEP at :1964-1973 — neither touches this. The finding dies on the merits, not on duplication.

  </details>

- **`texra version` resolves --output-format with its own reader that ignores the documented .texra/config.json key and swallows an invalid value** (slice b5)

  <details><summary>Why it was refuted</summary>

  KILLED under rule 2 (a dated ruling decided it), reinforced by rule 3 and a dedupe miss.

  **A dated ruling names both "divergences" as semantics to preserve.** `docs/proposals/2026-08-07-prod-structural-leads-triage.md:335-337`, Wave C, verbatim title:

  > "**version.ts hand-rolls isCliOutputFormat/parseVersionOutputFormat duplicating cliContext.ts's private pickEnum; unify only if warning-silence and no-config-load semantics preserved**"
  > fix: "Owner: cli runtime. Export pickEnum from cliContext.ts …, rewrite version.ts's parseVersionOutputFormat as pickEnum([flagString, cliEnvValue('TEXRA_OUTPUT_FORMAT')], CLI_…"

  That is a 21-verifier, refute-by-default triage of this exact target, and its ruling is the opposite of this finding's: the two behaviors the finding calls a silent defect — no workspace-config load, and no warning on an invalid value — are named as **semantics any unification must preserve**, and the sanctioned fix keeps the two-candidate list (flag, env) with no config candidate. The finding's dedupe checked `rounds1234-index.md` and the four survey docs but not this triage doc, so it re-files a settled lead with an inverted verdict.

  **The constraint is recorded, contrary to the finding's central claim.** The finding asserts "Nothing in version.ts records that constraint." The record is the test it cites itself, whose _name_ states the intent: `src/test-kernel/cli/CliRootArgs.vitest.ts:1470` — `it('prints version output without resolving workspace context', …)` — with a sibling at :1485, `it('honors TEXRA_OUTPUT_FORMAT for version output without workspace context', …)`. Both run `--cwd /definitely/missing/texra-version-test`. "Without resolving workspace context" is exactly the design; not loading `.texra/config.json` is the point of the command, not a drift. Provenance agrees: `7c72aa38d3` ("fix(cli): honor structured version output", 2026-06-30) introduced `parseVersionOutputFormat` deliberately, its body describing "lightweight version output" and adding those very tests in the same commit.

  So the remaining true statements — `texra version` ignores `texra.outputFormat`, and swallows an invalid `--output-format` — are a documented-elsewhere design point plus, at most, a one-sentence doc gap in `docs/guide/texra-cli.md`, not an "undocumented, unexplained, silently-diverging second resolver." The finding's own option 1 would violate the standing ruling; option 2 reduces to a comment and a doc caveat, which does not clear the bar for a medium-risk defect.

  </details>

- **buildDesktopMenuTemplate reads DESKTOP_MENU_GROUPS positionally, so a third group would vanish from the native menu while the palette picks it up** (slice b8)

  <details><summary>Why it was refuted</summary>

  REFUTED under criterion 7 (cost wrong + churn). The reads are accurate and the finding is not a duplicate, but it fails the bar it must clear.

  **It is not a defect.** The finding's own kind is `amend` and its claim is conditional: "a third group _would_ vanish." At HEAD the native menu is correct — `DESKTOP_MENU_GROUPS` is a 2-tuple (`as const` on the literal at `desktopCommandSurface.ts:69-90` fixes its length at 2), and `desktopMenuTemplate.ts:60-62` renders both of its elements. Nothing is dropped, mislabeled, or unreachable today. So the "a defect survives even at zero LoC" exemption does not apply; this must be judged as a simplification, and it is LoC-neutral.

  **The claimed −2 LoC is wrong; the finder's own proposed snippet is exactly 0.** Current form is 5 lines (`desktopMenuTemplate.ts:59-63`). Running the finder's exact replacement through the repo's prettier:

  ```
    submenu: DESKTOP_MENU_GROUPS.flatMap((group, index) =>
      index === 0
        ? group.map(commandItem)
        : [{ type: 'separator' } as const, ...group.map(commandItem)],
    ),
  ```

  is also 5 lines. Net 0, not −2. The tightest variant that survives prettier

  ```
    submenu: DESKTOP_MENU_GROUPS.flatMap((group, index) => [
      ...(index > 0 ? [{ type: 'separator' } as const] : []),
      ...group.map(commandItem),
    ]),
  ```

  is 4 lines: net −1 at best, on a file with one consumer.

  **It is speculative generality, which the charter says to remove, not add.** The edit trades a literal that reads "group, separator, group" for an index-compared ternary inside a flatMap, purchasing tolerance for an event that has never occurred: a third TeXRA-submenu section. The trigger is a developer editing `DESKTOP_MENU_GROUPS` — and that developer is already forced by the compiler to touch two other tables in the same file (`DESKTOP_COMMAND_ICONS` and `DESKTOP_COMMAND_HANDLERS`, both `satisfies Record<DesktopCommandId, …>`) and would see the new command's absence in the very menu they added it for. This is a developer-time slip caught by the author's own first smoke test, not a runtime silent degradation of the kind §15 of the review checklist targets (that section is about a fallback masking a _runtime_ failure nobody reports). "Cut before add" and the abstraction-discipline guardrail both cut against a zero-LoC hardening of a stable two-consumer seam.

  **The `Give up` clause misidentifies its own strongest counter.** It only concedes if the group list is "frozen by product decision," which nothing states. The real counter is that the change is line-neutral and the hazard is self-revealing, so the campaign's own churn arithmetic (section 13: 22 prior "reduction" PRs netted +5,046 LoC) rules it out regardless of whether a third group is ever added.

  Criteria 1-6 do NOT hold, and I want that on the record so this is not re-litigated as a dedupe or misread kill: `grep -rn DESKTOP_MENU_GROUPS` over `docs/` returns nothing; the title is absent from the 295-entry rounds1234 index; the only prior mention of `desktopCommandSurface.ts` in the survey corpus is round 2's verify-fixes.spec.ts entry (corrections 4/6 there concern `DESKTOP_COMMAND_ICONS` and `getDesktopCommandMenuEntries`, not the menu grouping), so there is no dated ruling either way. The file header comment (`:1-9`) is about _where_ Electron types may live, not about the positional read, and the finding correctly declines to treat it as a justification.

  </details>

- **A user-triggered state restore is re-validated against the schema that produced it, and the unreachable failure arm drops it to console.warn** (slice b10)

  <details><summary>Why it was refuted</summary>

  REFUTED on criterion 2/5 (a dated family-level KEEP the candidate never read or quoted) compounded by criterion 7 (churn-class, and the third time this exact lens has been litigated in this campaign).

  (1) A DATED RULING ALREADY DECIDED THIS FAMILY, AND SAID SO IN ORDER TO STOP THIS RE-AUDIT.

  `docs/proposals/2026-08-16-overdefensive-top10.md:522` opens "## 4. Runners-up (all explicit KEEP — recorded so later waves don't re-audit)", and its FIRST bullet (:524-525) is:

  "- Boundary safeParse corpus (~120 sites) — true boundaries (external APIs, persisted files, IPC/webview wire, model-output JSON)."

  The site under attack, `packages/extension/src/webview/MainViewProvider.ts:384`, is a `safeParse` whose `parsed.data` is the very next statement's `postToWebview(...)` payload — i.e. it sits on the IPC/webview wire, one of the four categories the KEEP enumerates. That doc shipped as #10732 (MERGED) with the whole #10756/#10757-#10769 follow-up tree; every entry that was actionable got an issue, and §4 exists precisely so later waves stop enumerating individual sites in these families. The candidate's dedupe section checks only the rounds-1-4 index and the four survey docs. It never mentions `overdefensive-top10.md`, never quotes §4, and therefore does not beat it.

  The counter the candidate would have to make — "this one is not a _true_ boundary because its input arrived through an in-process typed array, not off the wire" — is exactly the move round 2 already adjudicated and rejected. `docs/proposals/2026-08-26-simplification-survey-round2.md:3579` ruled on the one hunk that provably dented §4's characterization: "It is true that :527 carries no written rationale, which mildly dents the doc's characterization. But … Denting a KEEP's phrasing to buy zero lines is not beating the ruling." Same structure here: the candidate dents "true boundary" for one site and buys six lines.

  (2) THIRD LITIGATION OF THE IDENTICAL SHAPE, AT THE SAME MAGNITUDE THE CAMPAIGN HAS TWICE CALLED CHURN.

  Round 2 refuted "Drop four redundant defensive copies/re-parses on same-process typed handoffs" (index line 146; doc :3563-3588) at ~-3 LoC / 0 elements. Round 1 refuted two structurally identical candidates ("the last defensive copies in syncSlice…", "a defensive array copy and 21 per-site `satisfies`") partly on the same inflated-arithmetic grounds. This candidate is the same lens ("value re-validated against the schema that produced it, same process") at -6 LoC and **zero** element delta: no export removed, no file removed, no knip-baseline row, no ratchet row. Checklist §14 R6 (`.claude/skills/code-review/references/review-checklist.md:128`) is the governing bar — "A `refactor:`/`simplify:` … PR body must report constructs added vs deleted … alongside net LoC" — and there is nothing to report. Section 13's +5,046 LoC record is the reason the bar exists.

  The candidate's own escape hatch confirms the churn reading: its fallback proposal ("route the failure through `createLog(...).error` and surface it") is net **+1 LoC or worse**, and a reviewer who takes §15 seriously would pick exactly that arm — the arm the candidate offers is the one that loses lines, not the one it argues for.

  (3) WHAT DOES _NOT_ KILL IT, for the record, so a re-file knows where the real ground is.

  The mechanical claims are all correct, and I verified each: `setPendingState` has exactly one production call site (`stateRestoreCommand.ts:53`) and `consumePendingState` exactly one (`MainViewProvider.ts:380,382`, plus a vi.mock at `src/test-kernel/webview/SidebarSurfaceOwnership.vitest.ts:61-62`); `pendingStateManager.ts:14-28` stores the value verbatim; `buildMainViewState` does end in `MainViewPersistedStateSchema.parse` (`src/controllers/mainView/MainViewStateRestoreController.ts:51`); the schema is idempotent on its own output; and there really are exactly two `console.*` calls in the non-frontend extension host (`MainViewProvider.ts:386` and `extensionCommandSurface.ts:183`). The failure arm is genuinely unreachable. That makes this dead code, not a live defect — no user can hit the drop the candidate describes, so the defect-exemption ("survives even at zero LoC") does not apply and it is judged as the deletion it is filed as.

  If someone re-files this, the argument that has a chance is the one the candidate did not make: `postToWebview` at `MainViewProvider.ts:114-129` carries a written policy comment — "In dev/test runs the payload goes through the boundary's outbound schemas first (`assertKnownOutbound Message`) … production posts the typed payload as-is with no parse cost" — and `MainViewMessageSchema`/`CommonViewMessageSchema` include `state: MainViewPersistedStateSchema.nullish()` (`src/shared/schemas/commonViewMessages.ts:34`). So :384 is a _third_ parse in dev/test and the only outbound parse the file pays for in production, in direct tension with the policy its own file states three hundred lines earlier. That is a consistency argument against a documented owner rather than a line-count argument, and it would have to be batched with the rest of the outbound-post surface to clear R6. On its own it is still six lines.
