- **Two conventions for clearing an optional backend-owned field in one merge: `stage` rides a nullable wire value, its three siblings ride key-absence** (slice b13)

  <details><summary>Why it was refuted</summary>

  REFUTED on three independent grounds.

  **(2) A dated ruling decided this exact target, the other way, and forbade it as a standalone step.** `docs/proposals/2026-08-03-ssot-consolidation-plan.md` §A2 (:156-168) names the same two symbols the finding names: "Today: `undefined → null` at the producer …, hand-unwrapped at two consumers (`streamStateMerge.ts:14-19`, `syncSlice.ts:21-22`) … **Fix:** `.transform(v => v ?? undefined)` on `StreamMetadataSchema`'s … stage fields … **The wire keeps `null` (explicit clear semantics); consumers receive `undefined` uniformly.** … **Delete:** `metadataToStreamStatePartial` (`streamStateMerge.ts:9-21`)." `metadataToStreamStatePartial` is in that plan's §8 consolidated deletion ledger (:745). The follow-up plan re-scopes it: `docs/proposals/2026-08-04-ssot-consolidation-part-2.md` §L1 (:361-372) — "**L1. `StreamStage` end-to-end (extends A2)** … Store `stage: StreamStage | null` end-to-end; renderers call `formatStageLabel`; delete the shims and fallbacks. **Do A2's nullability heal as part of this, not as a separate intermediate state.**" The ruling keeps `null` on the wire, heals on the read side with a schema transform, and explicitly rules out landing the nullability change on its own. The finding proposes the inverse (delete the nullable wire, move `stage` onto omission-clearing) as a standalone change, and never cites either doc.

  **(6) Wrong read of the blast radius — twice.**
  (a) "one producer (`buildStreamMetadata`, whose only caller is `LitSessionRenderer.metadataFor`)" is false at HEAD. `buildStreamMetadata` has **two** production callers: `src/controllers/progressView/backend/LitSessionRenderer.ts:440` and `packages/trace-viewer/src/replayTrace.ts:216` — a separate app whose tsc is not in the root typecheck.
  (b) More damaging: `stage` has a **third** wire encoding the finding does not mention, and it is required-and-nullable, where omission genuinely cannot express clearing. `src/shared/schemas/progressView/projectionShape.ts:44-46` — `const ActiveStateSectionSchema = z.strictObject({ … stage: StreamContentProjectionLeaves.stage.nullable(), … })` — the field is **not optional**, so a cleared stage must ride an explicit `null`; its consumer is `packages/extension/src/progressView/frontend/slices/syncSlice.ts:17-20` (`const { conversationProgress, stage, badges } = data.activeState; … stage: stage ?? undefined`). The same `stage` fact therefore already travels one path where `null` is mandatory. Moving `StreamMetadata.stage` to omission-clearing makes the two stage encodings **diverge**, which is the opposite of the finding's stated payoff ("one convention, not two"). This is exactly why A2/L1 ruled for the null direction.

  **(3) The code's own comment is not defeated.** `StreamMetadataSchema`'s "Nullable over the wire: an explicit `null` clears a stage the frontend still holds, which a plain omission cannot express" (streamState.ts:150-153) is read as a claim about the same-category merge arm and refuted with the three sibling `hasOwn` deletes. But `stage`'s sibling on the _other_ stream-content path is `strictObject`-required, and there omission is literally unrepresentable. The comment states the wire-level invariant for the field, and the finding only attacks one of its two carriers.

  Mechanically the proposed edit does work (buildStreamMetadata is the only constructor of `StreamMetadata`; the restore list plus `Object.hasOwn` would clear identically on both hops) — it is not refuted for being broken. It is refuted for being a settled question answered the other way, for missing a producer, and for leaving the codebase with two divergent `stage` wire conventions instead of one.

  </details>

- **Anthropic tool attachments are uploaded to the Files API and the file id is never used — so the conversation-wide PDF page budget is wiped on every request** (slice b17)

  <details><summary>Why it was refuted</summary>

  REFUTED on criterion 6 (wrong read) plus a prior deliberate decision the finding never engages.

  **The headline mechanism is false.** The finding claims tool-attached PDFs stay `source:{type:'base64'}` forever, so their page counts are pruned every request and `getTrackedPdfPageCount()` "reads ~0 at the start of every buildToolResultBlock" — and calls this an "asymmetry" with the message-level path. It is not an asymmetry. `replaceDocumentDataWithUploads` (anthropicDocumentHandling.ts:165-241) walks messages through `iterateDocumentSources` -> `extractDocumentBlocks` — the _same_ walker `collectFileReferenceCounts` uses, which the finding itself quotes as descending into `tool_result` content (anthropicDocumentHandling.ts:34-50, comment explicitly names "PDFs attached as tool result attachments (e.g., from ArXiv downloads)... nested inside tool_result content"). So a tool-attached PDF is picked up by the message-level replacement on the very next request: it is re-uploaded, its `source` is rewritten in place to `{type:'file', file_id}` (line 236-237), and `onPageCount(fileId, pageCount)` re-registers the page count (modelHandlerAnthropic.ts:1016).

  Ordering confirms self-healing, not wiping. Inside `createResponseImpl`: `analyzeDocumentSources` (:921) sets `hasBase64Pdf`, `pruneTrackedFileMetadata` (:925-929) drops the now-orphaned tool-upload id, then `replaceDocumentDataWithUploads` (:1010-1019) re-uploads and re-registers under a new id — all before the request is dispatched, and long before the _next_ `buildToolResultBlock` runs. The `messages` array is the live one (`enforceCacheControlLimit(messages, ...)` at :913 mutates it in place too), so the rewrite persists across turns. Net effect: the conversation-wide page budget does accumulate; `getTrackedPdfPageCount()` at the next tool result is the sum of every PDF still live in history, and the "{remaining} of {max} PDF pages remaining in this conversation" string (:1756-1762) is substantially correct, not "computed from a wiped counter". I verified `supportsNativePdf` is `true` for every Anthropic model in llm-zoo (fable5/mythos5/opus5/opus48/... all `pdf:true`), so the replacement branch is not a theoretical path.

  **The primary proposal is a revert of a deliberate fix.** `git log -S "uploaded.base64Data"` returns exactly one commit: d8f5f70fc7 "fix: inline anthropic tool attachments" (2025-10-10), whose diff does precisely the opposite of what is proposed — it _replaces_ `source: {type:'file', file_id: uploaded.fileId}` with inline base64 in both the image and document arms of the tool-result builder. The proposal to "make the Anthropic tool-result blocks reference what was uploaded: source:{type:'file', file_id}" is a straight revert of that fix, offered with zero evidence that file sources are accepted inside `tool_result` content (the finding asserts "both shapes are supported once FILES_API_BETA is on" without citation; the Files API docs cover top-level user-content document/image blocks). Reverting a fix commit on an unverified API-shape assumption is a live regression risk for every Anthropic tool-use session that returns a PDF or image.

  What survives is only the finding's _secondary_ observation, and only in its _alternative_ form: the Files API upload inside `uploadToolAttachments` (anthropicTools.ts:120-125) is dead work. Its `fileId` is never referenced by any content block; for images it is used for nothing at all, and for PDFs only as a map key for a count that the message-level path re-derives one request later from a second upload of the same bytes. That is a real redundant network round trip per attachment plus an orphaned object in the org's Anthropic Files storage — but it is a small waste/cleanup item, not the "conversation-wide PDF page budget is wiped on every request" defect this finding is titled and risk-rated for, and its correct remedy is the finding's own discarded fallback, not its proposal. That reframed item should be re-filed on its own if the parent wants it; as written, the finding is refuted.

  </details>

- **The desktop main process hand-copies AgentDirectoryService.getDirectory's source→directory switch, comment included** (slice b17)

  <details><summary>Why it was refuted</summary>

  REFUTED on guardrails 2/5 (a dated ruling pins this port's shape, on the frozen SDK surface) and 7 (cost recomputed: the proposal is net-POSITIVE LoC, not -10).

  **1. The load-bearing premise is factually false.** The finding asserts "`AgentDirectoryService`, its sole implementation, already satisfies it" and "the only implementation behind that port is `AgentDirectoryService`". I grepped every construction site of `AgentDirectoriesPort`. There are at least six, and only one of them is `AgentDirectoryService`:
  - `packages/agent/src/node.ts:60-64` — a production inline literal (`custom: async () => options.agentsDir, builtIn: async () => '', builtInToolUse: async () => ''`), the SDK's own `createNodePlatform` bootstrap.
  - `src/test-kernel/support/FakePlatform.ts:585-589` — `const FAKE_AGENT_DIRECTORIES: AgentDirectoriesPort`, the shared fake reached by every `createFakePlatform` suite.
  - `src/test-kernel/agent/AgentRegistry.vitest.ts:55-72` — two typed literals (`testAgentDirectories()` and `mutableAgentDirectories`).
  - `src/test-kernel/agent/runtime/agentLoad.vitest.ts:239-243` and `:528-537` — two more typed literals.
    Adding a **required** member to a structural interface forces an edit at every one of them. The finding's entire "+1 declaration, zero new implementations" economics rests on a count that is off by five.

  **2. A dated architecture ruling fixes this port at exactly three methods, for embedders.** `docs/architecture/2026-07-26-embedding-the-agent-runtime.md` §2 is titled "`AgentDirectoriesPort` is three directory paths, not agent values", quotes the interface verbatim, and rules: "Three methods, each returning a **directory path string**. The port cannot carry an agent definition, a parsed object, a YAML string, or a virtual filesystem. Injecting it redirects the scan to _a different real directory on disk_; that is the entire capability." At `:340-353` it instructs embedders directly: "An embedder is free to supply a three-line literal instead:" followed by the exact three-method literal. `AgentDirectoriesPort` is a required field of `NodePlatformServices` (`src/platform/defaults/nodeHost.ts:70`), the documented SDK-embedder bootstrap contract (same doc, `:45`, `:107-114`, `:205-212`), on a surface CLAUDE.md calls "frozen, not open" with the Tier-1 public manifest still unfinished. Adding a fourth required member breaks every three-line literal that doc told people to write — starting with the repo's own at `packages/agent/src/node.ts:60`. The round-1 verifier already applied this exact reasoning to this exact surface (`docs/proposals/2026-08-25-simplification-survey-49-candidates.md:2469`).

  **3. Recomputed cost is net-positive.** Desktop: `packages/desktop/src/main/index.ts:672-686` is 15 lines → 1 line, so **-14**. Against that: `interfaces.ts` +1; `packages/agent/src/node.ts` +3 (it cannot delegate — it must hand-roll `custom → agentsDir`, builtIn/builtInToolUse → `''`, remote/inline → `undefined`); `FakePlatform.ts` +4; `AgentRegistry.vitest.ts` +5; `agentLoad.vitest.ts` +4 (two literals); plus the loose `vi.mock` objects at `ApplyTeamTool.vitest.ts:81`, `AgentCategoryResolution.vitest.ts:74`, `CliAgentShadow.vitest.ts:52`. That is roughly **+17 against -14 ≈ +3 net**. Section 13's "+5,046 LoC from 22 reduction PRs" is precisely this pattern: one visible deletion paid for by scattered additions the estimate never counted.

  **4. What survives is smaller than the finding claims.** The duplication itself is real — I re-read both sites and confirm `AgentDirectoryService.getDirectory` (`:62-76`) and the desktop switch (`:672-686`) state the same mapping with paraphrased comments, and that the extension routes through the owner (`agentHandlers.ts:74,84` → `AgentDirectoryManager.ts:75-77`). But it is one 15-line switch appearing twice, in two hosts, with the mapping already exhaustively type-checked in both places (`AgentSource` is a closed union; a sixth member breaks the desktop switch at compile time too, since neither switch has a `default`). The finding's stated hazard — "adding a sixth `AgentSource` member would silently leave the desktop switch non-exhaustive-by-copy rather than by compiler error" — is wrong: TypeScript's return-type analysis flags a non-exhaustive switch in a function declared to return `Promise<string | undefined>` at _both_ sites, so the duplicate costs a second mechanical edit, not silence. That downgrades this from a correctness risk to ~14 lines of cosmetic restatement, which does not buy an SDK-contract break.

  The finding's own escape hatch (desktop consuming the concrete `AgentDirectoryService` it builds at `packages/desktop/src/main/platform/index.ts:86`) is ratchet-safe — `AgentDirectoryService` is already exported from the `@agent/index` barrel desktop imports at `main/index.ts:30`, so no new deep-import specifier — but the instance lives in `platform/index.ts`, not `main/index.ts`, so it needs a second access path around `platform()`. Trading a duplicated switch for a shadow handle that bypasses the platform port is the dual-system trade CLAUDE.md's design guardrails reject.

  </details>

- **Anthropic treats every 3-output-token response as an empty response and throws away real short answers** (slice b18)

  <details><summary>Why it was refuted</summary>

  REFUTED by the maintainer 2026-08-27. The guard is a deliberate empirical sentinel, not a content-length check, and the finding inverted its meaning. (1) It is `=== 3`, not `< 3`: exact equality matches one specific observed Anthropic billing signature for a structurally empty response; a naive short-content guard would be a threshold. (2) TeXRA never requests 3-token completions - every generation path calls extractNormalizedResponse(responseObject, endTag, ...) with a required end tag, so structured tagged output is always expected; a legitimate short answer arrives wrapped in tags and is nowhere near 3 tokens. (3) Retryability is the correct handling for a genuinely empty API response, not evidence of waste. The only defensible residue is documentation: the comment says "Anthropic specific empty response check" without recording WHY 3, which is a comment improvement and not worth a PR on its own.

  </details>

- **createHelperModelKit's "Model is not recognized" branch is statically unreachable — the same guard runs one line earlier** (slice b21)

  <details><summary>Why it was refuted</summary>

  REFUTED on rule 7 (cost wrong / churn), with a supporting rule-3 and rule-2 hit. The reachability analysis is correct; the deletion is not achievable.

  1. THE HEADLINE DELETION IS 0 LoC, NOT -9. The guard at helperModel.ts:45-50 is not defensive garbage — it is the type narrowing `createModelHandler(originalConfig: ModelConfig, ...)` (ModelFactory.ts:386-390) requires. `resolveRuntimeModelConfig` returns `ModelConfig | undefined`. The finding's two offered routes both fail:
     (a) "Resolve the config first and derive the recognition failure from that single lookup" — I wrote it out: `const modelConfig = await resolveRuntimeModelConfig(...)` / `if (!modelConfig) return {kit: undefined, reason: '...'}` / `const reason = await getModelUnavailableReason(...)` / `if (reason) return {kit: undefined, reason}`. Both lookups still run, the `Model "X" is not recognized.` string still lives in helperModel.ts, and the line count is identical (12 lines before, ~12 after under prettier). The finding's own claim "either way one of the two 'not recognized' strings goes" is false for this route: nothing is deleted, only reordered. Pure churn.
     (b) "Keep the current order and drop lines 45-50, narrowing via the already-proven lookup" — TypeScript cannot narrow across the `getModelUnavailableReason` call; `npm run typecheck` fails. It only compiles with `modelConfig!`. `rg` for non-null assertions across `src/agent/runtime/*.ts` returns 0 — the subtree does not use them at all. So this route buys ~-4 net lines (6 removed, an assertion plus a comment explaining the cross-module invariant added back) by converting a compiler-enforced total function into a hand-maintained assumption about the internals of a module in a different directory.

  2. THE REPO ALREADY RULED ON THIS EXACT UNREACHABILITY AND CHOSE THE OPPOSITE (rule 3, and the finding cites the evidence against itself). computeModelOptions.ts:203-207: "Unreachable from `getModelUnavailableReason` today (it returns its own 'not recognized' message before a config resolves far enough to compute availability at all), but the table must still cover it: `unknown-model` is `available: false`, so leaving it out would defeat the whole point of this table being compiler-checked." The finding quotes this comment as proof the branch is dead, but the comment's actual holding is that being unreachable-from-`getModelUnavailableReason` is not a reason to drop an arm the type system wants. Route (b) is precisely the trade that comment refuses.

  3. THE RESIDUAL (helperModelPreference) HAS A FALSE RATIONALE AND SITS UNDER A STANDING "DO NOT REWRITE" RULING. The stated benefit — "a workflow-category launch does not pay for a value it never reads" — is wrong. Line 41 calls `getModelUnavailableReason(helperModel)`, which itself awaits `discoveredCopilotRoutes()` unconditionally (computeModelOptions.ts:502). The ONLY path that skips line 41 is the ToolUse early return at :39, which is exactly the path that needs the lookup. So moving the await inside the guard saves one `MODEL_CONFIGS[model]` property read and nothing else on any path. Meanwhile docs/proposals/2026-08-12-agent-sdk-readiness-reverify.md:82-86 rules on this exact function: "The one arguable single-caller extraction, `applyHelperModelPreference` (`helperModelPreference.ts:24`, one production caller `runAgent.ts:101`) ... earned under the 'single-caller extractions banned unless real logic' rule, barely. Watch, do not rewrite." Re-affirmed at docs/proposals/2026-08-14-agent-sdk-readiness-reverify.md:169-171: "Standing watch-items, unchanged: `applyHelperModelPreference` ... Revisit only if edited for another reason." A ~-4-line body rewrite whose stated motive evaporates on inspection is not "another reason".

  Net: the finding is a correct observation attached to a proposal that yields 0 LoC safely, or ~-4 LoC by giving up compiler-checked narrowing in a subtree with zero non-null assertions, plus ~-4 LoC of rewrite in a function two dated docs say to leave alone. That is section 13's pattern.

  </details>

Commit bcf1b7aa7c (#11184, merged 2026-08-20, five days ago) says verbatim in its message: "7481e16337 deleted the COPILOT arm, the only branch that ever returned a key. `inferPersistedModelHandlerCompatibilityKey` can now only throw (Google) or return undefined, which makes the `if (compatibilityKey)` logging branch in the wrapper statically unreachable. Drop the wrapper and call the guard directly; drop `asRecord`, a single-caller helper whose docstring still described shape-sniffing call sites that no longer exist." That PR asserts the finding's entire premise as established fact, refers to the survivor as "the guard" in prose, harvested everything actually dead around it (inferAndLogPersistedModelHandlerCompatibilityKey, asRecord, and in the review follow-up the tautological logger mock in ModelHandlerCompatibilityInference.vitest.ts), and deliberately kept the signature. The proposal's literal call-site rewrite (`if (key === undefined) assert...`) lets a persisted `null` skip the Google throw and flow through as `null` - the exact `=== undefined` vs `== null` trap CLAUDE.md names. The two sites are also not symmetric, contrary to "the same `??` for the workflow record": the tool-use schema (implementations/flows/tooluse/nodes/types.ts:54) is `.nullable().transform((key) => key ?? undefined).optional()`, so only there is the RHS a pure constant.

Recomputed: guard body -1 line (drop `return undefined;`); flow variant about -1 (swap the delegating return plus its 2-line comment for `assert(...)` + `return undefined;`); each of the two call sites GROWS from a 3-line `??` expression to a prettier-wrapped 2-statement form (4-5 lines), and the workflow site needs an added `?? undefined` coercion to keep its declared return type; plus the rename in the vitest import and the @agent type surface. Honest net is about +2, not -10. This is precisely the section-13 shape: a four-file rename across a resume path that buys a better name and no lines.

Never throws: the description is presentation metadata, not lifecycle state'), the write is serialized through enqueueMetaUpdate (:65 comment documents the race it prevents), and the checklist's no-downgrade-below-warn rule targets read failures that change run behavior — this is a side write whose failure costs only a display label. The only defensible tweak would be debug->warn for symmetry with the rest of this file ..., but the site's comment explicitly defeats a masking claim... Recording as keep so round 5 does not re-litigate it. Dedupe: no rounds-index or survey-doc entry names writeSessionDescription.

The ruling's basis is that a failed side write "costs only a display label"; the finding's harm is exactly a display label that is present for the live session and absent after restart. The proposed remedy is arguably worse for the user: skipping the emit means no label at all in the live session instead of a transient one, on a path that only fires when meta.json is missing/unreadable or the run was deleted under the process. That is a UX preference argument, not a new defect class, and CLAUDE.md's loudness rule is already discharged by the ruling's optional debug->warn note.

The mechanics in the finding are read correctly — it is the novelty and the dedupe that fail.

- **The orphan-stream sweep bypasses SessionStores' own deletion queue and fans out unbounded, unlike both sweeps on either side of it in the same call chain** (slice b22)

  <details><summary>Why it was refuted</summary>

  REFUTED on rule 6 (wrong read of where serialization lives) and rule 3 (the code explains itself, with explicit guards for exactly the interleaving claimed), with rule 7 (cost wrong) killing the second consequence.

  The line-level reads are accurate — `sweepOrphanedStreams` (SessionStores.ts:756-833) really does use an unbounded `Promise.all` (778-828) and really does call `deleteExecutionWithStreamState` (783) and `deleteStreamSidecars` (818) outside `enqueueDeletion`, while its two neighbours enter the queue. What is wrong is the inference that this is a defect.

  (a) The "queue's guarantee is not global" argument attributes the wrong authority. `SessionStores.deletionQueue` is a concurrency-1 PQueue _on one instance_ (`:120`); hosts sharing ~/.texra each have their own, so it was never the serializer for staged sidecar work. The serialization that actually protects a staged deletion is per-stream and one layer down, in `StagedDeletionCoordinator`, and it defeats the claimed interleaving explicitly:
  - `stage()` (StagedDeletionCoordinator.ts:461-473) is per-stream single-flight — it loops awaiting `current.settled` / `recoverFailedRollback` before it will stage the same stream again. Concurrent stagings of _distinct_ streams are the designed mode; the orphan sweep operates on distinct streams by construction (it filters on `!liveStreams.has(stream)`).
  - `recoverPendingRollbacks()` — the one thing `flush()` does that could touch a staged deletion — skips in-flight stagings outright: `if (state.kind !== 'staging') await this.recoverFailedRollback(...)` (:205-209). So the claimed race "a concurrent orphan sweep's staged sidecar deletion can be mid-flight when that flush runs" is the case the code deliberately guards.
  - `reconcile()` does the same twice: `if (deletionState?.kind === 'staging') return;` (:268) and `if (!liveStreams.has(stream) || state.kind === 'staging') return;` (:301). That is the direct answer to "move `reconcileStagedDeletions` (765) inside the queue too."
  - `StreamSnapshotStore` reinforces this: per-stream seed queues (`seedQueues` / `seedQueueFor`, :514-518) and per-key write mutexes (`queueWrite`, :1578-1590). And `stageDeleteStream`'s own commit path calls `await this.flush()` (:1196) from inside a deletion — the store calls the global drain from within deletion commits by design, so "flush concurrent with a deletion" is not an anomaly the queue was introduced to prevent.
  - `DELETION_IO_CONCURRENCY = 8` (StagedDeletionCoordinator.ts:53), used by all three of the coordinator's `pMap`s, is the subsystem stating that concurrent multi-stream deletion I/O is expected, bounded where it matters.

  (b) The fan-out cost is materially miscomputed, three ways.
  - `claimLease` re-reads _that execution's own claims directory_ (`judgeClaims(executionId, root)` → `readClaims(executionId, root)`), not a shared directory of all leases. An orphaned execution normally has no surviving claim, so `judgeClaims` returns an empty list and no owner probe runs at all.
  - Owner probing is gated behind `pidProvablyDead(pid)` (leaseOwnerLiveness.ts:93-99), a bare `process.kill(pid, 0)` syscall. `platform().processes.identity(pid)` is only reached for a foreign pid that still exists — i.e. pid reuse or a genuinely live owner, not the normal orphan case.
  - The one probe that does run per claim, `currentLeaseOwner()` → `platform().processes.selfIdentity()`, is memoized: `selfIdentity ??= await readIdentity(process.pid)` (nodeProcesses.ts:105-110). So the whole process pays at most one `ps`, not one per orphan. The quoted Windows "few hundred milliseconds" comment sits on `readWindowsIdentity`, reached only via those same gated paths.
    So "One `Promise.all` over the full orphan set therefore fans that out with no bound" describes a spawn storm that cannot occur. What remains is unbounded _file_ I/O and N global `flush()` drains — a hygiene nit with no demonstrated failure, and the codebase's settled precedent for bulk deletion is bounded-parallel, not serial: `deleteAllExecutions` uses `pMap(..., { concurrency: EXECUTION_STORAGE_CONCURRENCY })` = 32 (executionListing.ts:44, 444). "Serialize it like its neighbours" argues against the repo's own bulk-deletion pattern.

  The proposal also carries a regression the finding does not price. Wrapping each per-orphan unit in `enqueueDeletion` puts `claimLease` inside the concurrency-1 queue, and `claimLease` can spin with `delay(CLAIM_RECHECK_MS)` up to `MAX_CLAIM_ROUNDS` nested rounds (executionLease.ts:498-546). `flushSnapshotsAfterStartedDeletions` documents the opposite intent at :296-299 — "Serialize the flush after deletion work that has reached durable storage, **without waiting on pre-deletion lease barriers that this flush may itself release**" — and `deleteStream`'s docstring at :175-181 states the same ordering ("The lane is taken before the deletion queue, so a deletion waiting on a disposing generation does not hold up the queue's other work (`deleteAll`, the snapshot flush)"). The change would make the startup snapshot flush queue behind N lease claims, which is a worse startup property than the one being fixed.

  Dedupe/ruling checks came back clean (no `SessionStores`/`deletionQueue`/`sweep` hit in the rounds1-4 index; the three round-3 SessionStores rulings are about the transcript and the tombstone, not queue membership), so this is not a duplicate — it is simply not a defect. As a graded "defect" finding it fails on its own terms: neither consequence produces incorrect state, and the failure scenario for (b) is arithmetically wrong.

  </details>

- **runAgent mints the same stream tab id twice, from two expressions that are provably equal** (slice b22)

  <details><summary>Why it was refuted</summary>

  REFUTED on three independent grounds: a dated ruling that decided exactly this shape, an inverted safety argument, and a wrong cost.

  **(1) A dated ruling already declined this, by name.** `docs/proposals/2026-08-16-services-injection-audit.md:173`, under "**Thin — measured and declined**":

  > "**`streamId` formula at 4 sites** — agreement is by shared function (`getStreamTabId`); `childRunLoop.ts:280-286` documents it load-bearing. **No change.**"

  That is the identical claim (the formula being evaluated at more than one site) measured and dispositioned as thin. Reinforced by the round-3 identity-model KEEP, `docs/proposals/2026-08-26-simplification-survey-round3.md:1743,1755`, which enumerates the mint sites — "`runAgent.ts:112`, `childStream.ts:94,258`, `bash.ts:504`, `agentCliShared.ts:214`, `detachedChildRun.ts:55`, `WorkflowScriptTool.ts:350`" — and rules "the invariants worth pinning are already written down — **`getStreamTabId` is the one minter**". The invariant the repo holds is one owner of the _format_, not one _call_ per run; repeated calls to the single minter are the sanctioned pattern, not the violation. And `docs/proposals/2026-08-03-run-classification-consolidation.md:904-907` fixes the acceptance rule as "every remaining `getStreamTabId` caller is a **birth site**" — `runAgent.ts:150` is the registration birth site for a fresh execution, so it passes the rule as written.

  **(2) The streamTab.ts doc-comment does not say what the finding says it says, and the hazard is backwards.** The comment (streamTab.ts:16-18) forbids _re-deriving the format to address an existing run_: "Existing runs are addressed by the `streamId` stamped on their execution metadata at registration, never by re-deriving this format." Line 150 is the write that _stamps_ that metadata — it is the registration itself, not a lookup of an existing run. The rule it is accused of breaking is the rule it implements. streamTab.ts:29-41 makes the same distinction explicitly for the display parser ("that rule is about _addressing_ a run").

  Worse, the proposed edit degrades the invariant that actually matters. The stream the run really writes to is minted a _third_ time, in `buildAgentLaunchContext` (src/agent/runtime/AgentLaunchContext.ts:633-634): `const streamId = input.streamTabIdOverride ?? getStreamTabId(config.agent, { executionId })`, over the post-helper `config` that `executeAgent(config, …)` receives (runAgent.ts:175). Today the durable record (`:150`, `config.agent`) and the run's own stream scope (AgentLaunchContext, `config.agent`) derive from the _same_ object, so under any hypothetical drift they still agree — and the record's `streamId` agrees with its own `identity: { agent: config.agent }` on the very next line (`:151`). Pinning `:150` to `launchStreamId` re-keys the durable record to `request.config.agent` while leaving the run scope on `config.agent`, splitting the one pair that has to agree (durable FK ↔ the stream the run writes) in order to unify a transient one (the launch handle is untracked in the `finally`, runAgent.ts:252-259). The proposal does not achieve "one derivation" — three remain — and it moves the mismatch from a harmless place to a load-bearing one.

  **(3) Cost is wrong.** `streamId: getStreamTabId(config.agent, { executionId }),` → `streamId: launchStreamId,` is one line for one line; the `getStreamTabId` import stays live for `:112`. Net 0, not -2 — and realistically +2/+3, since a reviewer would demand a comment explaining why this line reads `request.config` while its neighbour at `:151` reads `config`. A 0-to-positive-LoC edit that trades a real invariant for a cosmetic one is the churn pattern section 13 counts (22 prior "reduction" PRs, +5,046 LoC).

  Not a defect finding: the finding itself concedes the two expressions evaluate identically today, so there is no wrong behavior to protect at zero LoC.

  </details>

- **SessionState re-resolves the ephemeral entry through `getOrCreateEphemeral` in two methods whose own guard proves it already exists** (slice b25)

  <details><summary>Why it was refuted</summary>

  REFUTED on rule 7 (cost wrong / churn) reinforced by rule 5 (settled convention not beaten).

  1. COST WRONG — net is 0 LoC, not -2. Recomputed line by line. `updateStreamState` body is 4 lines (:360-363) and collapses to 3 (`const entry = ...get(stream);` / `if (!entry?.execution) return;` / `entry.execution = updater(entry.execution);`) → -1. `resetPerRunChildState` cannot collapse the same way: narrowing `current` does NOT narrow `entry`, so `entry.execution = {...}` at :381 would be an access on `EphemeralStreamState | undefined`. The guard must become three lines (`const entry = this._ephemeralState.get(stream);` / `if (!entry?.execution) return;` / `const current = entry.execution;`) replacing the current two (:369-370) → +1. The write line count is unchanged in both. Net: 0. The proposal's own sketch (`const entry = ...; if (!entry?.execution) return;` then assign) does not typecheck for the second method without a third line or a non-null assertion.

  2. THE PERF CLAIM IS NOT A BENEFIT. "Two fewer Map lookups per conversation-progress and per new-run transition" is a `Map.get` on a map holding a handful of live streams, on a per-progress-tick path. That is not a cost anyone can measure.

  3. THE "TWO IDIOMS" RATIONALE IS A MISREAD OF THE FILE'S CONVENTION — the finding's only remaining argument. I enumerated every site: `grep -n "getOrCreateEphemeral\|_ephemeralState" src/controllers/session/SessionState.ts` yields writes at :248 (metadata write), :264 (read-for-write in `updateStreamMetadata`), :282, :332 (create-or-get for execution), :362, :381 — all through `getOrCreateEphemeral`; and direct `_ephemeralState.get` only at :360, :369 (non-creating guards), :398 (`getStreamState`, pure read), plus iteration/delete at :423, :504, :564, :578, :596, :658. So the file carries ONE idiom for non-creating reads and ONE for writes, applied without a single exception. `getStreamState` (:398) is not "the direct-read form of the same thing" — it never writes, so it is not an instance of the pattern being complained about. The premise "the file contains both idioms for the same read" is false.

  4. THE CODE REASONS ABOUT THIS CHOICE EXPLICITLY (rule 3-adjacent). `getStreamMetadata` at :279-282 carries a comment devoted to exactly the create-vs-not decision at an ephemeral access site: "A removed stream is read read-only from the durable summary mirror: the tombstone gate calls this to inspect a re-claimed identity, and minting the ephemeral record here would undo the deletion the barrier exists to protect." A file that deliberates in-comment over whether a given site may mint an entry is a file where "getOrCreateEphemeral is the single write door" is a held convention, not an accident of a merge. The finding's own "Give up" clause names this position and does not defeat it.

  5. NOT A DEFECT, so the defect exemption does not apply. The create branch in both methods is genuinely unreachable — `current` being defined proves the entry exists — so removing it changes nothing observable. Zero behavior risk AND zero behavior gain AND zero LoC, against a consistent convention: this is the exact shape of the churn that section 13 records as 22 "reduction" PRs netting +5,046 LoC.

Accurate observation, insufficient value.
